cases.name: A-plan-split-payment
cases.promptMarkdown:
Write a risk-based test plan for the feature below.

Feature brief: Split payment (release 5.3)

Customers can pay for one order with two cards. They choose how much goes on the first card; the rest goes on the second. Amounts are handled in cents; when an amount cannot be split evenly, the remainder cent goes on the first card. Both charges go through the external payment gateway PayGate. If the second charge is declined, the first charge must be refunded automatically within 60 seconds.

Constraints:

- PayGate's sandbox is available only on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
- Release date: 10 working days from today.
- One tester, half time, plus the two developers who build the feature.
- The existing single-card checkout must keep working; it handles about 4,000 orders a day.

Where information is missing, state your assumption and continue; do not ask questions. Reply with the deliverable only, as Markdown, starting at its first line, with no introduction and no code fence around it. Do not create or edit files.

graders.graderMarkdown:

FAIL if there is no risk register, if any score is not the product of its likelihood and impact, or if the order of testing ignores the scores.

graders.evidence:
# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

## 1. Scope and assumptions

**In scope:** paying one order with two cards; split amount entry and validation; two PayGate charges; automatic refund of the first charge when the second is declined; regression of existing single-card checkout.

**Out of scope:** more than two cards, split across non-card methods, PayGate's own internals, load testing beyond a smoke check, accessibility of the new screens beyond keyboard operation.

**Assumptions** (stated where the brief is silent; each is an open item for the kickoff on day 1):

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| A1 | Single currency with two decimals. All arithmetic in integer cents; no floating point anywhere in the split path. |
| A2 | The remainder-cent rule applies when the UI offers an "equal split" or percentage shortcut. A customer who types a whole-cent amount never produces a remainder. |
| A3 | Each part must be at least 1 cent and strictly less than the order total, so both cards are always charged something. PayGate's own minimum charge, if any, is higher and returned as a decline. |
| A4 | Charges are sequential: card 1 first, then card 2. If card 1 is declined, card 2 is never attempted. |
| A5 | The refund of card 1 is a PayGate refund against the original charge, triggered by a background job that retries on failure. The 60-second limit is measured from receipt of the card-2 decline to PayGate accepting the refund. |
| A6 | The feature ships behind a feature flag that can be switched off without a deploy. |
| A7 | An automated regression suite for single-card checkout exists and runs in CI. If it does not, building a minimal one is the first task for the developers. |
| A8 | Developers can build a local PayGate stub, driven by recorded sandbox responses, in the first two days. |
| A9 | The same card used for both halves is allowed and treated as two independent charges. |
| A10 | Release date is Friday 6 November 2026. Sandbox days are 27 Oct, 29 Oct, 3 Nov and 5 Nov. |

## 2. Risk register

Priority drives test depth and ordering. P1 items block release if any test fails.

| ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Single-card checkout regresses (shared checkout code, gateway client, order model). Affects ~4,000 orders/day. | Medium | Critical | P1 |
| R2 | Customer is charged on card 1 and the refund never happens, happens late, or happens twice. Direct money loss and chargebacks. | Medium | Critical | P1 |
| R3 | Split arithmetic wrong: parts do not sum to total, remainder cent goes to the wrong card, rounding in a float path, negative or zero part accepted. | Medium | High | P1 |
| R4 | Gateway timeout or unknown outcome on either charge leaves the order in an inconsistent state (charged but not placed, placed but not charged, double charge on retry). | Medium | Critical | P1 |
| R5 | Client-side amount tampering: split amounts trusted from the browser, letting a customer pay less than the order total. | Low | Critical | P1 |
| R6 | Duplicate submission (double click, retry, back button) produces three or four charges. | Medium | High | P2 |
| R7 | Order records, receipts, emails, and finance reconciliation do not show two transactions and a refund correctly. | High | Medium | P2 |
| R8 | Sandbox unavailable or flaky on the four available days, leaving the gateway integration untested against the real contract. | High | High | Schedule risk, see §5 |
| R9 | Refund succeeds but the customer sees an error and places the order again. | Medium | Medium | P2 |
| R10 | Performance: two sequential gateway calls double checkout latency past timeouts. | Low | Medium | P3 |
| R11 | Feature flag off path broken, so rollback is not possible. | Low | High | P2 |

## 3. Test design by risk

### R1 Single-card regression (P1)
- Run the full existing automated checkout suite on every build (A7).
- Manual exploratory pass of single-card checkout each sandbox day against the real gateway: successful charge, decline, 3-D Secure if used, refund from admin.
- Diff review by the tester of every change touching shared checkout code and the gateway client.
- Release-day check: flag off, run single-card suite; flag on, run single-card suite again.

### R2 Automatic refund (P1)
- Card 2 declined: refund of card 1 requested; order not placed; customer told clearly which card was declined and that card 1 will be refunded.
- Measure decline-to-refund latency in the stub (deterministic) and in the sandbox (real), 10 runs each. Pass: all under 60 s, report the max.
- Refund call fails once, twice, then succeeds: exactly one refund lands.
- Refund call fails permanently: alert raised, order flagged for manual action, no silent loss.
- Refund job is restarted mid-run: no duplicate refund (idempotency key verified in logs or stub).
- Card 2 declined with every decline reason the sandbox exposes (insufficient funds, stolen, expired, do-not-honour, fraud hold).

### R3 Split arithmetic (P1)
Unit tests, written or reviewed by the tester, with a boundary table:

| Total (cents) | Input | Expected card 1 | Expected card 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1001 | equal split | 501 | 500 |
| 1000 | equal split | 500 | 500 |
| 1 | equal split | 1 | 0 → rejected (A3) |
| 2 | equal split | 1 | 1 |
| 1000 | card 1 = 1 | 1 | 999 |
| 1000 | card 1 = 999 | 999 | 1 |
| 1000 | card 1 = 1000 | rejected | |
| 1000 | card 1 = 0 | rejected | |
| 1000 | card 1 = -1 | rejected | |
| 1000 | card 1 = 10.005 | rejected or rounded per spec, never silently truncated | |
| 99999999 | equal split | 50000000 | 49999999 |

- Property test: for random totals and splits, card1 + card2 == total and both parts > 0.
- Percentage input (if A2 holds): 33% of 1000 → 330 / 670; remainder cent rule applied.
- Order total changes after split entered (coupon applied, item removed): split is recalculated or reset, never stale.

### R4 Unknown gateway outcome (P1)
Stub-driven, then confirmed in sandbox where possible:
- Timeout on card 1: no card 2 attempt; order not placed; customer sees retry; a retry does not double-charge card 1 (idempotency key).
- Timeout on card 2 where PayGate actually charged: reconciliation detects it; card 1 is not refunded if card 2 later confirms; defined behaviour documented.
- Gateway returns 5xx on refund: retried, see R2.
- Application crash between card 1 success and card 2 attempt: recovery job refunds card 1 or completes card 2, never leaves a dangling charge.

### R5 Amount tampering (P1)
- Replay the checkout request with modified amounts (card1 + card2 < total, negative card 2, card 2 omitted). Server recomputes from the order and rejects.
- Modify order total in the client after split is shown.
- Confirm raw card numbers never appear in logs, order records, or error messages for either card.

### R6 Duplicate submission (P2)
- Double-click pay button; two browser tabs; browser back then pay again; network retry of the POST. Expect exactly two charges total.

### R7 Records and reconciliation (P2)
- Order detail, customer receipt, confirmation email, admin view, and finance export each show two charges with the correct amounts and last four digits.
- After a card-2 decline, the refund appears against the correct charge and the order is not counted as revenue.
- Partial refund of a split order from admin: confirm which card is refunded and that the UI makes this explicit. If this is undefined, record it as a gap, not a test failure.

### R9 Customer messaging (P2)
- Decline message names the declined card only, does not expose decline reason beyond what single-card checkout does, and states that the first card will be refunded with an expected timeframe.

### R10 Performance smoke (P3)
- Compare p95 checkout time single-card vs split against the stub with realistic gateway latency injected. Flag if split exceeds the existing front-end timeout.

### R11 Feature flag (P2)
- Flag off: no split UI, split API endpoint rejects or is absent, single-card unaffected. Flag toggled while a split checkout is in flight: in-flight completes or fails cleanly.

## 4. Test environments and tooling

| Environment | Use | Availability |
|---|---|---|
| Local PayGate stub (A8) | All R2, R3, R4, R6 failure and timing paths. Deterministic, repeatable, every day. | Days 2 onward |
| PayGate sandbox | Contract confirmation: real decline codes, real refund latency, real idempotency behaviour, 3-D Secure. | Tue and Thu only |
| CI | Unit, property and single-card regression suites on every commit. | Continuous |
| Staging with flag | Exploratory, records and reconciliation (R7), flag tests (R11). | Days 5 onward |

The stub is the primary environment. The sandbox is used only to confirm what the stub assumes. Every sandbox session starts by recording responses to refresh the stub.

## 5. Schedule

Tester capacity is 5 person-days across 10 working days. Developer time is used for stub, unit tests and fixing.

| Day | Date | Tester (half day) | Developers |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mon 26 Oct | Kickoff: confirm assumptions A1–A10, agree flag and refund design, write boundary table (R3). | Build PayGate stub from existing recordings; start feature. |
| 2 | Tue 27 Oct | **Sandbox.** Record real responses: each decline code, refund latency, timeout, idempotent retry. Baseline single-card exploratory. | Feed recordings into stub. |
| 3 | Wed 28 Oct | Review unit and property tests for R3; review diff of shared checkout code (R1). | Feature build continues. |
| 4 | Thu 29 Oct | **Sandbox.** First end-to-end split happy path if build allows; otherwise second recording session for refund edge cases. | First testable build by end of day. |
| 5 | Fri 30 Oct | R3 and R5 against build on stub. Run single-card regression suite. | Fix. |
| 6 | Mon 2 Nov | R2 and R4 failure paths on stub; latency measurement; R6 duplicates. | Fix. |
| 7 | Tue 3 Nov | **Sandbox.** Full R2 against real gateway: 10 decline-to-refund timings, each decline code, idempotent retry. R1 exploratory. | Fix. |
| 8 | Wed 4 Nov | Retest fixes; R7 records and reconciliation; R11 flag on staging. | Fix; freeze by end of day. |
| 9 | Thu 5 Nov | **Sandbox.** Final verification on release candidate: split happy path, decline with refund, single-card regression. Sign-off report. | No feature changes; fixes only for P1. |
| 10 | Fri 6 Nov | Go/no-go, release with flag off, flag on for 5% of traffic, monitor. | Release and monitor. |

**Schedule risks and fallbacks:**
- If the first testable build slips past day 4, day 7 becomes the only full sandbox end-to-end session and day 9 the only retest. Any P1 defect found on day 9 means release with flag off and enable the following Tuesday after a sandbox retest.
- If the sandbox is down on a scheduled day, that session moves to the next sandbox day and the release decision relies on the stub plus a 1% canary with live monitoring of refund latency.
- If no automated single-card suite exists (A7 fails), developers spend day 1 and 2 on it before the feature. This is cheaper than the alternative.

## 6. Entry and exit criteria

**Entry to sandbox end-to-end (day 7):** stub-based R2, R3, R4 tests pass; no open P1 defects; single-card suite green.

**Exit for release:**
- All P1 risk tests pass on the release candidate, including at least one sandbox run of decline-to-refund with all measured latencies under 60 s.
- Single-card regression suite green with flag off and flag on.
- No open P1 defects; P2 defects either fixed or accepted in writing by the product owner with a workaround.
- Feature flag verified to disable the feature cleanly.
- Monitoring in place before release: alert on any refund older than 60 s not yet accepted, alert on orders with a successful card-1 charge and no card-2 outcome after 5 minutes, dashboard of split vs single-card decline rates.

## 7. Release safeguards

- Ship with the flag off. Enable for 5% of traffic on release day, 50% after 24 hours with no refund alerts, 100% after the next sandbox day's confirmation.
- Daily reconciliation report for the first week: every split order has exactly two settled charges, or one charge and one refund, and nothing else.
- Rollback is the flag, not a redeploy.

## 8. Defect priorities

| Priority | Definition | Release effect |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Money wrong, refund missing or duplicated, single-card broken, card data exposed | Blocks release |
| P2 | Wrong records or messaging, duplicate-submission gap, flag misbehaviour | Blocks unless accepted in writing |
| P3 | Cosmetic, performance within timeout, minor validation message | Does not block |

## 9. Deliverables

- Boundary table and property tests for R3, committed with the feature.
- Stub recordings from each sandbox session, committed so the stub stays current.
- Sandbox session log per day listing what was run, what passed, and measured refund latencies.
- Sign-off report on day 9 against the exit criteria, listing accepted P2 items and the assumptions from §1 that were confirmed or changed.

graders.evidence:
# Split Payment (release 5.3) — Risk-Based Test Plan

## 1. Scope, assumptions and risk ranking

**Scope.** Paying one order with two cards through PayGate, including amount splitting in cents, the automatic refund of the first charge when the second is declined, and protection of the existing single-card checkout. Out of scope: PayGate's own correctness, three or more cards, partial refunds of split orders after fulfilment, and changes to card data capture.

**Assumptions made where the brief is silent.**

- Release day is Friday 6 November 2026. Working days are Monday to Friday with no holidays. Sandbox days in the window are 27 Oct, 29 Oct, 3 Nov and 5 Nov.
- The tester's half time is spent as four full days on the sandbox days plus one day spread across the rest. Developers own unit and integration tests and build a PayGate stub for non-sandbox days.
- The first card is charged first. The second card is charged only if the first succeeds. The order is confirmed only when both succeed.
- The "remainder cent" rule applies to a quick split option such as 50/50 or percentage entry. Customer-typed cent amounts are used exactly.
- The refund is a full refund of the first charge via PayGate's refund call. The 60 seconds run from receipt of the decline response.
- The first-card amount must be at least 1 cent and at most the total minus 1 cent. Using the same card twice is allowed and treated as two charges.
- Split payment ships behind a feature flag that can be turned off without a redeploy.
- PayGate's sandbox provides test cards that force decline, timeout and refund failure.
- The existing single-card checkout has an automated regression suite that can run against the stub.

**Risk register, ranked by likelihood times impact.** Testing effort follows this order.

| # | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Priority |
|---|------|-----------|--------|----------|
| R1 | Second charge declined but first charge not refunded, refunded late, or refunded twice. Customer loses money with no order. | High | Critical | 1 |
| R2 | Single-card checkout breaks or slows because it shares the gateway client and checkout flow with the new code. | Medium | Critical | 2 |
| R3 | Cent arithmetic wrong: charges do not sum to the order total, remainder on the wrong card, zero or negative amounts, float rounding. | High | High | 3 |
| R4 | Double charging on retry, double submit, refresh, or gateway timeout where the charge actually went through. | Medium | Critical | 4 |
| R5 | Stub behaviour differs from the real gateway, so defects only appear on sandbox days or in production. | High | High | 5 |
| R6 | Failure mid-flow: crash after first charge, refund call fails or times out, no alert raised, order stuck in limbo. | Medium | High | 6 |
| R7 | Client-side tampering of the split amounts or card totals lets a customer pay less than the order total. | Low | High | 7 |
| R8 | Records wrong downstream: receipts, order history, refund records and finance reconciliation show one charge instead of two. | Medium | Medium | 8 |
| R9 | Input validation and UI gaps: amount over total, non-numeric, currency formatting, back button, mobile layout. | High | Low | 9 |
| R10 | Latency doubles because of two sequential gateway calls, causing timeouts or abandoned checkouts. | Low | Medium | 10 |

## 2. Test approach by risk

**Levels and who runs them.**

| Level | Runs against | Owner | When |
|-------|-------------|-------|------|
| Unit tests for split arithmetic, state machine and refund timer | In-process | Developers | Continuously |
| Integration tests for charge, decline and refund paths | PayGate stub | Developers, reviewed by tester | Mon, Wed, Fri |
| End-to-end and exploratory testing | PayGate sandbox | Tester | Tue, Thu only |
| Single-card regression suite | Stub, then sandbox | Developers run it; tester reviews results | Every build, plus each sandbox day |
| Production verification | Live PayGate, small real amounts, internal cards | Tester with a developer | Release day |

**R1 Refund on second decline.** Sandbox tests: second card declined immediately; second card times out; second card declined and then the refund call fails; refund call times out; PayGate returns an ambiguous response. For each, verify the first charge is refunded exactly once, the order is marked failed, the customer sees a clear message, and the time from decline response to refund acknowledgement is under 60 seconds. Record the timing for every run. Run ten declined splits in parallel to check the timer holds under concurrency. Verify an alert fires when the refund cannot be completed. The stub reproduces these same cases on non-sandbox days so developers can fix without waiting for Tuesday.

**R2 Single-card regression.** The full existing regression suite runs on every build against the stub. On each sandbox day the tester also runs a manual single-card smoke of approve, decline, refund and receipt. On 27 October, before any split code is tested, the tester records single-card latency and behaviour against the sandbox as a baseline. The same measurements are repeated on 5 November and compared. Any degradation blocks release regardless of split-payment status.

**R3 Cent arithmetic.** Developers unit test the split function with the tester supplying the cases. Cases include: total of 1 cent is rejected; total of 3 cents split evenly gives 2 and 1; odd totals such as 100.01 split evenly put the extra cent on the first card; first amount equal to total; first amount of zero; first amount above total; amounts entered with three decimals; values prone to float error such as 0.10 plus 0.20; large totals near the gateway maximum; percentage splits that produce fractional cents. Every case asserts that the two charges sum exactly to the order total and that neither is below 1 cent. Tester repeats a sample of these in the sandbox to confirm PayGate receives the integer cent values.

**R4 Double charging.** Sandbox and stub: double-click submit; browser refresh after the first charge succeeds; network drop during the second charge; gateway timeout when the charge actually succeeded. Verify idempotency keys are sent for each charge and the refund, and that PayGate shows exactly one charge per card per order afterwards.

**R5 Stub fidelity.** On the first sandbox day the tester captures real PayGate responses for approve, decline, timeout and refund, and developers align the stub to them that evening. Any difference found later between stub and sandbox is logged as a defect against the stub and fixed before the next stub-based run.

**R6 Mid-flow failure.** Stub only, with developer help: kill the service after the first charge and before the second; restart and confirm a recovery job refunds or completes the order and raises an alert. Verify the order never stays in an intermediate state for more than the refund window. Check logs identify order, both charge references and the refund reference.

**R7 Tampering.** Tester intercepts the checkout request and modifies the first amount, the second amount and the total. The server must recompute the split from the server-side order total and reject mismatches. Confirm no card data touches new logging.

**R8 Downstream records.** After each sandbox session, check receipts, order history, admin order view and the finance export show two charges and, for failed orders, one refund. Confirm the amounts match PayGate's dashboard to the cent.

**R9 Validation and UI.** Stub-based exploratory session: boundary amounts, non-numeric input, locale formatting with commas, back button after first charge, mobile viewport, feature flag off hides the option. Accessibility check on the new amount field.

**R10 Latency.** Measure end-to-end checkout time for split versus single card during a sandbox session. Flag if split checkout exceeds twice the single-card baseline. No load test is planned because the sandbox cannot support it; production monitoring covers this after a dark launch.

## 3. Schedule, responsibilities and exit criteria

**Schedule.** Tester works full days on the four sandbox days. Developers must deliver a build with the stub by end of Monday 26 October or the plan slips one sandbox session.

| Date | Day | Activity |
|------|-----|----------|
| Mon 26 Oct | 1 | Tester reviews spec, writes arithmetic cases, agrees test cards and stub scenarios with developers. Stub delivered. |
| Tue 27 Oct | 2 | Sandbox 1. Single-card baseline. Capture real responses. Split happy path if build is ready. |
| Wed 28 Oct | 3 | Developers align stub to captured responses, run unit and integration tests. Tester reviews results. |
| Thu 29 Oct | 4 | Sandbox 2. R1 refund paths with timing, R4 double charge, R3 sample. |
| Fri 30 Oct | 5 | Developers fix. Regression suite on stub. |
| Mon 2 Nov | 6 | Tester verifies fixes on stub, R6 crash recovery, R9 exploratory. |
| Tue 3 Nov | 7 | Sandbox 3. Full re-run of R1 and R4, R7 tampering, R8 records. Code freeze at end of day. |
| Wed 4 Nov | 8 | Release candidate built. Regression suite on stub. Developers fix only blockers. |
| Thu 5 Nov | 9 | Sandbox 4. Release candidate verification, single-card baseline comparison, go/no-go decision. |
| Fri 6 Nov | 10 | Deploy with flag off. Enable for internal users. Real small-value split with a forced decline. Monitor refund alert and single-card error rate for two hours before public enable. |

**Responsibilities.**

- Tester: test design, sandbox sessions, exploratory testing, defect triage, go/no-go recommendation.
- Developers: unit and integration tests, PayGate stub, regression suite execution, fixes, alerting and recovery job.
- Release owner: go/no-go decision. Assumed to be the product owner.

**Entry criteria for each sandbox day.** Build deployed to the test environment by the previous evening, regression suite green on the stub, known blockers listed.

**Exit criteria for release.**

- All R1 scenarios pass in the sandbox with every refund under 60 seconds, including the parallel run.
- Single-card regression suite green on the release candidate, and sandbox baseline on 5 November matches 27 October.
- No open defects of critical or high severity. Medium defects accepted in writing by the release owner.
- Alert for failed refund verified to fire.
- Tampering tests rejected server-side.
- Feature flag verified to disable split payment without redeploy.

**Risks to this plan and mitigations.**

- Only four sandbox sessions exist, and the last is the day before release. If the build is not testable by 29 October, recommend releasing with the flag off and enabling after a sandbox session the following week.
- If a critical defect is found on 5 November, there is no sandbox day left for verification. Default decision is to ship dark and verify in production with internal cards before enabling.
- The tester has roughly 40 hours. Arithmetic and validation testing is deliberately pushed to developers' unit tests so sandbox time goes to the refund and double-charge paths.
- If PayGate's sandbox is down on a scheduled day, run the planned session on the stub and move sandbox verification to the next slot. Two lost sandbox days means the release ships dark.

graders.evidence:
# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

## 1. Scope and assumptions

**In scope:** paying one order with two cards, amount selection, cent arithmetic, two PayGate charges, automatic refund of the first charge when the second is declined, and non-regression of single-card checkout.

**Out of scope:** more than two cards, split across non-card methods, PayGate's own internal behaviour, PCI re-certification.

**Assumptions (stated where the brief is silent):**

- A1. Single currency (USD), all amounts are integer cents. Zero-decimal currencies are not supported in 5.3.
- A2. A valid split requires both cards to carry at least 1 cent. First-card amount equal to the total or zero is rejected as invalid input, not treated as single-card.
- A3. The UI offers a "split evenly" default plus a custom first-card amount. The remainder-cent rule applies to the even split.
- A4. The 60-second refund clock starts when PayGate returns the decline for the second charge.
- A5. PayGate sandbox provides test cards for approve, decline, timeout, and refund-failure outcomes.
- A6. A PayGate stub exists or will be built by developers in the first two days so testing is not blocked on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
- A7. An automated regression suite exists for single-card checkout and runs in CI. If it does not, building a minimal one is the first developer task.
- A8. Feature is behind a feature flag so release can proceed with split disabled if exit criteria are not met.
- A9. Today is Saturday 24 Oct 2026. Working days are Mon 26 Oct to Fri 6 Nov. Release is Fri 6 Nov. Sandbox days are 27 Oct, 29 Oct, 3 Nov, 5 Nov.

## 2. Risk analysis

Priority drives effort. P1 risks get real-gateway coverage on every sandbox day. P2 get stub coverage plus at least one sandbox run. P3 get stub or review coverage only.

| ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Priority |
|----|------|-----------|--------|----------|
| R1 | Second charge declined, first charge not refunded, or refunded late. Customer loses money, chargebacks follow. | Medium | Critical | P1 |
| R2 | Single-card checkout regresses. 4,000 orders a day affected. | Medium | Critical | P1 |
| R3 | Double charge from retries or duplicate submit when PayGate times out on either leg. | Medium | Critical | P1 |
| R4 | Process crash or restart between first charge success and second charge attempt leaves an orphaned charge. | Low | Critical | P1 |
| R5 | Cent arithmetic wrong: sum of legs differs from order total, remainder cent on wrong card, rounding in display vs. charge. | Medium | High | P2 |
| R6 | Refund itself fails or times out and no retry or alert exists. | Medium | High | P2 |
| R7 | Client can tamper with amounts so legs do not sum to the total, or sends negative or oversized values. | Low | High | P2 |
| R8 | Order, receipt, email, and finance records show wrong state after partial success or refund. | Medium | Medium | P2 |
| R9 | Same card entered twice, or second card identical to first after tokenisation. | Medium | Low | P3 |
| R10 | Added latency from two sequential gateway calls degrades checkout under daily load. | Low | Medium | P3 |
| R11 | Accessibility and usability of the split UI. | Medium | Low | P3 |
| R12 | Plan risk: only four sandbox days, so gateway-dependent defects found late cannot be re-verified before release. | High | High | Mitigated in section 5 |

## 3. Test approach by layer

**Unit tests (developers, days 1 to 3).** Pure functions for amount splitting and validation. Exhaustive edge cases for cents are cheap here and remove most of R5 and R7 from manual effort.

**Component tests against the stub (developers and tester, every day).** The payment orchestration state machine with scripted gateway outcomes: approve/approve, approve/decline, approve/timeout, decline/anything, approve/decline/refund-fail, crash between legs. This is where R1, R3, R4, and R6 get their depth.

**End-to-end against PayGate sandbox (tester, Tue and Thu only).** Confirms the stub matches the real gateway and measures the actual refund time. Each sandbox day has a fixed agenda (section 5) so nothing is wasted.

**Regression (CI, every build).** Existing single-card suite plus a smoke run against the sandbox on each sandbox day. Covers R2.

**Exploratory (tester, 2 hours).** Split UI, back-button and refresh during payment, browser tab duplication, same-card entry. Covers R9 and R11.

**Review rather than test.** Load impact (R10) is assessed by reviewing the gateway call pattern and the latency numbers from sandbox runs, not by a load test. Monitoring and alerting for orphaned charges is reviewed as a release gate.

## 4. Test design

### 4.1 Amount splitting (R5, R7)

| Case | Total | First card input | Expected first | Expected second |
|------|-------|-----------------|----------------|-----------------|
| Even split, odd total | 1001 | even | 501 | 500 |
| Even split, even total | 1000 | even | 500 | 500 |
| Smallest splittable | 2 | even | 1 | 1 |
| Smallest total odd | 3 | even | 2 | 1 |
| Custom minimum | 1000 | 1 | 1 | 999 |
| Custom maximum | 1000 | 999 | 999 | 1 |
| Custom equals total | 1000 | 1000 | reject | |
| Custom zero | 1000 | 0 | reject | |
| Custom over total | 1000 | 1001 | reject | |
| Negative | 1000 | -1 | reject | |
| Non-integer cents | 1000 | 33.3 | reject | |
| Total of 1 cent | 1 | any | split not offered | |
| Large total | 99999999 | even | 50000000 | 49999999 |
| Tampered request, legs do not sum to total | 1000 | 400 + 500 | reject server-side | |

Every accepted case asserts first plus second equals total, and that the amounts sent to PayGate equal the amounts shown to the customer.

### 4.2 Charge orchestration and refund (R1, R3, R4, R6)

| Scenario | Gateway outcomes | Expected result |
|----------|-----------------|-----------------|
| Happy path | approve, approve | Order paid, two charge records, one receipt |
| First declined | decline | No second attempt, order unpaid, customer can retry |
| Second declined | approve, decline | First refunded within 60 s, order unpaid, customer informed |
| Second timeout | approve, timeout | No blind retry of second leg. Status query then refund if not captured |
| First timeout | timeout | No duplicate first charge on retry. Idempotency key verified |
| Refund fails | approve, decline, refund error | Retry with backoff, alert raised, charge flagged for reconciliation |
| Refund slow | approve, decline, refund takes 70 s | Measured and reported. Alert if over 60 s |
| Crash between legs | approve, process killed | On restart, first charge is refunded or second leg resumed, never left orphaned |
| Double submit | two identical requests | Exactly two charges total, not four |
| Second card same as first | approve, approve on same token | Per A2 this is allowed if PayGate accepts it. Confirm on sandbox |

Refund timing is measured on each sandbox day with at least 10 approve/decline runs. Record minimum, median, and maximum.

### 4.3 Single-card regression (R2)

- Full existing automated suite on every build.
- Manual smoke on each sandbox day: one approve, one decline, one refund on single-card.
- Verify the split UI is absent and single-card is unchanged when the feature flag is off.
- Verify order and finance records for single-card orders have no new or changed fields that downstream reports depend on.

### 4.4 Records and communication (R8)

For each orchestration scenario above, check the order status, payment records, customer email, and the finance export. Specifically check that a refunded first charge appears as a refund and not as a successful payment.

### 4.5 Exploratory (R9, R11)

Two-hour charter: break the split UI. Refresh and back during each step, duplicate tab, keyboard-only completion, screen reader labels on the amount field.

## 5. Sandbox day schedule

| Day | Agenda | Owner |
|-----|--------|-------|
| Tue 27 Oct | Confirm sandbox test cards for decline, timeout, refund failure. Record real response shapes and timings. Validate the stub against these. Single-card smoke. | Tester plus one developer |
| Thu 29 Oct | First end-to-end split on a dev build. Happy path, second declined, refund timing baseline. | Tester |
| Tue 3 Nov | Full section 4.2 run on release candidate. 10-run refund timing sample. Full single-card smoke. | Tester plus one developer |
| Thu 5 Nov | Re-test of fixes only. Final single-card smoke. Go or no-go. | Tester |

Code freeze for gateway-touching changes is end of day Wed 4 Nov. Anything changed after that cannot be verified on the real gateway and ships behind the flag turned off.

## 6. Overall schedule and effort

Tester capacity is about 5 person-days across the 10 days.

| Days | Activity | Tester effort |
|------|----------|---------------|
| Mon 26 Oct | Finalise cases, agree stub contract with developers | 0.5 |
| Tue 27 Oct | Sandbox day 1 | 0.5 |
| Wed 28 Oct | Stub-based orchestration tests on first build | 0.5 |
| Thu 29 Oct | Sandbox day 2 | 0.5 |
| Fri 30 Oct | Records and communication checks, exploratory | 0.5 |
| Mon 2 Nov | Retest defects on stub | 0.5 |
| Tue 3 Nov | Sandbox day 3 | 0.5 |
| Wed 4 Nov | Retest, regression review, code freeze | 0.5 |
| Thu 5 Nov | Sandbox day 4, sign-off report | 0.5 |
| Fri 6 Nov | Release support, monitor first split orders | 0.5 |

Developers own unit tests, the stub, component tests for the state machine, and the crash-between-legs test, since those need test hooks in the code.

## 7. Entry and exit criteria

**Entry to sandbox day 2:** unit tests for section 4.1 passing, stub in place, feature flag working.

**Exit for release with split enabled:**

- All P1 scenarios passed on the real sandbox on 3 Nov or 5 Nov.
- Refund completed within 60 seconds in every sampled run.
- No open P1 or P2 defects.
- Single-card regression suite green on the release build, and single-card smoke passed on 5 Nov.
- An alert exists for any first charge older than 60 seconds with no matching second charge or refund.
- A reconciliation query exists that finance can run to find orphaned charges.

If any criterion fails, release ships with the flag off and the split feature is enabled after the next sandbox verification.

## 8. Risks to this plan

- **Sandbox outage on a scheduled day.** Mitigation: the stub is validated on 27 Oct so stub results carry more weight. If 3 Nov is lost, 5 Nov becomes the full run and release ships flag-off if fixes are needed.
- **Build not ready by 29 Oct.** Mitigation: that day is used to extend stub validation and single-card regression instead. The 3 Nov run becomes the first full end-to-end run.
- **Half-time tester is pulled elsewhere.** Mitigation: developers run the sandbox agendas, which are written to be executable by anyone.
- **Crash-between-legs test cannot be built in time.** Mitigation: it is replaced by a code review of the recovery path plus the orphaned-charge alert as the release gate.

# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

## 1. Scope and assumptions

**In scope:** paying one order with two cards, amount entry and split calculation, two PayGate charges, automatic refund of the first charge when the second is declined, and protection of the existing single-card checkout.

**Out of scope:** more than two cards, split across non-card methods, PayGate's own internals, and changes to refunds initiated by support staff.

**Assumptions, applied where the brief is silent:**

- Today is Saturday 24 October 2026. Working days run Monday 26 October to Friday 6 November. Release is Friday 6 November.
- PayGate sandbox windows are Tuesday 27 October, Thursday 29 October, Tuesday 3 November and Thursday 5 November. That is four windows in total.
- The tester has about 4 hours per working day, roughly 40 hours in total.
- Charges are authorised and captured in one step, so "refund" means a PayGate refund call, not a void.
- Orders are in a single currency with two decimal places. Zero-decimal currencies are not supported in 5.3.
- "Split evenly" refers to a default 50/50 suggestion shown in the checkout. The customer can overwrite the first-card amount.
- The refund runs from an asynchronous job with retries, and the 60-second limit is measured from the decline response to the refund being accepted by PayGate.
- The feature ships behind a feature flag that can be switched off without a deploy.
- The existing single-card checkout has an automated regression suite that can run against a PayGate stub.
- The developers will build and maintain a local PayGate stub. Without it, testing is limited to two days a week and this plan does not fit the schedule.

## 2. Risk analysis

Likelihood and impact are rated High, Medium or Low. Priority drives how much test effort each risk gets.

| ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Priority |
|----|------|-----------|--------|----------|
| R1 | Second card declined but first charge not refunded, or refunded late. Customer pays with no order. | High | High | 1 |
| R2 | Single-card checkout regresses. About 4,000 orders a day are affected. | Medium | High | 1 |
| R3 | Second charge times out or returns an unknown state. System cannot tell whether to refund. | High | High | 1 |
| R4 | Split arithmetic wrong. Total charged differs from order total by a cent or more. | Medium | High | 2 |
| R5 | Refund succeeds but the order is still created, or refund fails and the order is cancelled silently. Order and payment records disagree. | Medium | High | 2 |
| R6 | Double submission or retry charges a card twice. | Medium | High | 2 |
| R7 | Client-side amount tampering lets a customer underpay. | Low | High | 2 |
| R8 | Amount validation gaps: zero, negative, more than total, exactly total, non-numeric, sub-cent values. | High | Medium | 3 |
| R9 | Same card entered twice, or first card declined before the second is attempted. | Medium | Medium | 3 |
| R10 | PayGate behaves differently from the stub, so defects appear only on sandbox days. | High | Medium | 3 |
| R11 | Reconciliation, receipts and reports show one charge instead of two, or wrong amounts. | Medium | Medium | 3 |
| R12 | Refund job fails under load or when PayGate is slow, missing the 60-second limit. | Medium | Medium | 3 |
| R13 | Usability: customer does not understand which card gets the remainder cent. | Medium | Low | 4 |

Priority 1 and 2 risks get scripted tests, run on both stub and sandbox, and must pass before release. Priority 3 risks get scripted tests on the stub and one sandbox pass. Priority 4 risks get exploratory coverage only if time remains.

## 3. Test approach by level

**Unit tests, owned by developers.** Split calculation is pure arithmetic and is fully covered here, covering R4 and R8. Cases:

- Total 1 cent: first card 1, second card 0 or rejected, depending on design. Flag the decision.
- Total 999 cents, even split: first card 500, second card 499.
- Total 1000 cents, even split: 500 and 500.
- Customer-chosen first amount of 1 cent and of total minus 1 cent.
- First amount equal to total: treated as single-card or rejected. Flag the decision.
- First amount of zero, negative, greater than total, with fractional cents, and non-numeric input.
- Largest supported order value to check for integer overflow.
- Sum of both charges always equals the order total for a randomised set of totals and splits.

**Integration tests against the PayGate stub, owned by developers with tester review.** The stub replays fixtures captured from the sandbox on the first sandbox day. Cases cover R1, R3, R5, R6, R12:

- Both charges approved.
- First approved, second declined, refund approved within 60 seconds.
- First approved, second declined, refund declined by PayGate. Expected: alert raised, order held, no silent failure.
- First approved, second times out. Expected: status query or idempotent retry, then either completion or refund. No double charge.
- First declined. Expected: second card never attempted, no refund needed.
- Refund call times out, then succeeds on retry. Refund must still land within 60 seconds.
- Duplicate submission with the same idempotency key. Expected: one set of charges.
- Stub returns slow responses of 30 seconds or more to check the refund budget.

**End-to-end tests on the PayGate sandbox, owned by the tester.** Run on each of the four sandbox days. Cases cover R1, R3, R9, R10, R11:

- Happy path with two real sandbox cards, then check order record, receipt and both transactions in PayGate.
- Second card decline using PayGate's decline test card. Measure time from decline to refund acceptance with timestamps from logs and the PayGate dashboard.
- Second card with insufficient-funds, expired and fraud-flagged test cards, if PayGate provides them.
- Same card number on both slots.
- Receipt and order history show two charges and a refund where one happened.

**Regression, owned by the tester with developer help on automation.** Covers R2:

- Full automated single-card suite against the stub on every build.
- Manual single-card sandbox smoke on each sandbox day: approve, decline, refund by support.
- Confirm the feature flag off path is byte-for-byte the old checkout flow.

**Security and tampering, owned by the tester.** Covers R7:

- Modify the first-card amount in the request after the page renders. Server must recompute from the order total and reject mismatches.
- Replay a completed request with a different order ID.

**Exploratory sessions.** Two sessions of one hour each, covering R8, R9 and R13: browser back button mid-payment, refreshing between charges, switching cards after entering an amount, and checkout on a small screen.

## 4. Schedule

| Day | Date | Sandbox | Tester activity | Developer activity |
|-----|------|---------|-----------------|--------------------|
| 1 | Mon 26 Oct | No | Confirm assumptions, review design, agree on undefined cases from the unit list | Unit tests for split arithmetic, start stub scaffold |
| 2 | Tue 27 Oct | Yes | Explore PayGate: decline cards, refund API, timeout behaviour. Capture fixtures for the stub | Pair on fixture capture, implement charge flow |
| 3 | Wed 28 Oct | No | Review stub fixtures, write integration cases | Finish stub, implement refund job |
| 4 | Thu 29 Oct | Yes | First end-to-end run: happy path and second-card decline with refund timing | Fix findings |
| 5 | Fri 30 Oct | No | Single-card regression run, tampering tests | Fix findings, add idempotency |
| 6 | Mon 2 Nov | No | Failure modes on stub: timeouts, refund decline, slow PayGate | Fix findings |
| 7 | Tue 3 Nov | Yes | Full scripted sandbox pass, retest fixed defects, refund timing | Fix findings |
| 8 | Wed 4 Nov | No | Regression rerun, exploratory sessions, code freeze at end of day | Final fixes only |
| 9 | Thu 5 Nov | Yes | Release candidate run on sandbox, go/no-go report | Standby |
| 10 | Fri 6 Nov | No | Release with flag off. Enable for internal users. Production smoke with two low-value real cards and one forced decline | Monitor refund job and error rates |

If a sandbox day is lost, the next sandbox day absorbs its cases and the exploratory sessions are dropped.

## 5. Entry and exit criteria

**Entry to sandbox testing:** stub exists, unit tests pass, build deployed to a test environment with PayGate sandbox credentials and log access.

**Exit for release:**

- All priority 1 and 2 cases pass on the sandbox on Thursday 5 November.
- No open defect in R1, R2, R3 or R4.
- Refund observed within 60 seconds in every sandbox decline test, with the slowest time recorded.
- Single-card regression suite green on the release candidate build.
- Refund job has an alert for any refund not accepted within 60 seconds, verified by triggering it on the stub.
- Feature flag off path confirmed identical to the current checkout.

## 6. Residual risks and mitigations

- **Only four sandbox windows.** Anything PayGate does that the stub does not model will be found late. Mitigation: day 2 is spent entirely on capturing real behaviour, and the stub is built from those fixtures rather than from documentation.
- **Half-time tester.** Scripted coverage is prioritised over exploratory work. Developers own all unit and most integration tests.
- **No load test.** The 4,000 orders a day are protected by regression and the feature flag, not by load testing. Mitigation: enable the feature gradually in production and watch single-card error rates and latency for the first day.
- **Production behaviour of refunds.** Sandbox refund timing may not match production. Mitigation: the production smoke on release day includes one forced decline and a timed refund before the flag is opened to customers.
- **Undefined cases.** The brief does not define a 1-cent order, a first amount equal to the total, or the same card used twice. These are raised on day 1 and the chosen behaviour is tested, whichever it is.

# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

## 1. Scope and assumptions

**In scope:** two-card split at checkout, cent arithmetic and remainder rule, both PayGate charges, automatic refund of the first charge when the second is declined, and non-regression of single-card checkout.

**Out of scope:** more than two cards, split across non-card methods, partial refunds after fulfilment, PayGate's own internals.

**Assumptions, stated because the brief does not say:**

- Release date is Friday 6 November 2026. Sandbox days in the window are 27 Oct, 29 Oct, 3 Nov and 5 Nov.
- "Cannot be split evenly" refers to an "split evenly" option. Custom amounts are entered by the customer in whole cents, so no rounding occurs there.
- The first-card amount must be at least 1 cent and at most total minus 1 cent. Anything else is a validation error, not a single-card order.
- Card data is tokenised by PayGate. The application never stores PANs, so PCI scope is unchanged.
- "Declined" includes hard declines, soft declines, gateway timeouts and 5xx errors. All of them must trigger the refund.
- The refund is an asynchronous job that retries on failure. The 60-second clock starts at the second charge's failure response.
- The developers will build a PayGate stub that replays recorded sandbox responses, so testing can continue on non-sandbox days.
- An automated regression suite exists for single-card checkout. If it does not, the Friday 30 Oct slot becomes a manual regression pass and exploratory time is cut.
- The feature ships behind a feature flag with a kill switch.

## 2. Risk register

Ranked by likelihood times impact. Priority drives the order of testing and what must pass before release.

| # | Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Priority |
|---|------|--------|-----------|----------|
| R1 | Second card declined but first charge not refunded, or refunded late | Customer charged with no order; chargebacks; support load | Medium | P1 |
| R2 | Single-card checkout regresses | 4,000 orders/day at risk; direct revenue loss | Medium | P1 |
| R3 | Cent arithmetic wrong: totals do not add up, remainder on wrong card, negative or zero amounts | Over- or under-charging; reconciliation failures | Medium | P1 |
| R4 | Double charge on retry, timeout or ambiguous gateway response | Customer charged twice; refund logic may not cover it | Medium | P1 |
| R5 | Order left in inconsistent state when the customer abandons, refreshes or double-submits between the two charges | Orders paid but not placed, or placed but not fully paid | Medium | P2 |
| R6 | Input validation gaps on first-card amount | Bad requests reach PayGate; confusing errors | High | P2 |
| R7 | Refund itself fails at PayGate and is not retried or alerted | Same outcome as R1, but silent | Low | P2 |
| R8 | Reconciliation and reporting do not show two charges and a refund per order | Finance cannot reconcile; hard to detect R1 in production | Medium | P3 |
| R9 | Sandbox unavailable or unstable on a scheduled day | Schedule slips; untested paths at release | Medium | Schedule |
| R10 | Half-time tester is the single point of failure | Coverage gaps | Medium | Schedule |

## 3. Test approach by risk

Three layers, each usable on different days:

- **Unit tests (developers, any day):** cent arithmetic, remainder rule, validation, state machine for the two-charge flow. Tester reviews cases, does not write them.
- **Stub-based integration (tester, non-sandbox days):** full checkout against the PayGate stub. Covers timeouts, 5xx, malformed responses and refund failures that the sandbox cannot produce on demand.
- **Sandbox end-to-end (tester plus one developer, Tue/Thu):** real gateway behaviour, real refund timing, real decline codes.

**R1 Refund on decline (P1).** On the sandbox: second card hard decline, soft decline, insufficient funds. Measure time from decline response to refund confirmed at PayGate. Run each case at least three times on two separate sandbox days. On the stub: second charge timeout, 5xx, and malformed response all trigger the refund. Verify the order ends in a single terminal "payment failed, refunded" state and the customer sees one clear message.

**R2 Single-card regression (P1).** Run the existing regression suite against the stub on 30 Oct and against the sandbox on 3 Nov. Add an explicit check that an order with the split option untouched sends exactly one charge. Check feature flag off produces the pre-5.3 checkout byte-for-byte in the request to PayGate.

**R3 Cent arithmetic (P1).** Unit tests for even split on odd totals, remainder cent on card one, totals of 1 cent, 2 cents, 3 cents, and large values near integer limits. Property test: for any total and any first-card amount in range, card one plus card two equals total. End-to-end check that the two sandbox charges sum to the order total for at least one odd and one even total.

**R4 Idempotency (P1).** Stub returns timeout on charge one, then the client retries. Verify exactly one charge is created and the idempotency key is reused. Same for charge two and for the refund. Verify double-submit of the checkout form creates one order and at most two charges.

**R5 Abandonment and state (P2).** Close the browser after charge one succeeds. Verify the order does not remain half-paid indefinitely: either charge two proceeds server-side or charge one is refunded after a defined timeout. Refresh mid-flow and verify no duplicate charges.

**R6 Validation (P2).** First-card amount of 0, equal to total, greater than total, negative, non-numeric, more than two decimals, empty. Both cards the same card number. Expired or invalid second card entered before charge one is attempted, to confirm the first charge is not made needlessly.

**R7 Refund failure (P2).** Stub returns failure on the refund call. Verify retry with backoff, an alert raised, and the order flagged for manual action. Nothing should silently swallow the failure.

**R8 Reconciliation (P3).** Admin and finance views show two transactions and, where applicable, one refund per order. Export matches PayGate's sandbox transaction list.

**Exploratory (if time allows):** mixed card brands, 3DS challenge on the second card, currency display with the remainder cent, accessibility of the split control.

## 4. Schedule

Tester capacity is roughly four hours per day, about 40 hours in total. Sandbox days are protected for gateway work only.

| Day | Date | Activity |
|-----|------|----------|
| Mon | 26 Oct | Review plan with developers. Agree stub scope and sandbox test card set. Confirm regression suite runs. |
| Tue | 27 Oct | **Sandbox 1.** Record real responses for success, each decline type, timeout and refund. Smoke the happy path if a build exists. Developers build the stub from the recordings. |
| Wed | 28 Oct | Review unit tests for R3 and R6. Stub-based validation and arithmetic checks. |
| Thu | 29 Oct | **Sandbox 2.** Happy path, R1 decline and refund cases, first timing measurements. |
| Fri | 30 Oct | Single-card regression on the stub (R2). Retest fixes. |
| Mon | 2 Nov | Stub-based R4, R5, R7. Retest fixes. |
| Tue | 3 Nov | **Sandbox 3.** Full P1 and P2 pass. Single-card regression on sandbox. Repeat refund timing. This is the last day a found defect can be fixed and re-verified on the real gateway. |
| Wed | 4 Nov | Fix and retest on stub. R8 reconciliation. Exploratory. |
| Thu | 5 Nov | **Sandbox 4.** Confirmation run of all P1 cases only. Go/no-go decision by end of day. |
| Fri | 6 Nov | Release behind flag. Monitor. |

**If a sandbox day is lost (R9):** fall back to the stub for that day and move its sandbox cases to the next sandbox day. If 3 Nov is lost, recommend releasing with the flag off and enabling after a sandbox run the following week.

**If the tester is unavailable (R10):** developers own the sandbox sessions. The case list in section 3 is written so a developer can execute it without further briefing.

## 5. Entry and exit criteria

**Entry to sandbox 2:** stub exists, feature flag works, unit tests for arithmetic and validation pass.

**Exit for release:**

- All P1 cases pass on the real sandbox on 3 Nov or 5 Nov.
- Refund completed within 60 seconds in every measured run, with the slowest observed time recorded in the release notes.
- Single-card regression passes on both stub and sandbox.
- No open severity 1 or 2 defects. Severity 3 defects are listed in the release notes with an owner.
- A production alert exists for "charge one succeeded, charge two failed, refund not confirmed within 60 seconds".
- Kill switch verified to return checkout to single-card mode without a deploy.

## 6. Release recommendation

Enable the flag for a small share of traffic on 6 Nov and watch the refund alert and the split-order count for two working days before full rollout. Production load and real issuer behaviour cannot be exercised in the sandbox, so the first days of live traffic are part of the test.

# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

## 1. Assumptions

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| A1 | Today is Sat 24 Oct 2026. Working days are Mon–Fri, so the release is Fri 6 Nov 2026. Sandbox days in the window: Tue 27 Oct, Thu 29 Oct, Tue 3 Nov, Thu 5 Nov. |
| A2 | Tester capacity is about 5 person-days total. Developers own unit tests, a local PayGate stub, and test hooks. |
| A3 | PayGate's sandbox has test card numbers that trigger approve, decline, and timeout, plus a refund endpoint. No vendor simulator exists outside sandbox days, so the developers build a stub that mimics recorded sandbox responses. |
| A4 | The UI proposes a 50/50 default split that the customer can edit. The remainder-cent rule applies to that default. Each card must carry at least 1 cent, and the two amounts must sum exactly to the order total. |
| A5 | "Refunded within 60 seconds" means a full refund of the first charge is accepted by PayGate within 60 seconds of receiving the second card's decline. |
| A6 | The feature ships behind a feature flag. If not, this plan treats that as a P1 defect. |
| A7 | Single currency with two decimal places. No 3-D Secure, no more than two cards, no saved-card flows. |
| A8 | An automated regression suite exists for single-card checkout and runs in CI. |
| A9 | Card 1 is charged before card 2. If card 1 is declined, card 2 is never attempted. |

## 2. Risk register

Priority drives effort: P1 risks get sandbox time and sign-off gates, P2 get stub-based coverage, P3 get exploratory coverage only if time remains.

| ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Pri | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Card 2 declined but card 1 not refunded, or refunded after 60s. Customer charged with no order. | Med | Critical | P1 | Sandbox, timed, 10 repetitions |
| R2 | Single-card checkout regresses (4,000 orders/day). | Med | Critical | P1 | Automated suite each build, manual smoke, flag on and off |
| R3 | Split arithmetic wrong: amounts do not sum to total, remainder cent on wrong card, float rounding. | Med | High | P1 | Unit tests, boundary table |
| R4 | Unknown state after timeout on charge 2 or on the refund call. Orphan charge with no order. | Med | High | P1 | Stub (timeouts), sandbox (one real timeout card if available) |
| R5 | Double charge or double refund from retries, double-submit, or page refresh. | Med | High | P1 | Stub with idempotency assertions, manual double-click |
| R6 | Client-side amount tampering so the two charges do not equal the order total. | Low | High | P1 | API tests with altered payloads |
| R7 | Refund call fails. No retry, no alert, order silently confirmed. | Med | High | P2 | Stub (refund 500 / timeout), alert verification |
| R8 | Invalid input accepted: zero, negative, greater than total, three decimals, non-numeric. | High | Med | P2 | Unit and UI tests |
| R9 | Order records, receipts, and reconciliation show one transaction instead of two, or omit the refund. | Med | Med | P2 | Manual check after each sandbox flow |
| R10 | Checkout latency doubles because two sequential gateway calls are made. | Med | Med | P2 | Timing measured during sandbox runs |
| R11 | Same card entered in both slots. | Low | Low | P3 | One exploratory case; assume rejected |
| R12 | Schedule: sandbox only four days, half-time tester, feature may not be ready for the first sessions. | High | High | — | Mitigation in section 5 |

## 3. Test levels and ownership

| Level | Owner | Runs on | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | Developers | Every commit | Split calculation, validation, charge/refund state machine |
| Integration against PayGate stub | Developers write, tester reviews and extends | Any day | Decline, timeout, refund failure, retry, idempotency, flag on/off |
| Sandbox end-to-end | Tester, developer on call | Tue/Thu only | Scripted P1 flows with real gateway responses and timing |
| Regression | Tester | Each build and at release candidate | Automated single-card suite plus manual smoke |
| Release safeguards | Developers | Release day | Flag, dashboards, alerting, rollback |

## 4. Test cases

### 4.1 Split calculation (R3, R8) — unit, run daily

| Total | Input | Expected card 1 / card 2 |
|---|---|---|
| 100.00 | default split | 5000 / 5000 |
| 100.01 | default split | 5001 / 5000 |
| 0.03 | default split | 2 / 1 |
| 0.01 | any | Split not offered (A4) |
| 100.00 | first = 0.01 | 1 / 9999 |
| 100.00 | first = 99.99 | 9999 / 1 |
| 100.00 | first = 100.00 | Rejected |
| 100.00 | first = 0, negative, 100.01, 10.005, "abc" | Rejected with message |
| 999,999.99 | first = 500,000.00 | No overflow, no float drift |
| 0.10 + 0.20 style totals | default | Integer cents only, never 0.30000000004 |

### 4.2 Charge and refund flow (R1, R4, R5, R7, R9) — stub daily, sandbox on Tue/Thu

| ID | Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Both cards approved | Order confirmed, two transactions stored, receipt lists both amounts |
| F2 | Card 1 declined | Card 2 never called, no charge, clear message, order not created |
| F3 | Card 2 declined | Card 1 refunded, refund accepted by PayGate within 60s, order not created, customer told both outcomes |
| F4 | Card 2 times out | Treated as failed, card 1 refunded, no orphan charge, alert raised |
| F5 | Refund call fails or times out | Retried, order stays unconfirmed, alert raised, item lands in manual review queue |
| F6 | Same request submitted twice (double-click, retry) | Exactly one charge per card, idempotency key reused |
| F7 | Browser refresh or back between charge 1 and charge 2 | No second charge 1, state recovers or cleanly aborts with refund |
| F8 | Payload altered so card 1 + card 2 ≠ total | Rejected server-side before any charge |
| F9 | Flag off | Split option hidden, single-card flow unchanged |
| F10 | Refund timing under load | F3 repeated 10 times in sandbox; every refund ≤ 60s, p50 recorded |

### 4.3 Single-card regression (R2)

- Full automated suite on every build and on the release candidate, flag on and flag off.
- Manual smoke on each sandbox day: approved, declined, refund of a single-card order.
- Compare checkout latency before and after the change on the single-card path.

## 5. Schedule

| Day | Date | Sandbox | Tester (0.5d) | Developers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mon 26 Oct | | Confirm assumptions, finalise cases, request sandbox test cards | Build PayGate stub with decline, timeout, refund-fail switches |
| 2 | Tue 27 Oct | Yes | Record real sandbox responses and refund timing baseline, even without the feature | Make stub match recorded responses |
| 3 | Wed 28 Oct | | Review unit tests for 4.1 | Feature build, unit tests |
| 4 | Thu 29 Oct | Yes | First end-to-end on early build: F1, F2, F3 timed | On call for fixes |
| 5 | Fri 30 Oct | | Stub runs: F4–F8; regression suite | Fix defects |
| 6 | Mon 2 Nov | | Verify fixes on stub, exploratory R11, R9 checks | Observability, alerting, retry logic |
| 7 | Tue 3 Nov | Yes | Full P1 sandbox run including F10 (10 timed refunds) | On call |
| 8 | Wed 4 Nov | | Full regression, flag on/off, fix verification. Code freeze at end of day | Final fixes only |
| 9 | Thu 5 Nov | Yes | Release-candidate verification on sandbox. Go/no-go decision | On call |
| 10 | Fri 6 Nov | | Release, monitor dashboards | Staged rollout, rollback ready |

Schedule risk (R12): if the feature is not testable by Thu 29 Oct, Tue 3 Nov becomes the first real run and only one sandbox day remains for fixes. In that case, recommend releasing with the flag off and enabling it after a further sandbox verification the following Tuesday.

## 6. Entry and exit criteria

Entry to sandbox sessions: build deployed to test environment, stub-based P1 cases passing, flag toggles verified.

Exit for release:

- All P1 cases pass on sandbox on Thu 5 Nov.
- F10: 10 of 10 refunds accepted within 60s.
- No open severity 1 or 2 defects.
- Single-card regression suite green with flag on and flag off.
- Alert for refund failure and for orphan charge fires in test.
- Rollback by flag verified.

## 7. Release safeguards

- Feature flag on for a small share of traffic on day 1, widened over the following week.
- Dashboard: split orders, card 2 declines, refund latency, refund failures, orphan charges (charge without confirmed order).
- Daily reconciliation report comparing PayGate transactions against orders for the first week.
- Rollback is flag off. No data migration is involved, so rollback needs no further step.

## 8. Out of scope

Load testing against PayGate, 3-D Secure, multi-currency, more than two cards, mobile-specific UI beyond the shared API, PCI assessment (card data is tokenised by PayGate).

## 9. Residual risks after this plan

- Timeout and refund-failure behaviour is validated mainly on the stub. Real gateway behaviour under those conditions is seen at most once.
- Sandbox refund timing may not match production timing. The 60s target should be monitored in production, not assumed.
- Half-time tester leaves no slack. Any slip of more than one day consumes the final sandbox session.

# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

## 1. Scope and assumptions

**In scope:** two-card split checkout, cent allocation, PayGate charge sequencing, automatic refund on second-card decline, and non-regression of single-card checkout.

**Assumptions (made where the brief is silent):**

- A1. Today is Sat 24 Oct 2026; release is Fri 6 Nov 2026. Sandbox windows: Tue 27 Oct, Thu 29 Oct, Tue 3 Nov, Thu 5 Nov.
- A2. The customer may either type an amount for card 1 or pick "split evenly". The odd-cent rule applies to "split evenly"; a typed amount is used as-is.
- A3. Card 1 is charged first; card 2 is charged only if card 1 succeeds. If card 1 is declined, card 2 is never attempted.
- A4. Single currency per order; no multi-currency splits.
- A5. Card data is tokenised by PayGate; our system never stores PANs.
- A6. PayGate sandbox provides deterministic test cards for approve, decline, and timeout.
- A7. Refund-on-decline is implemented as a background job with retries and alerting when it cannot complete.
- A8. Developers will build a local PayGate stub so tests can run on non-sandbox days.
- A9. "Half time" tester = roughly 5 person-days across the 10-day window.

## 2. Risk assessment

Priority = likelihood × impact. Testing effort follows priority order.

| ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Priority |
|----|------|-----------|--------|----------|
| R1 | Card 2 declined, card 1 refund fails, is late (>60 s), or is duplicated. Customer loses money. | Med | Critical | **P1** |
| R2 | Single-card checkout regresses (4,000 orders/day). | Med | Critical | **P1** |
| R3 | Cent allocation wrong: amounts do not sum to the total, odd cent on wrong card, negative or zero amounts accepted. | High | High | **P1** |
| R4 | Partial-failure states: timeout or gateway outage between charge 1 and charge 2 leaves the order half paid with no refund. | Med | Critical | **P1** |
| R5 | Retry or double-submit produces duplicate charges (idempotency). | Med | High | **P2** |
| R6 | Input validation gaps: amount > total, amount = total, same card twice, non-numeric, currency rounding on display vs. cents. | High | Med | **P2** |
| R7 | Order, receipt, and reconciliation records show one charge instead of two; later customer-service refunds act on the wrong card. | Med | Med | **P2** |
| R8 | Stub diverges from real PayGate behaviour, so green tests on non-sandbox days hide real defects. | Med | High | **P2** |
| R9 | Performance: two sequential gateway calls push checkout latency past the current timeout. | Low | Med | **P3** |
| R10 | Security: card 2 token or amount exposed in logs, URLs, or client state. | Low | High | **P3** |

## 3. Test approach by risk

**R1 — Refund on second decline (P1)**
- Unit: decline on card 2 triggers exactly one refund of card 1 for the exact charged amount.
- Integration (sandbox): decline test card on card 2; measure wall-clock time from decline response to refund confirmation. Pass threshold: ≤ 60 s on 10 consecutive runs.
- Failure injection (stub): refund call returns 5xx, times out, or succeeds after retry. Verify retries, no duplicate refund, and alert raised when retries are exhausted.
- Verify order status reads "payment failed, refund issued" and customer notification is sent.

**R2 — Single-card regression (P1)**
- Run the existing single-card automated suite on every build.
- Manual smoke of single-card checkout on each sandbox day with real gateway.
- Confirm the split feature is behind a flag; test single-card with the flag both on and off.
- Compare single-card checkout latency before and after the change.

**R3 — Cent allocation (P1)**
- Unit, table-driven, run by developers: totals of 1, 2, 3, 99, 100, 101, 999, 12345 cents and a large value near the integer limit. Assert card1 + card2 = total and odd cent lands on card 1.
- Property-based test: for any total ≥ 2 cents and any valid card 1 amount, sum equals total and both amounts are ≥ 1 cent.
- UI: confirm the displayed amounts match the cents sent to PayGate (no float rounding on display).

**R4 — Partial failure between charges (P1)**
- Stub: card 1 succeeds, then card 2 call times out with unknown outcome. Verify the system queries PayGate for the final state before deciding to refund or complete.
- Stub: application crash after card 1 success. Verify recovery job detects the orphaned charge and refunds it.
- Sandbox: PayGate timeout test card on card 2.

**R5 — Idempotency (P2)**
- Submit the same checkout twice in quick succession (double-click, browser retry). Verify exactly two charges in total, not four.
- Verify an idempotency key is sent per charge and per refund.

**R6 — Validation (P2)**
- Boundary cases: card 1 amount = 0, = 1 cent, = total − 1, = total, > total, negative, decimals, blank.
- Same card entered for both slots (assume rejected; confirm with developers).
- Expected: clear error, no gateway call made.

**R7 — Records and downstream (P2)**
- Order detail, receipt email, admin panel, and reconciliation export show two charges with correct amounts and gateway references.
- Customer-service partial refund on a split order refunds the correct card.

**R8 — Stub fidelity (P2)**
- On the first sandbox day, record real PayGate request and response payloads for approve, decline, timeout, and refund. Update the stub to match before relying on it.

**R9, R10 (P3)**
- Time ten split checkouts in sandbox; flag if p95 exceeds the existing checkout timeout.
- Grep application logs and browser network traffic from one full split flow for tokens, PANs, or amounts in URLs.

## 4. Environments and sandbox strategy

The sandbox is available 4 of the 10 working days, so it is the scarce resource.

- **Non-sandbox days:** unit, property, UI, and failure-injection tests against the PayGate stub.
- **Sandbox days:** reserved for R1 timing, R4 real timeouts, R2 real-gateway smoke, R8 payload capture, and R9 latency. Prepare every sandbox-day script the day before so no window is wasted.
- **Contingency:** if PayGate sandbox is down on a scheduled day, the next window is 2 days away. Any P1 sandbox test not passed by Thu 5 Nov blocks release.

## 5. Schedule

| Day | Date | Activity | Who |
|-----|------|----------|-----|
| 1 | Mon 26 Oct | Review design, confirm assumptions A2/A3/A7 with developers, write sandbox-day scripts, build stub | Tester, Dev |
| 2 | **Tue 27 Oct (sandbox)** | Capture real payloads (R8), first R1 timing run on whatever is built, single-card smoke | Tester |
| 3 | Wed 28 Oct | Cent allocation and validation tests (R3, R6) against stub; update stub from captured payloads | Tester, Dev |
| 4 | **Thu 29 Oct (sandbox)** | R1 decline-and-refund timing, R4 timeout cards, single-card smoke | Tester |
| 5 | Fri 30 Oct | Failure injection on stub (R1 refund failures, R4 crash recovery), idempotency (R5) | Tester, Dev |
| 6 | Mon 2 Nov | Records and downstream (R7), security log review (R10), fix verification | Tester |
| 7 | **Tue 3 Nov (sandbox)** | Full regression: 10× R1 timing runs, R2 smoke, R9 latency | Tester, Dev |
| 8 | Wed 4 Nov | Fix verification on stub, exit criteria review | Tester |
| 9 | **Thu 5 Nov (sandbox)** | Final sandbox confirmation of any fixes, go/no-go | Tester, Dev |
| 10 | Fri 6 Nov | Release with flag off, enable for internal users, monitor | Dev |

Developers own unit and property tests (R3, R5) and the stub. The tester owns sandbox sessions, failure injection, and exit review.

## 6. Entry and exit criteria

**Entry:** feature deployable to a test environment by Tue 27 Oct, stub available by Wed 28 Oct, feature flag in place.

**Exit (release blockers):**
- All P1 tests pass, including 10 consecutive R1 refund runs ≤ 60 s against real sandbox.
- Single-card automated suite green on the release candidate, with flag on and off.
- No open P1 or P2 defects. P3 defects may ship with a logged ticket.
- Alerting for failed refunds verified to fire.

## 7. Out of scope

Multi-currency, more than two cards, saved-card wallets, chargeback flows, PayGate load testing.

## 8. Risks to this plan

- Only 4 sandbox windows: a sandbox outage or a late build consumes 25% of real-gateway test time. Mitigation: dark launch behind a flag on Fri 6 Nov, enable for internal users first, monitor refund-time metric in production before customer rollout.
- Half-time tester: P3 items are the first to drop if P1 fixes arrive late.
- Assumption A7 (background refund job) changes the R1 and R4 tests if wrong. Confirm on day 1.
