## 6. Test Approach

**Pyramid preset.** Backend / API: 70% unit, 20% integration, 10% E2E. The business logic (split arithmetic, charge sequencing, refund decision, state machine) lives in the backend; the UI is a form with two fields. Approximate case counts: 35–45 unit, 10–14 integration, 6–8 E2E (the gate plus one or two more).

**Test levels, who tests, independence.**

| Level | What | Who tests | Independence | Why this degree |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Component | Split arithmetic, validation, refund decision, state machine | The developer who wrote it, reviewed by the other developer | None to some | Fast feedback; the tester reviews the test list against R03 and R05 so the author's blind spots are covered |
| Component integration | Payment service against the PayGate stub: sequencing, idempotency, refund retry, timing | The other developer (not the author) | Some | Pairing the developers keeps stub and service honest with each other; the tester reviews |
| System | Full checkout on staging with the stub, then with the sandbox | The tester | High (outside the authors) | CRITICAL product risks about money need a tester who does not share the authors' assumptions |
| Acceptance | Each outcome path shown to the PO on a sandbox day | PO with the tester | High | Business confirmation of A1 to A4 in the running system |
| Regression (single-card) | Existing automated suite, smoke on staging and production | CI, read by the tester | Some | Automated suite is the existing baseline; the tester owns the pass/fail reading |

**Test types.** Functional (all levels); non-functional: refund timing (R01), single-card latency (R11), one accessibility pass (R19); structural: branch coverage on the split and refund modules, target 100% branches on those two modules only; change-related: confirmation of each fix and regression of single-card checkout on every build.

**Techniques per risk.**

- R03 cent arithmetic: equivalence partitioning and boundary-value analysis on the total and the card 1 amount (1, 2, odd, even, 999, 1000, 10^7 cents; card 1 at 1 and total − 1); property test that the two charges sum to the total and card 1 carries the odd cent.
- R07 validation: BVA on the input field at API level: 0, 1, total − 1, total, total + 1, negative, non-numeric, 3 decimals, empty.
- R01, R02, R05 outcome paths: decision table with conditions charge 1 result × charge 2 result × refund result; state-transition testing of the payment state machine with every valid and invalid transition.
- R04 idempotency: replay of the same request after a timeout, with the stub and the sandbox.
- R08, R18, R19: exploratory sessions, charter-based, time-boxed.
- Regression: the existing single-card suite, scoped by the developers' impact analysis of the diff.

**Quadrants check.** Q1: unit and integration tests in CI. Q2: the decision-table and state-transition cases, the API validation cases, the acceptance run with the PO. Q3: three exploratory sessions (outcome messaging, locale, accessibility). Q4: smoke suite, refund timing measurement, single-card latency comparison. No quadrant is empty.

**Deliverables.** This plan; test cases TC-SPLIT-001 onward; stub recordings; four progress reports; defect reports DR-SPLIT-NNN; completion report with go/no-go record; retrospective actions.

**Entry criteria for system-level execution (checked 2026-10-31, before the third sandbox window).**

- [ ] Feature code-complete behind the flag, merged, build green with the unit and integration suites passing.
- [ ] Stub (A6) in place and built from the 2026-10-28 sandbox recordings.
- [ ] Staging deployed with the build identified by version; flag toggle confirmed working.
- [ ] Fixture set below available; sandbox card numbers and decline codes confirmed.
- [ ] PO has answered A1 to A4 (or the assumptions stand by default, recorded in the plan).
- [ ] Form elements carry `data-testid` attributes.

**Exit criteria for the release.**

- [ ] All six release gate cases pass on the sandbox, on the release candidate build, on 2026-11-06 at the latest.
- [ ] 100% of P0 cases executed and passing; 100% of P1 executed and passing or each failure has a recorded PO exception.
- [ ] Zero open Critical defects; zero open High defects without a PO exception.
- [ ] Single-card regression suite green on the release candidate; single-card p95 latency within 10% of baseline.
- [ ] Flag-off state verified on staging; rollback step written and dry-run once.
- [ ] Completion report signed off by the tester and the PO.
- [ ] Running out of time ends testing only if the PO records acceptance of the untested risk.

**Release gate.**

| ID | What it proves | Level | Risk | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G1 (TC-SPLIT-001) | Card 2 hard decline: charge 1 refunded, refund acknowledged within 60 s, order not paid, customer told | E2E sandbox | R01 | N/A — not yet run |
| G2 (TC-SPLIT-002) | Card 2 declined and refund call times out: retried, refund lands within 60 s or order enters "refund pending" with an alert raised, never silent | Integration (stub) + sandbox if PayGate can simulate a refund failure | R02 | N/A — not yet run |
| G3 (TC-SPLIT-003) | Odd total (e.g. 10,001 cents) split: card 1 gets the extra cent, both charges sum to the total, amounts shown match | Unit + E2E sandbox | R03 | N/A — not yet run |
| G4 (TC-SPLIT-004) | Charge timeout followed by retry produces one charge per card, not two | Integration (stub) + sandbox | R04 | N/A — not yet run |
| G5 (TC-SPLIT-005) | Card 1 declined: no charge on card 2, no refund, order unpaid, customer told | E2E sandbox | R05 | N/A — not yet run |
| G6 (TC-SPLIT-006) | Single-card checkout: existing regression suite green and a manual single-card order succeeds on staging with the flag off and with the flag on | Regression + E2E | R10, R12 | N/A — not yet run |
| G7 (TC-SPLIT-007) | Happy path: both charges succeed, order paid, both transaction IDs stored and shown on the receipt | E2E sandbox | R05, R08 | N/A — not yet run |

A failed gate case blocks the release. Analysis cases (TC-SPLIT-008 onward: validation boundaries, locale, accessibility, messaging, reconciliation view) inform; if an analysis finding turns out to be caused by the change and would stop the release, its case moves into the gate with a dated note. Findings not caused by this change go to their own tickets and never gate it.

**Execution order (risk-based, overridden by the sandbox resource window and by dependencies).**

1. G6 regression suite on the first feature build, any day: it needs no sandbox and protects 4,000 orders a day.
2. G3 unit tests and the arithmetic property test, as soon as the module exists (no sandbox needed).
3. 2026-10-28 (sandbox, first window): record real responses for success, hard decline, soft decline, timeout; confirm decline-simulation card numbers. Dependency: the stub (A6) is built from these recordings, so this runs before any stub-based case.
4. G1, G2, G4, G5, G7 on the stub, in that order, as soon as integration is complete (any day).
5. 2026-10-30 (sandbox): G7 then G1, G5, G3 on the sandbox. G7 runs first because G1 and G5 reuse its fixture order and confirm the sandbox is healthy.
6. 2026-11-04 (sandbox): G4, G2 (if PayGate can simulate refund failure), then re-run of anything that failed on 2026-10-30 after a fix; PO acceptance walkthrough of G1, G5, G7.
7. 2026-11-06 (sandbox, last window): full gate G1 to G7 on the release candidate build. Nothing new is tested on this day; it is the confirmation run.
8. Analysis cases and exploratory sessions on stub days (2026-10-29, 2026-10-31, 2026-11-03, 2026-11-05), in the order R07, R08, R06, R18, R19.
9. If a gate case fails on 2026-11-06, the release either slips to the next sandbox window (2026-11-10) or ships with the flag off; the PO decides on the evening of 2026-11-06.

**Metrics to collect.**

- Test progress: gate cases run / passed per sandbox day (decision: is 2026-11-06 a confirmation run or a first run?).
- Defect: open defects by severity, with age (decision: exception or slip?).
- Risk coverage: CRITICAL and HIGH rows with at least one passed case on the sandbox (decision: residual risk at go/no-go).
- Refund timing: elapsed time from decline to refund acknowledgement, every run (decision: R01 met or not).
- Project: tester hours spent against the estimate in item 7 (decision: cut analysis scope on 2026-11-03 if over 70% consumed).

**Test data and environment.** Fixture set (credentials kept in the team's secret store, not here):

| Fixture | Description | State assumed | May be changed | How to rebuild |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FX-ORD-ODD | Order with total 10,001 cents | Unpaid, in cart | Read only; copy before paying | Seed script (developer-provided) |
| FX-ORD-EVEN | Order with total 10,000 cents | Unpaid, in cart | Read only; copy before paying | Seed script |
| FX-ORD-MIN | Order with total 2 cents | Unpaid | Read only; copy | Seed script |
| FX-CARD-OK-A, FX-CARD-OK-B | Two sandbox cards that succeed | Active | Read only | PayGate documentation |
| FX-CARD-HARD-DECLINE | Sandbox card that always declines | Active | Read only | PayGate documentation |
| FX-CARD-TIMEOUT | Sandbox card or amount that triggers a timeout | Active | Read only | PayGate documentation; if none exists, stub only and G4 sandbox run becomes "verified on stub" with a recorded exception |
| FX-STUB-PROFILES | Stub outcome profiles: success, hard decline, soft decline, timeout, refund timeout, gateway 500 | Built from 2026-10-28 recordings | Developers only | Re-record on a sandbox day |
| FX-SINGLE | Single-card order used by G6 | Unpaid | Copy per run | Seed script |

Environments: CI (unit, integration, stub); Staging with stub (every day); Staging pointed at PayGate sandbox (Tuesdays and Thursdays only, switched by configuration and recorded in each result); Production, flag off, for the post-deploy smoke.

**Deviations from the test policy and strategy.** The E2E share is slightly above the backend preset's 10% because the real gateway can only be exercised end to end; accepted for this release. No load test of the split path; accepted because volume is unknown and the single-card latency comparison covers the shared path.

## 7. Estimate

**Technique.** Three-point estimation, tester's effort only, decomposed by task; the developers' test effort is inside their build estimate. Chosen because one estimator is available, the work is new and the margin matters against a hard 40-hour budget.

| Task | a | m | b | E |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plan, risk register, assumptions to PO | 3 | 4 | 6 | 4.2 |
| Test case design (gate + analysis, about 20 cases) | 5 | 7 | 10 | 7.2 |
| Sandbox day 1: recordings, fixtures, stub validation | 3 | 4 | 5 | 4.0 |
| Sandbox days 2–4: gate runs, re-runs, PO walkthrough | 9 | 11 | 14 | 11.2 |
| Stub-day execution: analysis cases, exploratory sessions (3 × 1 h), regression reading | 5 | 7 | 10 | 7.2 |
| Defect reports, progress reports, completion report | 3 | 4 | 6 | 4.2 |
| **Total** | **28** | **37** | **51** | **38 ± 3.8** |

**Result.** 38 ± 4 tester hours (between 34 and 42) against a 40-hour budget. The budget holds only at the most likely path; the pessimistic case exceeds it by about 11 hours.

**Assumptions behind the figure.** The stub exists by 2026-10-29 (A6); the existing regression suite runs without tester effort (A7); no more than two gate cases fail on the sandbox and need a re-run; the PO answers A1 to A4 within two days. If the stub is late, add 6–8 hours of sandbox-day rework and cut the analysis cases first (R15).

## 8. Budget and Schedule

Budget: 40 tester hours plus developer test effort inside the build. No tool purchase; PayGate sandbox is already provisioned.

| Day | Date | Sandbox | Tester (4 h) | Developers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Mon 2026-10-27 | No | Plan review with team, assumptions to PO, start case design | Build; split module with unit tests first |
| 2 | Tue 2026-10-28 | Yes | Record real responses, confirm decline cards, fixture set | Build stub from recordings |
| 3 | Wed 2026-10-29 | No | Finish gate cases, run G3 unit review, G6 regression on first build | Integration, idempotency, refund retry |
| 4 | Thu 2026-10-30 | Yes | G7, G1, G5, G3 on sandbox; progress report 1 | Fixes |
| 5 | Fri 2026-10-31 | No | Entry criteria check; stub runs of G2, G4; analysis cases R07 | Code complete target |
| 6 | Mon 2026-11-03 | No | Exploratory R08, R06 with finance; 70% budget checkpoint | Fixes; latency comparison R11 |
| 7 | Tue 2026-11-04 | Yes | G4, G2 on sandbox; re-runs; PO walkthrough; progress report 2 | Fixes |
| 8 | Wed 2026-11-05 | No | Exploratory R18, R19; flag-off and rollback dry run with Ops; defect verification on stub | Release candidate build cut |
| 9 | Thu 2026-11-06 | Yes | Full gate G1–G7 on the release candidate; completion report draft; go/no-go with PO | On call for blocking fixes only |
| 10 | Fri 2026-11-07 | No | Release; production smoke with flag off, then flag on for a small cohort if Ops supports it | Deploy, monitor refund alerts |

Contingency: if the release candidate is not ready for 2026-11-06, the gate cannot be confirmed on the real gateway before release. The decision is then slip to 2026-11-10 (next sandbox) or ship flag-off; recorded on 2026-11-05 at the latest.

## 9. Configuration Management of Testware

- This plan, the test cases, the stub profiles, the seed scripts and the reports live in the repository beside the feature code, under version control, with the plan ID and version above; changes after sharing are made with a dated correction note, never by deletion.
- Every case references the requirement it covers (brief sentence or assumption ID) and every result names the build version and the environment (CI, staging-stub, staging-sandbox, production) it was obtained on. "Latest build" is not accepted in a result.
- The staging environment is a baseline: application build, stub version, PayGate sandbox configuration and feature-flag state are recorded with each sandbox day's report, so a result from 2026-10-30 can be reproduced on 2026-11-06 by restoring the same versions.
- The stub recordings from 2026-10-28 are a versioned artifact; re-recording creates a new version and the affected results are re-run.
- CI runs the unit, integration and regression suites on every build and stores results with the commit hash; the gate results from sandbox days are attached to the board ticket with build and date.

# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Plan ID | TP-SPLIT-5.3 |
| Version | 0.1, 2026-10-24 (first draft, not yet shared) |
| Owner (test management role) | The half-time tester |
| Board | N/A — tracker URL not given; the plan refers to tickets by key `SPLIT-nn` once they exist |
| Release date | Friday 2026-11-07 (10 working days from Friday 2026-10-24) |
| PayGate sandbox days in the window | Tue 2026-10-28, Thu 2026-10-30, Tue 2026-11-04, Thu 2026-11-06 (four days) |

## 1. Context of testing

**Scope.**

In scope:

- The split payment flow: amount entry for card 1, derivation of the card 2 amount, both charges through PayGate, order placement on double approval.
- The compensation path: card 2 declined, card 1 refunded automatically within 60 seconds, order not placed, customer told what happened.
- The split arithmetic in cents, including the remainder cent going to card 1.
- Regression of the existing single-card checkout (about 4,000 orders a day), which must keep working with the feature on and off.
- Tampering resistance of the amounts sent from the browser.

Out of scope:

- PayGate's own correctness (its sandbox is the oracle for its responses, not a test object).
- Load and stress testing of checkout. There is no load environment or time in the window; a latency check on the split path replaces it (see item 6, deviations).
- Three or more cards, saved-card wallets, 3-D Secure challenges, and partial refunds of a completed split order. Assumed not part of release 5.3.
- Accounting reconciliation reports. Covered by a non-test measure (item 5, R06) rather than by tests.

**Objectives.**

1. Show that no customer can be charged for an order that is not placed, and that no placed order is charged more or less than its total.
2. Show that the single-card checkout behaves exactly as it does today, feature flag on or off.
3. Give the release decision a record of what passed, what did not run and which risks stay open, measured on a named build and environment.

**Test basis.**

- The feature brief above (the only written source available).
- PayGate's API documentation for charge, refund and idempotency semantics (assumed to exist; version to be recorded on first sandbox day).
- The existing single-card checkout tests and their last results (assumed to exist in the repository).
- Acceptance scenarios to be written from this plan with `/qa-bdd` on day 1, so the brief gets a testable rewrite before code lands.

## 2. Assumptions and constraints

Assumptions (each stated because the brief does not settle it; each is a question for the product owner on day 1, and testing proceeds on the assumption until answered):

- A1. The card 1 amount is entered in whole cents and must be at least 1 cent and at most total minus 1 cent. Zero and the full total are rejected with a message pointing the customer to single-card checkout.
- A2. The remainder-cent rule applies to a "split evenly" shortcut that halves an odd total; manual entry needs no rounding since it is already in cents.
- A3. Charges run sequentially: card 1 first, card 2 only after card 1 is approved. If card 1 is declined, card 2 is never attempted.
- A4. The 60-second refund target is measured from PayGate's decline response for card 2 to PayGate's acceptance of the refund request.
- A5. The feature ships behind a feature flag, off by default, so the off state is production's current behavior and can be tested as such.
- A6. Charge requests to PayGate carry an idempotency key, so a retry after a timeout cannot charge the same card twice.
- A7. A refund that fails raises an alert to support with the order and charge identifiers, and a manual refund runbook exists or will be written by release.
- A8. The stack is a web front end over a backend checkout service that owns the split arithmetic and the charge orchestration. The pyramid preset in item 6 rests on this.
- A9. Staging is deployed from a CI pipeline and the deployed build is identifiable by commit.
- A10. One currency, no fees or rounding in PayGate's responses.

Constraints:

- C1. PayGate's sandbox is available only on Tuesdays and Thursdays: four days in the window. Every test that needs the real gateway is pinned to those days; every other day runs against a PayGate stub the developers maintain.
- C2. One tester at half time, about 40 person-hours across the window, plus two developers.
- C3. Release in 10 working days with no slack for a second sandbox cycle after Thursday 2026-11-06.
- C4. Single-card checkout runs about 4,000 orders a day, so any regression costs money within hours.

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Who | Responsibility | Relevance to testing |
| :--- | :-- | :------------- | :------------------- |
| Product owner | N/A — name not given; assumed one exists | Confirms assumptions A1 to A7, accepts residual risk at the gate, signs the completion report | Owns the exceptions on P1 failures and the go/no-go |
| Developers (2) | The two building the feature | Unit and integration tests, PayGate stub, fixes, feature flag and kill switch | Hold the testing role at component and component integration level; one developer peer-reviews the other's tests |
| Tester (half time) | The one tester | Test analysis, design and execution at system and system integration level; monitoring and reporting | Holds the test management role and the testing role for the higher levels |
| Support / operations | N/A — not named; assumed a support function exists | Handles refund-failure alerts and the manual refund runbook | Validates the runbook once, on a sandbox day |
| PayGate account contact | N/A — not named | Sandbox access, test card list, API version | Blocks every sandbox-day test if access fails |
| Finance | N/A — not named | First-week reconciliation of split orders after release | Non-test control for arithmetic and refund risks |

## 4. Communication

| Form | Frequency | Template |
| :--- | :-------- | :------- |
| Stand-up note from the tester (progress, blockers, next sandbox day plan) | Daily, written in the team channel | Three lines: done, next, blocked |
| Progress report | After each of the four sandbox days | The progress report content in the package's reporting reference: period, progress against plan, impediments, metrics, new risks, next period |
| Defect reports | As found | `/qa-defect` format, `DR-SPLIT-NNN`, one ticket per finding, linked from this plan |
| Risk register review | At each progress report | Re-score rows in place with a dated note; never delete a row |
| Completion report with go/no-go record | Friday 2026-11-07, before the release decision | Every case one per row, "Not run — resume point" section, residual risks and defects not fixed |
| Retrospective | Week after release | Whole team; three questions; actions with owner and date |

## 5. Risk register

Scale: likelihood 1 to 5, impact 1 to 5, score is the product. Levels: 15 to 25 critical, 8 to 14 high, 4 to 7 medium, 1 to 3 low.

| # | ID | Risk description | Category | L | I | Score | Level | Mitigation strategy | Owner |

| 2 | R02 | Double charge: a timeout after card 1 or card 2 is charged leads to a retry that charges again | Product | 3 | 5 | 15 | 🔴 Critical | Idempotency key per charge (A6) checked by integration test against the stub with injected timeouts; one sandbox probe of PayGate's idempotency behaviour on day 1 | Dev |

## 6. Test approach

**Test levels, who tests and independence.**

| Level | Test object | Who tests | Independence | Why this degree fits |
| :---- | :---------- | :-------- | :----------- | :------------------- |
| Component (unit) | Split function, amount validation, orchestration state machine | The developer who wrote it, tests reviewed by the other developer | None to some | Fast feedback on arithmetic and state logic; peer review catches the author's blind spots on boundaries |
| Component integration | Checkout service against the PayGate stub: sequencing, timeouts, idempotency, persistence between calls | The other developer (not the author) | Some | The double-charge and orphan-charge risks (R02, R05) are interaction defects; a second pair of eyes on the stub contract matters |
| System and system integration | Full checkout on staging against PayGate sandbox and against the stub | The tester | High (did not write the code, same organisation) | Money-moving defects need someone who challenges the implementation's assumptions, which is what the critical rows ask for |
| Acceptance | The BDD scenarios on sandbox day 3 | Product owner, walked through by the tester | High | Validates the assumptions A1 to A7 against business intent, not just against the code |

**Test types.** Functional (all levels); non-functional: security (amount tampering, R07), performance efficiency limited to a latency comparison (R11), reliability of the compensation path (R01, R05, R06). Accessibility: a keyboard-only pass of the new amount field during the exploratory session; no full audit (see deviations).

**Pyramid preset.** Backend / API: 70 % unit, 20 % integration, 10 % end to end, because the split arithmetic, the orchestration and the refund rule live in the checkout service (A8). The UI adds one amount field and a confirmation screen, covered by two component tests and the end-to-end gate cases.

**Testing quadrants.**

- Q1 (technology facing, supports the team): unit and integration tests in CI, owned by developers.
- Q2 (business facing, supports the team): BDD scenarios from `/qa-bdd`, API tests of the checkout endpoint.
- Q3 (business facing, critiques the product): two exploratory sessions on sandbox days 3 and 4 (charters: "break the compensation path", "what does the customer see when it goes wrong"); acceptance walkthrough with the product owner.
- Q4 (technology facing, critiques the product): smoke suite on every build; tampering tests; latency comparison. No load test, by decision (deviations).

**Techniques by risk level.**

| Risk rows | Technique | Coverage items and target |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------------ |
| R01, R05 (critical, high) | State transition testing on the orchestration: Pending, Card1Charged, Card2Charged/OrderPlaced, Refunding, Refunded, RefundFailed, Card1Declined | All transitions, valid and invalid attempted, one invalid transition per case |
| R02 (critical) | Error guessing and decision table: timeout before/after PayGate records the charge × retry with same/different idempotency key | Every feasible column |
| R04, R08 (high) | BVA (3-value) on the card 1 amount: 0, 1, 2, total−2, total−1, total, total+1; EP on the input: whole cents valid, negative, non-numeric, three decimals invalid; "split evenly" on even and odd totals and on a 1-cent total | Every boundary and every partition |
| R03 (high) | Regression: the existing single-card suite, flag on and flag off | 100 % of the suite's P0 and P1 cases on each build |
| R06, R07 (high) | Checklist-based: refund failure handling; tampered request bodies (sum below total, negative card 2, card 1 above total) | Every checklist item |
| R09, R10, R11 (high to medium) | Exploratory sessions with charters; scripted latency comparison | Session notes with findings; one timing table |
| R12 to R16 (project) | N/A — project risks are controlled by schedule and ownership, not by test cases | N/A — no coverage item |

**Deliverables.**

- Acceptance scenarios (`.feature`), day 1.
- Test cases `TC-SPLIT-NNN` with ISTQB technique rows, days 1 to 3.
- PayGate stub recordings from sandbox day 1, owned by the developers.
- Fixture set document (below).
- Four progress reports, one completion report with the go/no-go record, defect reports.

**Entry criteria.**

Component and component integration (developers):

- Acceptance scenarios reviewed by the product owner.
- Stub built from sandbox recordings (after Tuesday 2026-10-28).

System and system integration (tester), checked Monday 2026-11-03:

- Feature flag, split flow and compensation path merged and deployed to staging from a CI run that passed, build identified by commit.
- Unit and integration suites green in CI, branch coverage of the split and orchestration modules at or above 80 %.
- PayGate sandbox credentials and test cards available (fixture set complete).
- Amount field and confirmation screen carry `data-testid` attributes.
- Refund-failure alert wired to a test channel.

**Exit criteria** (measured against the release gate below and the full case list):

- Every release gate case passed on the final build, on staging, with the real sandbox where the case requires it.
- 100 % of P0 cases run and passed; 100 % of P1 run and passed or each failure carries a recorded product-owner exception.
- Zero open critical defects; zero open high defects without a recorded exception.
- Single-card regression suite passed with the flag on and with the flag off.
- Refund latency measured on sandbox: every observed compensation under 60 s, and the production alert on refund latency deployed.
- Completion report signed by the tester and the product owner.

If time runs out before these are met, testing stops only when the product owner has reviewed the open items and recorded acceptance of the risk.

**Release gate.** The smallest set whose failure stops the release. Results are filled in on the final build.

| ID | What it proves | Needs sandbox | Risk | Result |
| :- | :------------- | :------------ | :--- | :----- |
| G1 | Split with both cards approved places the order; the two PayGate charges sum exactly to the order total | Yes | R04 | N/A — not yet run |
| G2 | "Split evenly" on an odd total puts the extra cent on card 1 (10.01 → 5.01 and 5.00) and both charges are recorded in cents | Yes | R04 | N/A — not yet run |
| G3 | Card 2 declined: card 1 is refunded automatically, the refund request is accepted within 60 s of the decline, no order is placed, the customer sees why | Yes | R01 | N/A — not yet run |
| G4 | Card 1 declined: card 2 is never charged, no order is placed | Yes | R01, A3 | N/A — not yet run |
| G5 | Single-card checkout, flag on: the existing regression suite passes on the release build | Yes | R03 | N/A — not yet run |
| G6 | Card 1 amount of 0 and of the full total are rejected; the backend rejects a tampered body whose two amounts sum below the total | No (stub) | R07, R08 | N/A — not yet run |
| G7 | Timeout after card 2 is charged, then retry: exactly one charge per card exists at PayGate and the order is placed once | No (stub; idempotency probed on sandbox day 1) | R02 | N/A — not yet run |
| G8 | Flag off: checkout page, request payload and PayGate calls are byte-for-byte what the previous build produced | No | R03 | N/A — not yet run |

Cases that fail for reasons the change did not cause get their own ticket and stay out of the gate's pass/fail. If an analysis finding turns out to be caused by the change, its case moves into the gate with a dated note here.

**Execution order.** Risk-based by default; the sandbox window and two dependencies move cases.

1. G8 on Monday 2026-10-27, on the stub, before any feature code is deployed: records the baseline the flag-off comparison needs (dependency: G8 needs the previous build's recording first).
2. Sandbox day 1, Tuesday 2026-10-28: single-card regression on sandbox to baseline G5; PayGate idempotency and refund probes that G7 and the stub depend on (resource window: real gateway needed, and the stub cannot be trusted until these recordings exist).
3. Unit and integration cases as code lands, days 2 to 6, developers, on every push.
4. G6 and G7 on the stub as soon as the orchestration is merged, days 4 to 6 (no sandbox needed, so they run before the sandbox cases despite lower risk than G3).
5. Sandbox day 2, Thursday 2026-10-30: G1 and G2 if the split flow is deployed, else repeat of step 2 with the first deployed parts; contract check of stub against sandbox.
6. Sandbox day 3, Tuesday 2026-11-04, the main run: G3, G4, G1, G2, G5 in that order (G3 first because it carries the critical risk), then exploratory session 1 and the acceptance walkthrough.
7. Days 7 and 8 on the stub: remaining analysis cases (receipts, emails, same-card, validation partitions), fixes retested.
8. Sandbox day 4, Thursday 2026-11-06: retest of every gate case that failed or changed since day 3, full gate rerun on the release candidate, exploratory session 2, refund latency table, runbook check with support.
9. Friday 2026-11-07: completion report and go/no-go record.

**Metrics to collect.**

- Gate cases passed / 8, per build (decides go/no-go).
- Single-card regression pass rate per build, flag on and flag off (decides whether R03 is live).
- Refund latency: every compensation observed on sandbox, max and count over 60 s (decides R01 residual risk).
- Risk coverage: register rows with at least one executed case / 11 product rows (decides what the completion report declares untested).
- Open defects by severity (exit criterion).
- Tester hours spent against the estimate in item 7, checked at each progress report (triggers the cut list).

Control directives are recorded with their reason at the next progress report. Pre-agreed ones: if the entry criteria are unmet on Monday 2026-11-03, the product owner chooses on that day between slipping the release and shipping with the flag off; if hours spent exceed the estimate's upper bound by day 3, analysis cases for R09 and R10 are dropped first, then exploratory session 2.

**Test data: fixture set.** Credentials live in the team's secret store; this document names records, never secrets.

| Fixture | Description | State assumed | May tests write to it | Rebuild |
| :------ | :---------- | :------------ | :-------------------- | :------ |
| F01 PayGate sandbox account | Merchant account for staging | Active, API version recorded on day 1 | Read only; charges and refunds are the expected writes and are logged | PayGate contact; nobody in the team can |
| F02 Test cards: approve, decline, insufficient funds, refund-fails (if offered), timeout (if offered) | PayGate-documented card numbers | As documented | Read only | From PayGate docs |
| F03 Orders with totals 0.01, 0.02, 10.00, 10.01, 999,999.99 (assumed maximum) | Seeded carts on staging | Unpaid | Tests consume them; reseed after each run | Seed script owned by developers |
| F04 Customer account for checkout | Staging customer with a shipping address | Logged out | Order history grows; nothing else | Seed script |
| F05 Previous-build recording for G8 | Captured page, payload and gateway calls from the pre-feature build | Captured on 2026-10-27 | Read only | Recapture from the previous build tag |
| F06 Stub recordings | PayGate responses captured on day 1 | Versioned with the stub | Read only | Recapture on any sandbox day |

A case whose fixture is missing or in the wrong state is blocked, not failed.

**Environment.** Staging deployed by CI from a named commit, feature flag readable from the flag service, PayGate stub selectable by configuration, refund alert routed to a test channel. The flag state and the gateway (sandbox or stub) are recorded in every result.

**Deviations from the test policy and strategy.**

- No load test: no load environment and no time; the latency comparison in R11 and the canary rollout stand in for it, and the residual risk is recorded.
- No full accessibility audit: one new field; a keyboard pass covers it, and a full audit is deferred to the next release.
- Component integration tests of the gateway run against a stub five days out of seven: a deliberate acceptance of R14, controlled by the day 1 recordings and the day 3 contract check.

**Non-test measures.** Feature flag as kill switch; canary at 5 % of orders for the first day with an automatic halt if checkout error rate rises above the previous week's mean plus 50 %; refund-failure alert and manual runbook; finance reconciliation of all split orders in week one; production alert on refund latency above 45 s.

## 7. Estimate

Technique: three-point estimation, one estimator, decomposed by task. Values are tester person-hours.

| Task | a | m | b |
| :--- | :- | :- | :- |
| Test analysis and design (scenarios, cases, fixture set) | 6 | 8 | 12 |
| Stub-based system and API runs on non-sandbox days | 4 | 6 | 10 |
| Four sandbox days (gate, contract check, exploration) | 12 | 16 | 20 |
| Defect reporting and retests | 3 | 4 | 8 |
| Progress reports, completion report, go/no-go record | 3 | 4 | 6 |
| Total | 28 | 38 | 56 |

E = (28 + 4 × 38 + 56) / 6 = 39.3; SD = (56 − 28) / 6 = 4.7.

**Tester effort: 39 ± 5 person-hours (between 35 and 44), against 40 available.** The pessimistic value exceeds capacity, which is why R13 is critical and the cut list exists.

Developer test effort is not estimated here; the assumption is that each developer spends about a third of the window on tests and the stub (about 24 hours each), and that the stub is ready by Wednesday 2026-10-29.

Assumptions behind the figures: sandbox access works on the first attempt; the feature meets the entry criteria on Monday 2026-11-03; the single-card regression suite is automated and runs in under 30 minutes; no more than four defects of high severity or above are found.

## 8. Budget and schedule

Budget: N/A — no monetary budget given; the cost is the staffing above and the PayGate sandbox, which is assumed already contracted.

| Day | Date | Sandbox | Developers | Tester (about 4 h) |
| :- | :--- | :------ | :--------- | :----------------- |
| 1 | Mon 2026-10-27 | No | Flag, split function, orchestration skeleton | Confirm assumptions with product owner; BDD scenarios; capture F05; G8 baseline |
| 2 | Tue 2026-10-28 | Yes | Record PayGate responses for the stub | Single-card regression on sandbox; idempotency and refund probes; progress report 1 |
| 3 | Wed 2026-10-29 | No | Stub ready; unit tests for arithmetic and state machine | Test cases for critical and high rows; fixture set |
| 4 | Thu 2026-10-30 | Yes | Integration tests against stub; deploy to staging | G1, G2 if deployed, else contract check only; progress report 2 |
| 5 | Fri 2026-10-31 | No | Compensation path, alert, recovery job | G6, G7 on stub; API tampering cases |
| 6 | Mon 2026-11-03 | No | Code complete; fixes | Entry criteria check; control decision if unmet |
| 7 | Tue 2026-11-04 | Yes | On call for fixes | Main run: G3, G4, G1, G2, G5; exploratory session 1; acceptance walkthrough; progress report 3 |
| 8 | Wed 2026-11-05 | No | Fixes | Remaining analysis cases on stub; retests on stub |
| 9 | Thu 2026-11-06 | Yes | Release candidate cut by 09:00 | Full gate rerun; exploratory session 2; refund latency table; runbook check; progress report 4 |
| 10 | Fri 2026-11-07 | No | Release behind flag, canary 5 % | Completion report; go/no-go record; post-release sanity |

## 9. Configuration management of testware

- Test cases, scenarios, the fixture set, this plan and the stub recordings live in the application repository under version control, each with an identifier (`TP-SPLIT-5.3`, `TC-SPLIT-NNN`, `DR-SPLIT-NNN`, `F0n`) and linked to the `SPLIT-nn` ticket they trace to.
- Every result names the staging build by commit and pipeline run, the flag state, and whether the gateway was the sandbox (with its API version) or the stub (with its recording version). A result without these is not accepted into a report.
- The staging environment, once it passes the entry criteria on Monday 2026-11-03, is the baseline; changes to it after that go through the team's change process and are noted in the next progress report.
- The pre-feature build tag and the F05 recording are kept so the G8 comparison can be reproduced.
- CI runs unit and integration suites on every push and the smoke suite on every deployment; the gate cases that need the sandbox are run by the tester and their evidence is attached to the ticket.
- Corrections to this plan after it is shared are made in place with a dated note; nothing is deleted.

# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Plan ID | TP-SPLIT-5.3 |
| Version | 1.0, 2026-10-24 |
| Owner (test management role) | QA tester (half time) |
| Tracker | N/A — tracker not named in the brief; assumed to be the team's existing board, tickets referenced as `SPLIT-nnn` |
| Release date | Friday 2026-11-06 (10 working days, Mon–Fri, assuming no public holidays in the window; if 2026-11-02 is a holiday locally, every date from D6 on slips one day and the release becomes 2026-11-09) |

## 1. Context of testing

**Scope, in:**

- Split of one order total across two cards: customer-chosen amount on card 1, remainder on card 2, integer cents, remainder cent on card 1.
- Two sequential PayGate charges for one order.
- Automatic refund of charge 1 within 60 seconds when charge 2 is declined.
- Order, payment and ledger state after every outcome (both succeed, first declined, second declined, refund fails).
- Regression of the existing single-card checkout (about 4,000 orders a day).
- Test levels: component, component integration, system integration (against PayGate sandbox), acceptance.

**Scope, out:**

- More than two cards (not in the brief).
- Partial refunds or refunds of a completed split order after fulfilment (post-purchase refund flow unchanged; assumed to be covered by existing regression).
- PayGate's own behaviour (contractual, outside our control); we test our handling of its responses.
- Load testing of checkout: no load tooling or environment is named, and 10 days with a half-time tester cannot build one. Covered instead by a non-test measure (canary rollout, item 6).
- Currencies without minor units: assumed every supported currency has 2 decimal minor units.

**Objectives:**

1. Prove that the split rules produce two amounts that always sum to the order total, with the odd cent on card 1.
2. Prove that money is never left in an inconsistent state: no order is placed with only one successful charge, and no customer is charged twice for one order.
3. Prove that the compensating refund is issued within 60 seconds of a declined second charge.
4. Prove that single-card checkout behaves exactly as before.

**Test basis:** the feature brief above; PayGate API documentation (sandbox test cards and decline codes); the existing single-card checkout behaviour as deployed today (recorded on D2 as the oracle). Acceptance criteria beyond the brief: N/A — none written yet; the 7 rules in the risk register's "test conditions" below are proposed as the acceptance criteria and should be confirmed by the Product Owner on D1.

## 2. Assumptions and constraints

**Assumptions (stated because the brief does not say):**

- A1. Architecture is a web front end plus a backend payment service; the split, sequencing and refund logic lives in the backend. PayGate is called from the backend only.
- A2. Card data is tokenised by PayGate; our system never stores PAN. Security testing targets amount tampering and idempotency, not card storage.
- A3. The 60-second window is measured from the moment our system receives PayGate's decline for charge 2 to the moment PayGate acknowledges the refund request for charge 1.
- A4. The feature ships behind a feature flag. If it does not, the plan asks for one (item 6, non-test measures); without it, R03 is re-scored to likelihood 3.
- A5. A staging environment exists that can point at PayGate's sandbox, and a stub of PayGate exists or will be written by the developers by D3 for non-sandbox days.
- A6. Charge order is fixed: card 1 is charged first, card 2 second. If charge 1 is declined, charge 2 is never attempted.
- A7. Minimum amount per card is 1 cent (so the card 1 amount is in the range 1 to total − 1). To be confirmed by the Product Owner on D1.
- A8. A Product Owner exists and accepts the feature; the two developers also hold the automation role for unit and integration tests.
- A9. CI runs unit and integration tests on every push and the team practises continuous delivery (a person decides the release), not continuous deployment.

**Constraints:**

- PayGate sandbox reachable only on Tuesdays and Thursdays: D2 (2026-10-27), D4 (10-29), D7 (11-03), D9 (11-05). Four windows in total; the last one is one day before release.
- Tester capacity: 10 days × 4 h = 40 h.
- Developers: 2, building the feature in the same window; their test effort competes with build effort.
- Single-card checkout cannot be degraded: 4,000 orders a day in production.

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Who | Responsibility | Relevance to testing |
| :--- | :-- | :------------- | :------------------- |
| Test management and testing role | QA tester (half time) | Plan, design, system integration execution, reporting, go/no-go record | Owns this plan and the release gate evidence |
| Developers (2) | Feature authors | Unit and component integration tests, PayGate stub, defect fixes, decline-code catalogue | Hold the testing role at component levels; provide the stub by D3 |
| Product Owner | N/A — not named; assumed to exist | Confirms acceptance criteria (D1), accepts P1 exceptions, signs go/no-go | Acceptance decision |
| Payments / finance | N/A — not named; assumed a finance contact exists | Reconciliation of PayGate settlements against orders after release | Monitors the non-test measure for R01, R02, R04 |
| PayGate support | External | Sandbox availability, decline-code behaviour | Contingency when a sandbox window is lost |

## 4. Communication

| Form | Frequency | Template |
| :--- | :-------- | :------- |
| Daily stand-up note (progress, blockers, next sandbox window plan) | Daily, written in the ticket | Progress report content of the `qa-reference` skill's `references/test-reporting.md` |
| Sandbox-day results page | End of each sandbox day (D2, D4, D7, D9) | "Reporting Every Case" row format, one case per row, with build and environment |

| 5 | R05 | Refund request itself fails or times out: order stuck with one charge captured and no refund | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Gate case G6 with stub returning refund failure; retry with backoff; alert and manual-refund queue; daily reconciliation report (non-test measure) | Dev/QA |
| 6 | R06 | Server trusts client-submitted amounts: tampered split (a + b ≠ total, negative, zero, non-integer cents, above total) accepted | Product | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Server-side validation; EP/BVA at API level; gate case G5 | Dev/QA |
| 7 | R07 | Order placed, ledger or order status wrong after a partial failure (shows paid when refunded, or pending forever) | Product | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | State transition cases check order status, payment records and customer-facing message after every outcome | QA |
| 8 | R08 | Same card used for both halves accepted or rejected inconsistently | Product | 2 | 2 | 4 | 🟡 MEDIUM | One analysis case; behaviour to be decided by Product Owner on D1 (assumed: allowed) | QA |
| 9 | R09 | Checkout latency doubles with two sequential gateway calls; front-end or gateway timeout fires before charge 2 completes | Product | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Measure end-to-end time on sandbox days; timeout values reviewed against PayGate p99; canary watch on checkout p95 | Dev |
| 10 | R10 | PayGate sandbox behaviour differs from production (decline codes, refund latency), so sandbox passes do not predict production | Product | 3 | 3 | 9 | 🟠 HIGH | Decline-code catalogue from PayGate docs reviewed on D1; canary rollout with a declined-second-card test purchase on a real card by the team on release day | Dev/QA |
| 11 | R11 | Only four sandbox windows; a lost window (outage, build not ready) leaves gate cases unrun before release | Project | 4 | 4 | 16 | 🔴 CRITICAL | Sandbox-facing cases scheduled first on each window; stub-based runs on other days; code freeze on gateway-facing code after D7; if D9 is lost, release decision waits for the next window (2026-11-10) | QA/PO |
| 12 | R12 | Half-time tester (40 h) cannot cover design, execution and reporting; estimate (item 7) uses 38 ± 4 h | Project | 4 | 3 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Developers own unit and integration levels; analysis cases below MEDIUM dropped first; progress reported daily against the estimate | QA |
| 13 | R13 | Feature not "Ready for QA" before D4, leaving only two sandbox windows for the gate | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Backend-first delivery: payment service ready for API tests by D3, UI by D5; D2 window used for oracle and sandbox calibration so no window is wasted | Dev |
| 14 | R14 | Acceptance criteria not written; tester and developers interpret edge rules (A6, A7, R08) differently | Project | 3 | 3 | 9 | 🟠 HIGH | Static review of the brief with the three amigos on D1 (`/qa-static`); the 7 test conditions below adopted as acceptance criteria | PO |

**Test conditions derived from the brief and the assumptions** (proposed acceptance criteria):

1. Card 1 amount must be in the range 1 to total − 1 cents (A7); any other value is rejected server-side with a field-level error.
2. Card 2 amount = total − card 1 amount; both are integers in cents; their sum equals the order total.
3. When the customer asks for an even split of an odd total, card 1 receives the extra cent.
4. Charges are sequential: card 1 then card 2; card 2 is not attempted if card 1 is declined.
5. If card 2 is declined, card 1 is refunded within 60 seconds, the order is not placed, and the customer sees why.
6. If the refund fails, the order is marked for manual refund, an alert is raised and the customer is told the refund is being processed.
7. Single-card checkout behaves as before with the feature on and off.

## 6. Test approach

**Pyramid preset:** Backend / API heavy (70% unit, 20% integration, 10% end to end). The split arithmetic, sequencing and compensation all live in the backend service (A1); the UI only collects one amount.

**Levels, who tests, independence:**

| Level | Test object | What it proves | Who tests | Independence | Why this degree |
| :---- | :---------- | :------------- | :-------- | :----------- | :-------------- |
| Component | Split function, validation, state machine | R02, R06 arithmetic and partitions | Developers | None | Cheap, fast, written with the code; the arithmetic is deterministic and the tester reviews the unit test list on D3 |
| Component integration | Payment service with PayGate stub | R01, R04, R05, R07 sequences including timeouts and refund failure, which the sandbox cannot inject on demand | Developer B tests developer A's work | Some | A peer catches assumptions the author made; runs every day, not only Tue/Thu |
| System integration | Staging against PayGate sandbox | Real gateway responses, timing of the 60 s refund, R10 | QA tester | High | Money-handling defects need a different perspective from the authors; the tester is outside the pair that built it |
| Acceptance | Staging, flag on | Business rules 1 to 7 | Product Owner, guided by the tester | High | Validation that the rules match the business intent |

**Types:** functional (all levels), security (amount tampering and idempotency, API level), performance (checkout time measured on sandbox days, no load test), reliability (refund retry and failure paths, integration level with stub). Usability: exploratory session on the split UI (D5), no accessibility audit in this release because the UI change is one amount field on an existing page; accessibility of the new field is one exploratory checklist item.

**Techniques by risk level:**

| Risk level | Technique | Applied to |
| :--------- | :-------- | :--------- |
| CRITICAL (R01, R02, R04, R11) | State transition, all transitions, one invalid transition per case; BVA 3-value; decision table for the outcome matrix (charge 1 × charge 2 × refund result) | Payment state machine; split function; sequencing |
| HIGH (R03, R05, R06, R07, R10) | EP each-choice; BVA 2-value; regression against recorded oracle; error guessing on timeouts and retries | Validation API; order status; single-card checkout |
| MEDIUM (R08, R09) | Happy path plus one negative; measurement | Same-card rule; latency |
| LOW | N/A — no LOW rows in the register |

**Decision table for the outcome matrix** (integration level, all 5 feasible rules are cases):

| Condition | Rule 1 | Rule 2 | Rule 3 | Rule 4 | Rule 5 |
| :-------- | :----: | :----: | :----: | :----: | :----: |
| Charge 1 succeeds | T | F | T | T | T |
| Charge 2 succeeds | T | N/A | F | F | timeout |
| Refund of charge 1 succeeds | – | N/A | T | F | – |
| Action: order placed | X | | | | |
| Action: refund issued ≤ 60 s | | | X | attempted | |
| Action: manual-refund alert | | | | X | X |
| Action: customer told order failed | | X | X | X | X |

**Testing quadrants check:** Q1 unit and integration tests in CI (developers). Q2 API cases for rules 1 to 7 and the acceptance walk-through with the Product Owner. Q3 one 90-minute exploratory session on the split UI with the stub (D5) and one on sandbox (D7). Q4 smoke of single-card checkout, amount-tampering security cases, latency measurement. No quadrant is empty.

**Deliverables:** this plan; test cases TC-SPLIT-001 onward (`/qa-cases`); PayGate stub scenarios list; fixture set (below); sandbox-day results pages (D2, D4, D7, D9); defect reports DR-SPLIT-nnn; go/no-go record (D10); completion report with retrospective.

**Entry criteria, system integration level (start of sandbox execution on D4):**

- [ ] Payment service and UI for split merged to main, CI green on the build under test, build identifier recorded.
- [ ] Staging deployed with that build and pointed at PayGate sandbox; feature flag state recorded.
- [ ] Sandbox test cards for success and for each decline code available in the fixture set.
- [ ] Unit and integration tests for the split function and state machine passing in CI (developer sign-off in the ticket).
- [ ] Logs expose charge, decline and refund timestamps so the 60 s window can be measured.
- [ ] `data-testid` on the split amount field, card forms and the result message: N/A if the front-end stack does not use them; otherwise required.

**Entry criteria, component and component integration levels:** code compiles, stub available (D3), the 5 decision-table rules enumerated in the test file names.

**Exit criteria (release decision on D10):**

- [ ] Every release gate case passed on the release candidate build on D9 (sandbox) or, for G6, in CI on the same build.
- [ ] 100% of P0 cases executed and passed; 100% of P1 cases executed and passed or each failure has a recorded Product Owner exception.
- [ ] Zero open Critical defects; zero open High defects without a Product Owner exception.
- [ ] Single-card smoke passes flag off and flag on, on the release candidate.
- [ ] Residual risk for every CRITICAL row recorded in the go/no-go record.
- [ ] Go/no-go signed by the tester and the Product Owner.
- [ ] If the D9 window is lost (R11), the release waits for 2026-11-10 unless the Product Owner records acceptance of releasing on stub evidence only.

**Release gate** (the only cases whose failure blocks the release):

| ID | What it proves | Level / environment | Risk | Result |
| :- | :------------- | :------------------ | :--- | :----- |
| G1 (TC-SPLIT-001) | Odd total split as evenly as the customer asks: card 1 gets the extra cent, both charges captured, sum equals total, order placed | System integration, staging + sandbox | R02 | N/A — not run yet |
| G2 (TC-SPLIT-002) | Card 2 declined: card 1 refunded, refund acknowledged within 60 s (log timestamps), order not placed, customer told | System integration, staging + sandbox | R01 | N/A — not run yet |
| G3 (TC-SPLIT-003) | Card 1 declined: card 2 never charged, no refund attempted, order not placed | System integration, staging + sandbox | R01, R04 | N/A — not run yet |
| G4 (TC-SPLIT-004) | Single-card checkout unchanged against the D2 oracle, flag off and flag on | System integration, staging + sandbox | R03 | N/A — not run yet |
| G5 (TC-SPLIT-005) | Server rejects card 1 amount of 0, total, total + 1, −1, a non-integer, and a pair not summing to total, even when the UI is bypassed | API, staging | R06 | N/A — not run yet |
| G6 (TC-SPLIT-006) | Refund call fails: order marked for manual refund, alert raised, customer told refund is in progress, no second refund on retry | Component integration with stub, CI | R05 | N/A — not run yet |
| G7 (TC-SPLIT-007) | The same checkout submitted twice (double click or retried request with the same idempotency key) produces exactly one charge per card | System integration, staging + sandbox | R04 | N/A — not run yet |

**Execution order** (risk-based by default; sandbox resource window and dependencies override):

1. G6 — runs first, on D3 in CI, because it needs only the stub and is not bound to a sandbox day.
2. G5 — D3, API level on staging; no sandbox needed.
3. G4 (flag off) — first on D4, because the oracle recorded on D2 is the dependency and it protects the 4,000 daily orders.
4. G2 — D4, highest CRITICAL product risk that needs the real gateway.
5. G1 — D4, after G2 because G2 needs a fresh order anyway and G1's data (odd total) is reused for G3.
6. G3 — D4, depends on the odd-total fixture from G1.
7. G7 — D4 if time allows, otherwise D7; it needs sandbox to confirm PayGate saw one charge.
8. G4 (flag on) — D7, after the full feature is in the build.
9. All seven repeated on the release candidate on D9. Cases moved by the resource window: G1, G2, G3, G4, G7 (sandbox only on Tue/Thu).

**Analysis cases (inform, do not gate):** BVA on total = 2 cents (split 1/1), total = 1 cent (no valid split, rejected), large totals near the gateway's per-transaction limit; same card twice (R08); currency rounding display in the UI; latency measurement (R09); exploratory session on the UI; order history and email content after each outcome (R07); back button and session expiry between the two charges (error guessing). If an analysis finding is traced to the change and would stop the release, its case moves into the gate with a dated note here.

**Metrics collected:**

- Gate cases passed / total, per build (test progress).
- Risk coverage: CRITICAL and HIGH rows with at least one executed case, per sandbox day.
- Open defects by severity (defect).
- Sandbox hours used versus the 12 h planned, and tester hours versus the estimate (project and cost).
- Residual risk level of R01, R04, R11 at the go/no-go (risk).

**Control directives, pre-agreed:** if the build is not ready for D4, D4 is used for G5 and the exploratory session on the stub and the gate shifts to D7, with D9 as the only repeat; if that happens, the Product Owner is asked on D4 whether to move the release. If any CRITICAL gate case fails on D7, gateway-facing code is frozen after the fix and D9 runs the full gate again.

**Test data and environment:** staging pointed at PayGate sandbox; the stub for other days. Fixture set (credentials live in the team vault, never here):

| Fixture | Description | State assumed | May be changed | Rebuild |
| :------ | :---------- | :------------ | :------------- | :------ |
| FX-CARD-OK-1, FX-CARD-OK-2 | PayGate sandbox cards that always approve | Active | Read only | From PayGate sandbox docs |
| FX-CARD-DECLINE-INSUFFICIENT, FX-CARD-DECLINE-GENERIC | Sandbox cards for each decline code in the catalogue | Active | Read only | From PayGate sandbox docs |
| FX-ORDER-ODD | Test customer basket with total 10,001 cents | Basket, unpaid | Written by G1 to G3; recreate after each run | Script `seed-split-orders`: N/A — to be written by the developers by D3 |
| FX-ORDER-SINGLE | Basket for single-card oracle, total 4,999 cents | Basket, unpaid | Written by G4 | Same script |
| FX-STUB-SCENARIOS | Stub responses: approve, decline, timeout-after-success, refund-fail | Versioned in the repo | Read only during a run | Git |

**Non-test measures:** feature flag off by default in production (A4); canary rollout of the flag to 5% of customers for 24 h with checkout error rate, p95 checkout time and refund-alert count watched, rollback by switching the flag off; daily reconciliation of PayGate captures and refunds against orders for the first two weeks; code review of the idempotency key and refund retry.

**Deviations from test policy and strategy:** N/A — no written test policy exists in the brief; this plan follows the package's default strategy. The one deliberate deviation from the default pyramid is that no end-to-end suite is automated in this release: with 40 tester hours, the end-to-end share is run manually on sandbox days and automation of G1, G2 and G4 is logged as debt for release 5.4.

## 7. Estimate

**Technique:** three-point estimation (one estimator, margin must be visible). Tester effort in hours, decomposed:

| Task | a | m | b |
| :--- | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Static review of brief, acceptance criteria, test design (cases G1–G7 plus analysis) | 6 | 8 | 12 |
| API cases on staging (G5, tampering, BVA) | 4 | 6 | 10 |
| Sandbox execution, 4 windows × 3 h | 12 | 12 | 12 |
| Exploratory sessions (2) | 3 | 4 | 6 |
| Single-card oracle and regression | 2 | 3 | 5 |
| Reporting, defect reports, go/no-go record | 3 | 4 | 6 |
| **Total** | **30** | **37** | **51** |

E = (30 + 4 × 37 + 51) / 6 = 38.2 h; SD = (51 − 30) / 6 = 3.5 h. **Reported as 38 ± 4 h (between 34 and 42 h)** against 40 h available: no slack for a lost sandbox window or a late build (R11, R12). Developer test effort, estimated the same way: 16 / 20 / 30 h gives 20 ± 2 h across both developers for unit tests, the stub, integration tests and the seed script.

**Assumptions behind the figure:** the stub exists by D3; the build is ready for sandbox on D4; no more than 3 defects of High or above need retest on sandbox; the tester already knows the checkout codebase and PayGate's docs.

## 8. Budget and schedule

Budget: N/A — no monetary budget stated; cost is the 40 tester hours and about 20 developer hours above.

| Day | Date | Sandbox | Tester activity (4 h) | Developer test activity |
| :-- | :--- | :-----: | :-------------------- | :---------------------- |
| D1 | Mon 10-26 | | Three amigos static review; confirm A4, A6, A7, R08; test design starts | Decline-code catalogue; idempotency design |
| D2 | Tue 10-27 | Yes | Record single-card oracle on current build; calibrate sandbox cards and decline codes | Stub skeleton |
| D3 | Wed 10-28 | | Finish cases; G5 and G6 on stub/CI | Unit tests for split; stub scenarios; seed script |
| D4 | Thu 10-29 | Yes | Gate run 1: G4 off, G2, G1, G3, G7 on first build | Fixes |
| D5 | Fri 10-30 | | Exploratory session on stub; defect reports; results page | Integration tests (decision table rules 1–5) |
| D6 | Mon 11-02 | | Analysis cases on stub; retest fixes | Fixes; UI complete |
| D7 | Tue 11-03 | Yes | Gate run 2 (all 7) plus sandbox exploratory; gateway code freeze after this day | Fixes only |
| D8 | Wed 11-04 | | Retest on stub; draft go/no-go | Fixes only |
| D9 | Thu 11-05 | Yes | Gate run 3 on the release candidate; final results page | On call for blockers |
| D10 | Fri 11-06 | | Go/no-go record; release with flag off, canary plan handed to the developers | Release; canary watch |

## 9. Configuration management of testware

- This plan, the test cases, the stub scenarios, the seed script and the results pages are versioned in the repository alongside the feature, under a `qa/split-payment/` folder; the plan ID and version appear at the top of each.
- Every result names the build (commit and CI run) and the environment (staging, PayGate sandbox, feature flag state); a result without them is not accepted into a results page.
- The staging environment used on D4, D7 and D9 is recorded as a baseline (application build, stub version where used, flag values, PayGate sandbox API version) in the results page of that day; changes between windows go through the normal deploy record.
- A previous baseline is restored by redeploying the recorded build; the oracle from D2 is kept with its build identifier so G4 remains reproducible.
- CI holds the unit and integration results per commit; gate case G6 is tagged `@gate @integration @p0 @automated` so its pipeline result is traceable to this plan.
- Corrections to this plan after it is shared are made in place with a dated, attributed note, never by deletion.

# Test Plan: Split Payment (release 5.3)

Plan version 1.0, 2026-10-24. Owner: QA (test management and testing roles both held by the one tester). Status: draft for review by the two developers and the Product Owner on day 1.

## 1. Context of testing

**Scope.** Paying one order with two cards through PayGate: the customer sets the first-card amount, the rest goes on the second card, amounts are integers in cents, an "uneven" split puts the remainder cent on the first card, and a declined second charge triggers an automatic refund of the first charge within 60 seconds. The existing single-card checkout (about 4,000 orders a day) is in scope as the regression target.

**In scope**

| Area | Test levels | Business priority |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Split amount calculation and validation (cents, remainder cent, boundaries) | Component, system | P0 |
| Two-charge orchestration with PayGate (approve, decline, timeout, duplicate protection) | Component integration, system integration | P0 |
| Automatic refund of the first charge on second-charge decline, within 60 s | Component integration, system integration | P0 |
| Order payment state and customer-facing outcome (receipt, error message) | System, acceptance | P1 |
| Single-card checkout regression, feature flag off and on | System | P0 |
| Security hygiene of the new path (card tokens not logged, server-side amount validation) | System | P1 |

**Out of scope** (and why): three or more cards (not in the brief); support-initiated partial refunds and chargebacks (unchanged code); gateways other than PayGate (none in use); load or stress testing of checkout (the feature adds one gateway call per split order, not new traffic; latency is checked, load is not); a full WCAG audit of the new form (a basic keyboard and label check runs inside the exploratory session; a full audit does not fit 40 tester hours and is logged as debt); native mobile apps (assumed web checkout only).

**Objectives.** Show that split orders charge exactly the order total across two cards; show that no customer is left charged without an order; show that single-card checkout is unchanged; give the Product Owner the evidence for a go/no-go on Thursday 5 November 2026.

**Test basis.** The feature brief above; PayGate's API documentation for charge, refund and error codes (assumed available); the existing single-card checkout test suite; the order payment state model (assumed, see item 2). Findings from the static review of the brief are in item 2 under "Ambiguities in the test basis".

## 2. Assumptions and constraints

**Constraints (given)**

- PayGate sandbox is reachable only on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
- Release in 10 working days.
- One tester at half time, plus the two developers building the feature.
- Single-card checkout must keep working at about 4,000 orders a day.

**Assumptions (stated, not confirmed)**

- A01 Today is Saturday 24 October 2026. Day 1 is Monday 26 October; day 10 and the release date is Friday 6 November 2026. Sandbox windows inside the plan: Tue 27 Oct, Thu 29 Oct, Tue 3 Nov, Thu 5 Nov. Four windows, none repeatable.
- A02 The feature ships behind a feature flag, off by default. If no flag is planned, this plan asks for one on day 1: it is the main non-test risk control for R03 and P03.
- A03 One currency with two minor-unit decimals. Zero-decimal currencies are out of scope.
- A04 Charges run sequentially: first card, then second card. The second charge is never attempted if the first is declined.
- A05 The refund of the first charge is a full refund, and "within 60 seconds" is measured from the time our system receives the second-charge decline to the time PayGate acknowledges the refund request.
- A06 PayGate tokenizes cards; no primary account number reaches our servers. Both charges and the refund carry an idempotency key.
- A07 The stack is a web checkout UI over a backend API that calls PayGate over HTTPS; a CI pipeline runs unit and integration tests on every push.
- A08 The developers can provide a deterministic PayGate stub (approve, decline with code, timeout, refund failure) for every day that is not a sandbox day.
- A09 PayGate sandbox offers test cards for approve, decline and timeout outcomes. If it has no timeout card, timeout is tested only on the stub, and that gap is recorded as residual risk.
- A10 Tracker: N/A — none named; the plan uses Jira-style placeholders (ticket PAY-530, cases TC-PAY-NNN, defects DR-PAY-NNN).
- A11 The tester belongs to the same squad as the developers (independence: some). See item 6.

**Ambiguities in the test basis** (raised to the Product Owner on day 1; the plan proceeds under the stated reading)

- The brief says the customer chooses the first-card amount and also that an uneven amount puts the remainder cent on the first card. If the customer enters an exact cent amount, there is never a remainder. Reading adopted: the UI offers a "split evenly" shortcut; on an odd total, the first card takes the extra cent. Manual entry with more than two decimals is rejected.
- Minimum amount per card is not stated. Reading adopted: 1 cent per card, unless PayGate enforces a minimum, which the Tue 27 Oct sandbox session will establish.
- What the customer sees when the refund fails is not stated. Reading adopted: order not paid, customer told to retry, order flagged for manual review, alert raised to operations.

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Who | Responsibility | Relevance to testing |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Product Owner | N/A — not named | Owns acceptance criteria and the go/no-go decision; signs exceptions | Resolves the ambiguities above; attends the Thu 5 Nov acceptance run |
| Developers (2) | N/A — not named | Build the feature, write unit and component integration tests, build the PayGate stub | Hold the testing role at component levels; one reviews the other's module |
| Tester (half time) | N/A — not named | Test management and testing roles; system and system integration tests; this plan, reports, go/no-go record | 40 person-hours total |
| Operations / payments support | N/A — not named | Owns the manual-review queue and the refund alert | Confirms the refund-failure handling is operable |
| PayGate | External | Sandbox and test cards | Availability window fixes the schedule |

## 4. Communication

- Daily stand-up (15 min) with developers; the tester reports gate status, blockers and sandbox readiness.
- A written progress report in the ticket after each sandbox day (Tue 27 Oct, Thu 29 Oct, Tue 3 Nov, Thu 5 Nov): period, progress against this plan, impediments, metrics in item 6, new or re-scored risks, plan for the next period.
- Go/no-go meeting Thu 5 Nov, late afternoon, on the completion report.
- Templates: test cases in TC-PAY-NNN format; defects in DR-PAY-NNN format with severity, steps, expected versus actual, build, environment and flag state; progress and completion reports as described in item 6, every case one row.

## 5. Risk register

| # | ID | Risk Description | Category | L | I | Score | Level | Mitigation Strategy | Owner |

| 1 | R01 | Split arithmetic wrong: the two charges do not sum to the order total, or the remainder cent lands on the second card, or float conversion loses a cent | Product | 3 | 5 | 15 | 🔴 CRITICAL | Pure function for the split, unit-tested with EP, 3-value BVA and a decision table; property check "first + second = total" over random totals; gate cases G01 and G07 | Dev / QA |
| 2 | R02 | Second charge declined and the first charge is not refunded, or refunded after 60 s: customer charged with no order | Product | 3 | 5 | 15 | 🔴 CRITICAL | State transition tests of the order payment model; refund timer asserted in integration test on the stub and measured on sandbox; alert when refund not acknowledged within 60 s; gate case G03 | Dev / QA |
| 3 | R03 | Single-card checkout regresses (shared checkout code or data model changes); 4,000 orders a day exposed | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Feature flag off path tested as the production state; existing checkout regression suite in CI on every build; canary at a small share on release day with rollback by flag; gate case G05 | Dev / QA |
| 4 | R04 | Duplicate charge after a PayGate timeout, a retry, or a double-submitted form | Product | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Idempotency key per charge and per refund; integration test with stub timeout then retry; error guessing session on double submit; gate case G06 | Dev / QA |
| 5 | R05 | Refund request itself fails or times out, leaving a charged customer with no automatic recovery | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Retry with backoff, then order to manual-review queue and operations alert; integration test on stub; verified on sandbox if PayGate can simulate refund failure; gate case G08 | Dev / Ops |
| 6 | R06 | First-card amount validation lets through 0, negative, above total, or more than two decimals; or rejects 1 cent and total minus 1 cent | Product | 3 | 3 | 9 | 🟠 HIGH | 3-value BVA on the amount at both boundaries, client and server side; server-side validation is the one that counts; gate case G07 | QA |
| 7 | R07 | Order state inconsistent with charges: order marked paid after one successful charge, or still pending after both succeeded | Product | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | State transition testing with valid-transitions coverage, plus one invalid transition per case; daily reconciliation report of PayGate charges against orders (non-test measure); gate case G02 | Dev / QA |
