| 9 | R09 | Display and input rounding differs from the cents model (for example an entered 10.005) | Product | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | EP on input formats in the UI; one unit test per rejected format | Dev |
| 10 | R10 | Checkout latency doubles with two sequential gateway calls; customer abandons or retries | Product | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Measure end-to-end time for a split order on sandbox; compare with single-card; accept if within twice the single-card median, else raise | QA |
| 11 | R11 | Customer does not understand which card takes the extra cent or why both cards appear on the receipt | Product | 3 | 2 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Exploratory session with the Product Owner on wording and receipt; usability only, no scripted cases | PO / QA |
| 12 | P01 | PayGate sandbox available only Tue and Thu: four windows in the plan, none repeatable; a lost window cannot be recovered | Project | 4 | 4 | 16 | 🔴 CRITICAL | PayGate stub for all other days; every sandbox day has a pre-agreed script and entry criteria; the Tue 27 Oct window is used for gateway discovery before the feature exists | QA / Dev |
| 13 | P02 | Tester capacity is 40 hours; the estimate in item 7 reaches 48 hours at the top of its range | Project | 4 | 3 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Developers own unit, component integration and the stub automation; the drop list in item 7 is agreed with the Product Owner on day 1 | QA / PO |
| 14 | P03 | Feature not ready for the Thu 29 Oct window, which compresses all gateway testing into Tue 3 Nov and Thu 5 Nov | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Partial entry criteria for Thu 29 Oct (charge and refund orchestration only, no UI); release can ship with the flag off if Thu 5 Nov fails, which is a scope decision for the Product Owner | Dev / PO |
| 15 | P04 | Sandbox behaviour differs from production PayGate (decline codes, refund latency) | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Canary on release day with real low-value orders by the team; post-release sanity checks on production; residual risk recorded in the completion report | QA / Ops |
| 16 | P05 | PayGate sandbox lacks a test card for timeout or refund failure | Project | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Established on Tue 27 Oct; if missing, those paths are proven on the stub only and listed as unmitigated residual risk | QA |

Monitoring: the register is re-read at each progress report; a row is re-scored in place with a dated note when its facts change (for example after the Tue 27 Oct discovery session).

## 6. Test approach

**Test levels, who tests, independence**

| Level | Test object | Who | Independence | Why it fits the risk |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Component | Split function, validation, refund timer, state model | Developers; each developer reviews the other's tests | None, raised to some by cross-review | Fast, cheap, where the arithmetic defects of R01 and R06 are found |
| Component integration | Orchestration against the PayGate stub, idempotency, state transitions | Developers, cases reviewed by the tester | Some | Timeout and retry paths (R04, R05) need deterministic doubles; the stub is the only way to run them daily |
| System and system integration | Checkout UI to backend to PayGate sandbox, flag off and on | Tester | Some (same squad, A11) | A payment feature would merit high independence; not available in this team. Compensated by Product Owner acceptance and by the reconciliation report after release |
| Acceptance | The gate scenarios, run by the Product Owner with the tester on Thu 5 Nov | Product Owner | High relative to the developers | Business validation of the ambiguities resolved in item 2 |

**Test pyramid.** Preset Backend / API: 70% unit, 20% integration, 10% end-to-end. The business logic (split, remainder, refund orchestration, state) lives in the backend; the UI adds one input and one shortcut.

**Testing quadrants.** Q1: unit and component integration tests in CI, developer-owned. Q2: the gate cases below as API and end-to-end tests, plus Gherkin scenarios for the remainder-cent and refund rules written on day 1 to settle the ambiguities. Q3: two exploratory sessions (boundaries and double submit; receipt wording and basic accessibility with the Product Owner) and the Thu 5 Nov acceptance run. Q4: the existing smoke suite on each build, the security checklist (R08), and a latency measurement (R10). Nothing in Q4 covers load: stated out of scope above.

**Techniques by risk.** R01: equivalence partitioning, 3-value boundary value analysis on totals of 1, 2, 3 cents and on even versus odd totals, decision table for the remainder rule (conditions: split evenly or manual; total even or odd). R02 and R07: state transition testing over the order payment states Pending, FirstCharged, Paid, RefundPending, Refunded, RefundFailed, ManualReview, Failed; valid-transitions coverage, one invalid transition per case. R04 and R05: error guessing (timeout then retry, double submit, refund timeout). R06: 3-value BVA on the first-card amount at 0 and at total. R08: checklist-based. R11: exploratory.

**Entry criteria, system-level execution (stub days).** Build merged and green in CI with unit and integration tests; staging deployed with the stub and the flag toggleable per session; fixture set below seeded; split-amount input and submit button carry test identifiers.

**Entry criteria, sandbox days.** All of the above, plus staging pointed at PayGate sandbox with credentials verified by 09:00; the day's script agreed the day before; no deployments to staging during the session except the one planned build. For Thu 29 Oct the partial criterion of P03 applies.

**Exit criteria (release).** Every gate case passed on the release candidate build on Thu 5 Nov, on sandbox; all P0 cases passed; P1 failures each carry a recorded Product Owner exception; zero open Critical or High defects without exception; the single-card smoke suite green with the flag off and on; refund latency measured on sandbox under 60 s on every observed decline; completion report signed by the tester and the Product Owner. If time runs out, the Product Owner accepts the residual risk in writing or the feature ships with the flag off.

**Release gate**

| ID | What it proves | Risk | Technique | Where it runs | Result |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| G01 | Odd-cent total split evenly puts the extra cent on the first card; first + second = total for even, odd, 1-cent and 2-cent totals | R01 | BVA, decision table | Unit in CI; one end-to-end on sandbox | N/A — not yet run |
| G02 | Both charges approved: order Paid, two charge records with the right amounts, receipt shows both cards | R07 | State transition | Sandbox | N/A — not yet run |
| G03 | Second charge declined: first charge refunded automatically, refund acknowledged within 60 s, order not Paid, customer told | R02 | State transition, timing | Stub daily; sandbox Tue 3 Nov and Thu 5 Nov | N/A — not yet run |
| G04 | First charge declined: second charge never attempted, no refund issued, order Failed | R02, R07 | State transition | Stub; sandbox | N/A — not yet run |
| G05 | Single-card checkout unchanged with the flag off and with the flag on (existing smoke suite) | R03 | Regression | CI every build; staging each sandbox day | N/A — not yet run |
| G06 | PayGate timeout on the second charge, then retry: exactly one charge per card, no duplicate | R04 | Error guessing, idempotency | Stub; sandbox only if a timeout card exists (P05) | N/A — not yet run |
| G07 | First-card amount of 0, above total, negative and 10.005 rejected server-side; 1 cent and total minus 1 cent accepted | R06, R01 | 3-value BVA | API test in CI; one end-to-end on stub | N/A — not yet run |
| G08 | Refund failure: retries, then order to ManualReview and operations alert raised; customer not shown a success | R05 | State transition | Stub; sandbox if simulable (P05) | N/A — not yet run |

**Execution order.** Risk-based for the gate, with the sandbox window overriding priority:

1. G01, G07 as unit and API tests, from the first merged build (no gateway needed; cheapest, CRITICAL risk).
2. G05 flag off, on every build (the production state today; must stay green before anything else is believed).
3. G03, G04, G06, G08 on the stub, Fri 30 Oct to Mon 2 Nov (deterministic doubles; proves the paths before spending a sandbox window).
4. G02, G03, G04, G01 end-to-end on sandbox, Tue 3 Nov (resource window; G02 first because G03 depends on a known-good first charge).
5. G06, G08 on sandbox, Tue 3 Nov, only if the Tue 27 Oct discovery found the matching test cards; otherwise recorded as stub-only.
6. G05 flag on, staging, Tue 3 Nov after the gate run.
7. Full gate repeat on the release candidate, Thu 5 Nov, same order as 4 to 6 (confirmation of fixes plus regression).

**Analysis cases, not gating.** Double submit of the split form; same card entered twice; browser back after the first charge; a split where the first amount equals the total (should degrade to single card or be rejected, Product Owner to decide); receipt and email wording; keyboard and label check of the new input; log inspection for tokens; latency comparison. Findings not caused by this change are filed as separate defects and linked, never gating.

**Metrics collected.** Gate cases passed over total, per build. CRITICAL and HIGH risk coverage: register rows with at least one executed case. Open defects by severity. Refund latency on sandbox: every observed value and the maximum. Sandbox windows used over four planned. Tester hours spent against the item 7 estimate.

**Test data: fixture set.** Credentials and sandbox keys stay in the team vault; the plan names only identifiers.

| Fixture | Description | Assumed state | May be changed |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| CARD-OK-A, CARD-OK-B | PayGate sandbox approve cards | Valid | Read only |
| CARD-DECLINE | Sandbox decline card (insufficient funds) | Valid | Read only |
| CARD-TIMEOUT | Sandbox timeout card | Existence confirmed Tue 27 Oct | Read only |
| CARD-REFUND-FAIL | Sandbox card whose refund fails | Existence confirmed Tue 27 Oct | Read only |
| ORD-EVEN, ORD-ODD, ORD-1C, ORD-2C, ORD-MAX | Staging orders with totals 10.00, 10.01, 0.01, 0.02 and 99,999.99 | Pending, unpaid | Written by tests; recreated by seed script after each session |
| FLAG split_payment | Feature flag on staging | Off outside sessions | Toggled per session, state recorded in every result, restored to off |

A case whose fixture is missing or in the wrong state is blocked, not failed. How to rebuild: the seed script owned by the developers; sandbox cards cannot be rebuilt by us.

**Environments.** Developer machines with the stub (dry runs only, never results). CI on every push. Staging with the stub on non-sandbox days and with PayGate sandbox on Tue and Thu. Production canary on Fri 6 Nov at a small share of traffic, flag on, with team-placed low-value orders and the reconciliation report watched; rollback is the flag.

**Non-test measures.** Feature flag with kill switch; daily reconciliation of PayGate charges and refunds against orders; alert on any refund not acknowledged within 60 s; operations runbook for the ManualReview queue.

**Deviations from test policy and strategy.** N/A — no written policy or strategy was provided; this plan follows the package's default.

## 7. Estimate

Technique: three-point estimation, one estimator, decomposed by task. Figures are tester person-hours.

| Task | a | m | b |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Static review of the brief, Gherkin scenarios, this plan's review | 2 | 3 | 5 |
| Fixture set and PayGate discovery session (Tue 27 Oct) | 2 | 3 | 5 |
| Gate automation at API and end-to-end level, with developer support | 6 | 10 | 16 |
| Three sandbox sessions (Thu 29 Oct, Tue 3 Nov, Thu 5 Nov) | 8 | 12 | 16 |
| Single-card regression and flag-off checks | 2 | 4 | 6 |
| Exploratory sessions (two) | 3 | 4 | 8 |
| Defect retests, progress and completion reports, go/no-go record | 3 | 4 | 8 |
| Total | 26 | 40 | 64 |

E = (26 + 4 × 40 + 64) / 6 = 41.7; SD = (64 − 26) / 6 = 6.3. Reported as 42 ± 6 person-hours (36 to 48) against 40 available.

Assumptions: developers deliver the stub by Wed 28 Oct and write all unit and component integration tests (about 40 developer hours, assumed as one quarter of their time); the automation reuses the existing checkout end-to-end framework; no more than two sandbox-day defects need a retest on a later sandbox day. Drop list if the top of the range is reached, in this order and with Product Owner agreement: receipt-wording exploratory session, latency comparison, basic accessibility check. The gate is never dropped.

## 8. Budget and schedule

Budget: N/A — no cost figures given; capacity is the 40 tester hours and the developers' time above.

| Day | Date | Activity |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 1 | Mon 26 Oct | Plan review; ambiguities to Product Owner; Gherkin scenarios; flag confirmed; stub agreed |
| 2 | Tue 27 Oct (sandbox) | PayGate discovery: test cards, decline codes, refund latency baseline, minimum amount; fixture set written |
| 3 | Wed 28 Oct | Developers build; unit tests; stub delivered; tester writes G01 and G07 API tests |
| 4 | Thu 29 Oct (sandbox) | Partial entry criteria: orchestration against sandbox for G02, G03, G04 if built; otherwise discovery continues |
| 5 | Fri 30 Oct | Stub runs of G03, G04, G06, G08; G05 flag off |
| 6 | Mon 2 Nov | Exploratory session 1; defects filed; progress report |
| 7 | Tue 3 Nov (sandbox) | Full gate on sandbox; G05 flag on; latency measured |
| 8 | Wed 4 Nov | Fixes; confirmation tests on stub; exploratory session 2 with Product Owner |
| 9 | Thu 5 Nov (sandbox) | Gate repeat on release candidate; acceptance run; completion report; go/no-go |
| 10 | Fri 6 Nov | Release with flag off, then canary on; team-placed real orders; sanity checks; reconciliation watched |

## 9. Configuration management of testware

- This plan, the Gherkin scenarios, the test cases and the fixture document live in the product repository under version control, with identifiers TC-PAY-NNN and DR-PAY-NNN linked to ticket PAY-530.
- Every recorded result names the build (commit SHA and pipeline run), the environment (CI, staging-stub, staging-sandbox, production-canary), the flag state, and the PayGate sandbox API version read on Tue 27 Oct.
- Staging is baselined at the start of each sandbox session: the deployed build is recorded, and no other deployment happens during the session. A session on a build that failed CI is not started.
- Automated gate cases run in the pipeline and carry a gate tag; stub-only cases are tagged so a sandbox run can be filtered to the cases that need the real gateway.
- Corrections to this plan after sharing are made in place with a dated, attributed note; nothing is deleted.

# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Plan ID | TP-SPLIT-5.3 v1.0 |
| Date | 2026-10-25 |
| Author | QA (test management role and testing role held by the same person, see item 6) |
| Release date | 2026-11-06 (Friday, working day 10; assumed 10 working days counted from Monday 2026-10-26, no public holidays) |
| Board | N/A — no tracker URL given; assumed JIRA epic "Split payment", ticket IDs written as SPLIT-nnn once known |
| Status | Draft for review by the two developers and the product owner on 2026-10-26 |

## 1. Context of Testing

**Scope, in:**

- Split of one order across two cards: customer enters the first-card amount; the second card takes the remainder.
- Cent arithmetic: amounts handled as integer cents; when an amount cannot be split evenly, the extra cent goes on the first card.
- Two charges through PayGate, in order: first card, then second card.
- Automatic refund of the first charge within 60 seconds when the second charge is declined.
- Order state, receipt and confirmation email showing both charges.
- Regression of the existing single-card checkout (about 4,000 orders a day) with the feature flag on and off.
- PayGate integration contract: charge, decline, refund, timeout and error responses.

**Scope, out:**

- More than two cards (not in the brief).
- Partial refunds, returns and chargebacks after the order is placed (unchanged flows; covered only by the single-card regression suite).
- PayGate's own correctness (external system; tested only at its interface).
- Performance testing under production load (no load environment named; see risk R11 for the measure taken instead).
- Accessibility audit of the new amount field: a scanner pass is in the analysis set; a full WCAG audit is deferred to 5.4 and recorded as a residual risk.

**Objectives:**

1. Show that the two charges always sum to the order total and that the remainder cent lands on the first card.
2. Show that a declined second charge leaves the customer with no money taken, within 60 seconds, every time.
3. Show that single-card checkout behaves exactly as in 5.2.
4. Give the product owner a go/no-go record on 2026-11-05 built from results on PayGate's sandbox, not on a stub.

**Test basis:**

- The feature brief above (the only written requirement; assumptions in item 2 fill its gaps and must be confirmed in the 2026-10-26 review).
- PayGate API documentation for charge, refund, decline codes, minimum charge amount and idempotency keys (assumed to exist; to be fetched by Dev A on day 1).
- Existing single-card checkout test cases and automated suite (assumed to exist and pass on the current main build).

## 2. Assumptions and Constraints

**Assumptions (each one is a question for the day-1 review; the plan proceeds as if the answer is "yes"):**

- A1. The feature ships behind a feature flag `split_payment`, off by default, so single-card checkout runs the 5.2 code path when the flag is off.
- A2. The first-card amount must be at least 1 cent and at most total minus 1 cent; anything else is rejected with a validation message before any charge is made. "Cannot be split evenly" refers to the UI's default "split in half" suggestion on an odd total.
- A3. Charges are sequential: the second card is charged only after the first succeeds. If the first is declined, no second charge is attempted and the order is not placed.
- A4. If the refund call itself fails or times out, the order is marked "refund pending", a retry runs, and an alert reaches payments operations. The brief does not say this; the plan treats it as required behavior because the alternative is a customer charged with no order.
- A5. Each charge carries an idempotency key so a retried submission cannot charge a card twice.
- A6. Card data never reaches application logs; only PayGate tokens are stored (existing PCI posture, unchanged).
- A7. The stack is a web checkout (browser UI plus backend payment service); the split arithmetic, orchestration and refund logic live in the backend service.
- A8. The developers build a PayGate stub (fake) that reproduces the sandbox's real responses captured on day 2, so testing is not limited to two days a week.
- A9. A company test card can make a small real charge in production after release and be refunded.

**Constraints:**

- C1. PayGate sandbox available only on Tuesdays and Thursdays: 2026-10-27, 2026-10-29, 2026-11-03, 2026-11-05. Four windows, the last one the day before release.
- C2. One tester at half time: 4 hours a day, 40 hours across the 10 days.
- C3. Two developers build the feature and write component and integration tests; they are not available as additional system testers.
- C4. Single-card checkout must keep working at about 4,000 orders a day.
- C5. No further sandbox window exists between the final gate run (Thursday 2026-11-05) and release (Friday 2026-11-06). A gate failure found on 2026-11-05 cannot be re-verified on the sandbox before release.

## 3. Stakeholders

| Product owner | PO of checkout | Confirms assumptions A1 to A9, owns the go/no-go decision, grants exit-criteria exceptions | Decides on 2026-11-05 from the gate record |
| Tester | QA, half time | Test management role and testing role: this plan, test design, system and system-integration execution, reports | Sole independent tester |
| Developer A | Backend | Payment service, PayGate adapter, refund orchestration, unit and integration tests, PayGate stub | Tests own code at component level; runs the day-2 sandbox capture |
| Developer B | Frontend | Amount field, validation, receipt; component tests | Tests own code at component level |
| Payments operations | Finance / support lead | Receives refund-pending alerts, reconciles PayGate statements | Confirms the refund-failed path (A4) is operable |
| Release manager | N/A — assumed the PO also holds this role | Deploys 5.3, flips the flag | Needs the sanity checklist for release day |

## 6. Test Approach

**Pyramid preset.** Backend / API: 70 percent unit, 20 percent integration, 10 percent end-to-end. The business logic (cent split, charge sequencing, refund, state machine) lives in the backend payment service (A7). The UI contributes one amount field and a receipt, covered by component tests and a small number of end-to-end cases.

**Test levels, who tests, independence:**

**Coverage floors.** Split and state-machine modules: 80 percent branch coverage, read, not chased. Critical path requirements coverage: every objective in item 1 and every CRITICAL and HIGH risk traced to at least one case, 100 percent.

**Testing quadrants check.** Q1: component and integration tests in CI (developers). Q2: gate and analysis cases, BDD scenarios for the three charge outcomes written with `/qa-bdd` on day 1. **Exit criteria (release):**

- [ ] Every release gate case passed on the PayGate sandbox, on the release candidate build, on 2026-11-03 or 2026-11-05.
- [ ] 100 percent of P0 cases and 100 percent of P1 cases passed, or a recorded PO exception per P1 failure.
- [ ] Zero open Critical defects; zero open High defects or a recorded PO exception.
- [ ] Existing single-card regression suite green on the release candidate with the flag off and on.
- [ ] No card data found in logs from any sandbox run.
- [ ] Refund time measured under 60 seconds on every GATE-03 run.
- [ ] Go/no-go record signed by QA and the PO.

Running out of sandbox days ends testing only if the PO reviews and accepts the risk in writing.

**Release gate (built from risk; a failure here blocks):**

| Gate ID | Case | What it proves | Register link | Result |
| :------ | :--- | :------------- | :------------ | :----- |
| GATE-01 | Even split, both approved | Two charges sum to the total; order placed; receipt shows both | R01 | N/A — not yet run |
| GATE-02 | Odd total, default half split | Remainder cent on the first card; sum equals total | R01 | N/A — not yet run |
| GATE-03 | First approved, second declined | First charge refunded automatically, measured under 60 s; order not placed; customer told | R02 | N/A — not yet run |
| GATE-04 | First declined | No second charge attempted; order not placed | R05 | N/A — not yet run |
| GATE-05 | Single-card checkout, flag off and flag on | Behavior identical to 5.2 on the existing regression suite | R03 | N/A — not yet run |
| GATE-06 | First amount at the boundaries: 0, 1, total minus 1, total, total plus 1 | Only 1 to total minus 1 accepted; rejection happens before any charge | R06 | N/A — not yet run |
| GATE-07 | Second declined and refund call times out | Order enters refund pending, retry succeeds, operations alert fired | R07 | N/A — not yet run |
| GATE-08 | Submit twice with the same idempotency key | Exactly one charge per card on the PayGate statement | R04 | N/A — not yet run |

**Execution order for the gate (risk-based, with resource and dependency overrides):**

1. GATE-05 on the stub environment, day 5 (2026-10-30), before anything else: it needs no sandbox and a failure here is the cheapest to find early. Repeated on the release candidate on day 9.
2. GATE-06 on the stub, day 5: validation runs before any charge, so it needs no sandbox; moved ahead of CRITICAL cases for that reason.
3. GATE-01, then GATE-02, on the sandbox on 2026-11-03: GATE-01 first because every other sandbox case depends on an approved first charge working.
4. GATE-03 on the sandbox on 2026-11-03, timed with a stopwatch from the decline response to the refund confirmation in PayGate.
5. GATE-04 on the sandbox on 2026-11-03.
6. GATE-08 on the sandbox on 2026-11-03: needs PayGate's statement to count charges.
7. GATE-07 on the stub on 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-02 (the sandbox cannot be made to time out on demand); re-checked on the sandbox on 2026-11-05 only for the "refund pending" state display, which the sandbox can show.
8. Full re-run of 1 to 6 on the release candidate on 2026-11-05, after confirmation testing of any fixes from 2026-11-03.

**Analysis cases (inform, do not gate):** exploratory session on abandonment and connection loss between charges (R09); same card twice (R13); receipt and email content (R10); latency measurement (R11); minimum charge at 1 cent (R12); log inspection (R08, which moves into the gate if any card data is found, with the date noted here). Findings not caused by this change are logged as their own tickets and linked from the plan.

**Metrics collected:**

| Metric | Decision it informs |
| :----- | :------------------ |
| Gate cases run, passed, failed, blocked, per sandbox day | Whether 2026-11-05 is a confirmation run or a first run |
| Open defects by severity | Exit criteria, PO exceptions |
| Risk coverage: CRITICAL and HIGH risks with at least one executed case | Whether residual risk is known or unknown |
| Refund time on each GATE-03 run, in seconds | Pass or fail on R02; representativeness (P05) |
| Tester hours used against the estimate in item 7 | Whether to drop analysis cases or ask for help |

**Test data and environment requirements (fixture set):**

| Record | Description | State assumed | May be changed | Rebuild |
| :----- | :---------- | :------------ | :------------- | :------ |
| FX-CARD-OK-1, FX-CARD-OK-2 | PayGate sandbox test cards that approve | Active | Read only | From PayGate sandbox docs |
| FX-CARD-DECLINE | Sandbox card that declines every charge | Active | Read only | From PayGate sandbox docs |
| FX-CARD-DECLINE-2ND | Card or amount pattern that declines only above a threshold, used as second card | Active | Read only | From PayGate sandbox docs; if none exists, use FX-CARD-DECLINE as the second card |
| FX-ORDER-EVEN | Cart totalling 10000 cents | Unpaid | Written by tests; reset after each run | Seed script, Dev A |
| FX-ORDER-ODD | Cart totalling 10001 cents | Unpaid | Written by tests; reset after each run | Seed script, Dev A |
| FX-ORDER-MIN | Cart totalling 2 cents | Unpaid | Written by tests | Seed script |
| FX-STUB-CATALOGUE | Recorded sandbox responses, versioned | Matches 2026-10-27 captures | Changed only by Dev A with a version bump | Re-capture on a sandbox day |
| Sandbox credentials | Location: team secret store | N/A — not recorded here | Off limits | PayGate account owner |

Environments: staging with stub (every day), staging pointed at the PayGate sandbox (Tuesdays and Thursdays), production for the post-release sanity. Each result names the build identifier and which PayGate target was in use.

**Deviations from the test policy and strategy:** two. The release gate is run on the sandbox only twice instead of on every candidate build, because of C1. The PO acceptance is a demo on the sandbox rather than a separate UAT cycle, because of C2.

## 7. Estimate

Technique: three-point estimation for the tester, since there is one estimator and no history for a two-card flow. Developer test effort by ratio against their build effort.

Tester effort, decomposed:

| Task | a | m | b |
| :--- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Assumption review, BDD scenarios, test cases, fixture set | 5 | 7 | 10 |
| Day-2 sandbox capture with Dev A, stub review | 2 | 3 | 5 |
| Review of developer unit and integration tests | 2 | 3 | 5 |
| Stub-based system run and regression (days 5 and 6) | 5 | 7 | 10 |
| Sandbox gate runs (2026-11-03 and 2026-11-05) | 6 | 8 | 12 |
| Exploratory session, log inspection | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| Defect reports, confirmation testing | 1 | 3 | 6 |
| Daily notes, go/no-go record, completion report | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| Total (hours) | 25 | 37 | 56 |

E = (25 + 4 × 37 + 56) / 6 = 38 hours. SD = (56 − 25) / 6 = 5 hours. Reported as 38 ± 5 hours, between 33 and 43 hours, against 40 hours available. The pessimistic case exceeds availability; item 8 says what is dropped first.

Developer test effort: ratio of 2 development hours to 1 test hour, assumed from similar payment work. With two developers at 8 days of build each, that is roughly 40 to 55 hours of component, integration and stub work. Assumptions: the stub takes under a day; no third rework cycle; the existing regression suite runs in CI without manual effort.

## 8. Budget and Schedule

Budget: N/A — no monetary budget given; effort in item 7 is the budget. No new tooling is needed; the PayGate stub is built in-house.

| Day | Date | Sandbox | Activity |
| :-- | :--- | :------ | :------- |
| 1 | Mon 2026-10-26 | No | Assumption review; BDD scenarios; stub interface agreed; PayGate minimum amount and refund SLA checked |
| 2 | Tue 2026-10-27 | Yes | Capture real responses: approve, declines, refund, refund latency. These become the stub catalogue and the oracle |
| 3 | Wed 2026-10-28 | No | Developers build; tester writes gate and analysis cases, fixture seed script reviewed |
| 4 | Thu 2026-10-29 | Yes | Contract test of the PayGate adapter against the sandbox, even if the feature is incomplete |
| 5 | Fri 2026-10-30 | No | Entry criteria checked. GATE-05, GATE-06, GATE-07 on the stub |
| 6 | Mon 2026-11-02 | No | Remaining gate cases rehearsed on the stub; regression suite; exploratory session |
| 7 | Tue 2026-11-03 | Yes | First full gate run on the sandbox, release candidate build RC1. Defects filed same day |
| 8 | Wed 2026-11-04 | No | Fixes; confirmation on the stub; RC2 built |
| 9 | Thu 2026-11-05 | Yes | Confirmation and full gate re-run on the sandbox against RC2. Go/no-go record to the PO by end of day |
| 10 | Fri 2026-11-06 | No | Release with flag off; flag on in production; sanity charge-and-refund with the company test card (A9); logs checked |

**Contingencies, decided in advance:**

- If entry criteria are missed on day 5, 2026-11-03 becomes the first and only full gate run and the PO is told that day that release carries one sandbox run instead of two.
- If any gate case fails on 2026-11-05 and cannot be confirmed on the sandbox before release, the options are to ship 5.3 with the flag off and enable it after a sandbox confirmation on Tuesday 2026-11-10, or to slip the release. The plan recommends shipping with the flag off: single-card checkout is protected (R03) and the feature waits two working days.
- If tester hours reach the pessimistic estimate, the analysis cases for R10, R11 and R13 are dropped first and recorded as not run with a resume point.

## 9. Configuration Management of Testware

- This plan, the BDD scenarios, the test cases, the stub catalogue and the seed script are versioned in the repository alongside the feature, under a `qa/split-payment` folder, each with an identifier and version. Corrections to shared documents are made in place with a dated note, never deleted.
- Every result names the build identifier (commit and pipeline run), the environment, the flag state and the PayGate target (stub catalogue version or sandbox). A result without these is not accepted as evidence.
- The staging environment used for the gate is a baseline: application build, flag configuration, stub catalogue version and PayGate sandbox account. It changes only through the normal deploy pipeline, and the deploy record is the source of truth for what ran, not the branch name.
- The stub catalogue is itself a configuration item: re-captured only on a sandbox day, version bumped, and the version recorded in every stub-based result so a later reader knows which real responses it reflected.
- Earlier baselines (RC1 of 2026-11-03) remain deployable so a disputed result can be reproduced.
- CI runs component, integration and the existing regression suite on every push; the sandbox runs are manual and their evidence (screenshots, PayGate statement export, refund timing) is attached to the test cases in the tracker.

# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

**Document ID:** TP-SPLIT-5.3 · **Version:** 1.0 · **Date:** 2026-10-25 · **Author:** QA (test management and testing roles) · **Status:** Draft for review

## 1. Context of Testing

**Scope, in:**

- Split of one order across two cards: first-card amount chosen by the customer, remainder on the second card, integer cents, remainder cent to the first card.
- Two sequential PayGate charges and the automatic refund of the first charge when the second is declined, within 60 seconds.
- Order, receipt and payment-record consistency after a split payment (paid, refunded, failed).
- Server-side validation of the split amounts and protection against client-side tampering.
- Regression of the existing single-card checkout (about 4,000 orders a day).

**Scope, out:**

- More than two cards, saved-card wallets, instalments, or splitting across non-card methods: not in the brief.
- Refund of a *completed* split order after the fact (customer-service refunds): existing behavior, covered only by one regression check that a split order can still be refunded manually.
- Load and soak testing of PayGate: the sandbox is shared and time-boxed; a latency check on the two-call sequence replaces it (see item 6, Q4).
- Chargebacks, disputes and PayGate's reporting portal: outside the team's control.

**Objectives:**

1. Show that no customer can be left charged without an order, or charged twice, for any combination of PayGate outcomes on the two charges.
2. Show that the split arithmetic is exact in cents for all boundaries, including the remainder-cent rule.
3. Show that the single-card checkout behaves exactly as before the change.
4. Give the release decision on 2026-11-06 a written record of what passed, what did not run, and what risk remains.

**Test basis:** the feature brief above; PayGate API documentation (charge, refund, idempotency key, sandbox test cards and decline codes); the existing single-card checkout test cases and automated suite; the order payment state model in the codebase; PCI DSS SAQ scope the team already operates under.

## 2. Assumptions and Constraints

**Assumptions** (each one stated because the brief does not settle it):

- A1. Today is Sunday 2026-10-25. The ten working days are 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-06, and the release is Friday 2026-11-06.
- A2. The PayGate sandbox windows inside that period are Tue 2026-10-27, Thu 2026-10-29, Tue 2026-11-03 and Thu 2026-11-05. "Available on Tuesdays and Thursdays" means the full working day.
- A3. The split arithmetic rule means: the customer may enter an exact first-card amount, or choose a proportional split (for example "half and half"); when a proportional split yields a fractional cent, the extra cent goes to the first card. If the UI offers only an exact amount, the remainder-cent cases become unit tests of the shared rounding helper and the proportional gate case is marked `N/A`.
- A4. Split payment ships behind a feature flag. Flag off is the production state until the release decision, and is the rollback.
- A5. Charges are sequential: card 1 first, then card 2. A declined card 1 means card 2 is never attempted.
- A6. The backend calls PayGate with an idempotency key per charge, and PayGate's sandbox supports forcing a decline, a timeout and a refund failure through documented test cards or amounts. If it does not, risk R16 becomes an issue and the stub carries those paths.
- A7. The existing single-card checkout has an automated regression suite that runs in CI against a PayGate stub, plus a live sandbox smoke. If it does not, the first sandbox window includes recording responses to build one.
- A8. Orders are single-currency, two-decimal. Minimum order total is 0.01; maximum is the checkout's existing maximum (assumed 999,999.99). Minimum charge per card is PayGate's minimum (assumed 0.01).
- A9. The test environment is a staging deployment of the checkout that can target PayGate sandbox or a local PayGate stub by configuration.
- A10. Developers own component and component integration tests and pay for them out of their own build time; the tester's half-time is spent on design, system-level execution, defect handling and reporting.

**Constraints:**

- C1. Live gateway behavior can be observed only on four days. Anything not proven on 2026-11-05 cannot be proven live before release.
- C2. One tester at half time: about 40 hours in total, roughly 4 hours per working day.
- C3. The release date is fixed by the brief; scope and the flag state are the variables, not the date.
- C4. The single-card flow must not regress; 4,000 orders a day means a defect reaches thousands of customers before a rollback.

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Who (assumed) | Responsibility | Relevance to testing |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Product Owner | PO for checkout | Accepts the feature, owns exceptions to exit criteria, decides go/no-go | Runs acceptance cases on 2026-11-05; signs the completion report |
| Developers (2) | Feature pair | Build the feature, write unit and integration tests, build the PayGate stub, fix defects | Hold the testing role at component and component integration level |
| Tester (1, half time) | QA | Test management role (this plan, monitoring, reporting) and testing role at system level | Designs cases, runs sandbox sessions, files defects, writes reports |
| PayGate integration contact | Vendor support | Confirms sandbox test cards, decline codes, refund latency | Needed before the first sandbox window; blocks R16 if silent |
| Payments operations / Finance | Reconciliation owner | Reconciles charges and refunds against orders | Reviews the refund-failure path and the ledger output of split orders |
| Customer support lead | Support | Receives customer complaints after release | Reviews the customer-facing messages for a declined second card |

## 4. Communication

| Form | Frequency | Content | Template |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Stand-up | Daily, 10 min | Blockers, which sandbox cases are queued for the next window | N/A — verbal |
| Progress report | End of each sandbox day (10-27, 10-29, 11-03, 11-05) | Gate table with results per build, defects by severity, risk changes, next window's queue | Progress report, `qa-reference` test-reporting |
| Defect reports | As found | DR-SPLIT-NNN with severity, steps, build, flag state, PayGate request IDs | `/qa-defect` |
| Register review | At each progress report | Re-scored rows with dated notes | This document, item 5 |
| Completion report | 2026-11-05 evening, updated 11-06 if a fix lands | Every case one per row, "Not run — resume point", residual risks | Completion report, `qa-reference` test-reporting |
| Go/no-go record | 2026-11-06 morning | Evidence per gate case and exit criterion, exceptions, open defects | `/qa-release` |
| Retrospective | Within 5 working days after release | What to keep, what to change, actions with owners | Retrospective, `qa-reference` test-reporting |

Channel for all of the above: the team chat channel for release 5.3 and the tracker epic for split payment (assumed to exist; the plan links to it once the ID is known).

## 5. Risk Register

Scale: Likelihood 1–5, Impact 1–5, Score = L × I. Levels: 15–25 CRITICAL, 8–14 HIGH, 4–7 MEDIUM, 1–3 LOW.

| # | ID | Risk Description | Category | L | I | Score | Level | Mitigation Strategy | Owner |
| :-- | :-- | :--- | :--- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | R01 | Second charge declined and the first charge is not refunded, or is refunded after 60 s: customer pays with no order | Product | 3 | 5 | 15 | 🔴 CRITICAL | State transition tests on the payment state machine (integration, stub); gate case G03 live on sandbox with timing captured from PayGate timestamps; refund-failure path alerts ops (G03b in analysis set) | Dev / QA |
| 2 | R02 | Split arithmetic wrong: cents do not sum to the total, remainder cent on the wrong card, float rounding | Product | 3 | 5 | 15 | 🔴 CRITICAL | 3-value BVA and EP unit tests on the integer-cent helper; property test that card1 + card2 = total for random totals; gate cases G01, G02 | Dev |
| 3 | R03 | Single-card checkout regresses (4,000 orders/day) | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Feature flag (A4) with flag-off tested as today's behavior; existing automated regression on every build; gate case G06 live on sandbox; post-release sanity | Dev / QA |
| 4 | R04 | Duplicate charge on retry after a PayGate timeout or on double-submit | Product | 3 | 5 | 15 | 🔴 CRITICAL | Idempotency key per charge verified in integration tests with a stub that times out then succeeds; gate case G05 live; code review of retry logic | Dev / QA |
| 5 | R05 | First card declined but second card is still charged, or order left half-paid | Product | 2 | 4 | 8 | 🟠 HIGH | Decision table rule 4 at integration level; gate case G04 live | Dev / QA |
| 6 | R06 | Amount validation gaps: first-card amount 0, equal to total, above total, negative, fractional cent, below PayGate minimum, same card twice | Product | 4 | 3 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | EP and 2-value BVA cases at unit and API level; gate case G07 for the overcharge boundary; the rest in the analysis set | Dev / QA |
| 7 | R07 | Refund call fails or is asynchronous at PayGate, so the 60 s target is missed or the refund is silently lost | Product | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Confirm refund semantics with PayGate contact before 10-27; retry with backoff and an ops alert; analysis case measuring refund latency over 10 runs on sandbox | Dev / Ops |
| 8 | R08 | Customer closes the browser or double-submits between charge 1 and charge 2, leaving a partial state | Product | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Server-side orchestration independent of the client session; integration test that kills the client mid-flow; exploratory charter on sandbox day 3 | Dev / QA |
| 9 | R09 | Receipt, order history or ledger shows one charge, wrong amounts, or a refund not linked to the order; reconciliation breaks | Product | 3 | 3 | 9 | 🟠 HIGH | Analysis cases checking receipt, order record and ledger export after G01, G02, G03; Finance reviews one real sandbox export | QA / Finance |
| 10 | R10 | Client can tamper with the first-card amount or the total; two card tokens widen PCI exposure | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Server recomputes card-2 amount from the stored order total; gate case G08 sends a tampered request via API; security checklist (tokens never logged, no PAN in requests) | Dev / QA |
| 11 | R11 | Two sequential gateway calls double checkout latency; timeouts tuned for one call fire on the second | Product | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Timing captured on every sandbox gate run; timeout values reviewed; no load test (out of scope, see item 6) | Dev |
| 12 | R12 | Flag-off path differs from pre-change behavior because shared checkout code was refactored | Product | 2 | 4 | 8 | 🟠 HIGH | Impact analysis of the diff on shared modules; regression suite run with flag off on every build | Dev / QA |
| 13 | R13 | Sandbox available only on 4 days: a window lost to a broken build or an unready feature removes 25% of live test time | Project | 4 | 4 | 16 | 🔴 CRITICAL | Window 1 used for a gateway spike that needs no feature build; stub built from window-1 recordings for all other days; a queue of sandbox cases prepared the day before each window; control directive in item 6 for fixes landing after 11-05 | QA |
| 14 | R14 | Tester half-time capacity (about 40 h) is below the pessimistic estimate (44 h) | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Developers own all unit and integration execution; analysis set ordered by risk so the tail can be dropped with a recorded exception; PO pre-agrees the drop list | QA / PO |
| 15 | R15 | Feature not "Ready for QA" before window 2 (10-29), leaving two live windows for gate, fixes and retest | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Entry criteria relaxed for window 2 to "deployed behind flag, happy path works"; devs commit to a 10-28 deploy; otherwise the schedule shifts to the contingency in item 8 | Dev lead |
| 16 | R16 | Sandbox cannot force a decline, timeout or refund failure, so R01 and R04 cannot be proven live | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Ask the PayGate contact on 10-26; verify on window 1; if unsupported, those paths are proven on the stub and the register records the residual risk as accepted by the PO | QA / PO |
| 17 | R17 | No PayGate stub exists, so nothing gateway-related can run on 6 of the 10 days | Project | 3 | 3 | 9 | 🟠 HIGH | Devs build a stub on 10-26 and 10-27 from PayGate docs and window-1 recordings; contract check of stub against recordings | Dev |

Risk control: each sandbox-day progress report re-scores rows whose facts changed, with a dated note; a risk that becomes an issue reprioritizes the next window's queue.

## 6. Test Approach

**Where the logic lives:** in the backend orchestration and arithmetic, with a thin checkout UI. Preset: **Backend / API: 70% Unit · 20% Integration · 10% E2E.** The sandbox constraint reinforces this: everything that can be proven below system level is, so the four live windows are spent only on what needs the real gateway.

### Test levels, who tests, and independence

| Level | Test object | Techniques | Who tests | Independence | Why that degree |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Component | Cent-split helper, amount validator, idempotency key builder | 3-value BVA, EP, property test (sum invariant), branch coverage ≥ 80% on the helper and orchestrator | Author developer, peer-reviewed by the other developer | None, raised to Some by review | Arithmetic defects are cheap to find here and the developers know the code; QA reviews the BVA table so the boundaries are not the author's own guess |
| Component integration | Orchestrator with PayGate stub: charge 1 → charge 2 → refund, timeouts, retries, client disconnect | Decision table (below), state transition (valid transitions, plus invalid ones attempted one per case), error guessing on timeouts | Developers write and run; QA reviews the decision table and state table for completeness | Some | The interaction defects (R01, R04, R05) show here first; QA's review of the tables is the independent view, since QA cannot spend hours in the integration suite |
| System and system integration | Deployed checkout against PayGate sandbox (Tue/Thu) and stub (other days) | Gate cases, API cases (tampering, boundaries), exploratory charters | Tester | Some (same team, not the author) | A higher degree is not available with this staffing; the money risk is offset by the PO acceptance step and by Finance reviewing the ledger output |
| Acceptance | Gate cases G01 and G03 on sandbox, customer-facing messages | Checklist of acceptance criteria | Product Owner, with Support lead reviewing messages | Business representative | Validates that a declined second card is explained in a way the customer accepts |

### Decision table for charge outcomes (integration level, every feasible column exercised)

| Condition / Action | Rule 1 | Rule 2 | Rule 3 | Rule 4 | Rule 5 | Rule 6 |
| :--- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Charge 1 result | OK | OK | OK | Declined | OK | Timeout |
| Charge 2 result | OK | Declined | Declined | N/A | Timeout | N/A |
| Refund of charge 1 result | – | OK ≤ 60 s | Fails | – | – | – |
| Order placed and paid | X | | | | | |
| Charge 2 attempted | X | X | X | | X | |
| Charge 1 refunded, customer told | | X | | | X after status query shows no charge 2 | |
| Order in "refund pending", ops alerted | | | X | | | |
| No duplicate charge after retry | | | | | X | X |
| Customer sees decline, nothing charged | | | | X | | X |

### Testing quadrants check

- **Q1** (technology, supports the team): unit and integration tests above, in CI on every push, flag on and flag off.
- **Q2** (business, supports the team): gate and analysis cases TC-SPLIT-NNN, API cases for tampering and boundaries, acceptance checklist.
- **Q3** (business, critiques the product): one 60-minute exploratory charter per sandbox window 3 and 4 ("abandon and retry between the two charges"; "what does the customer see and receive by email when card 2 declines"); PO acceptance on 11-05.
- **Q4** (technology, critiques the product): smoke suite per build; security checklist (tokens, logging, tampering); latency of the two-call sequence recorded on every sandbox gate run. No load test: the sandbox is shared and time-boxed, and the change adds one gateway call per order rather than new throughput. Residual risk is R11, MEDIUM, accepted.

### Deliverables

Test cases TC-SPLIT-NNN (gate and analysis, tagged), fixture set, PayGate stub recordings, defect reports DR-SPLIT-NNN, four progress reports, completion report, go/no-go record, retrospective actions.

### Entry criteria

| Level | Entry criteria |
| :--- | :--- |
| Component and integration | Helper and orchestrator merged to main behind the flag; stub available; CI green |
| System, sandbox window 2 (10-29) | Feature deployed to staging behind the flag; happy path works on the stub; sandbox decline codes confirmed; fixture set seeded; `data-testid` on the split form fields |
| System, windows 3 and 4 | Full "Ready for QA" state; build identified by commit and pipeline run; all CI suites green on that build, flag on and off |
| Acceptance | Gate cases G01 to G08 passed at least once on sandbox; customer messages final |

### Exit criteria (measured against the release gate)

- Every gate case passed on the release candidate build on sandbox, on 2026-11-05 or later.
- 100% of P0 analysis cases executed and passing; P1 failures each have a recorded PO exception.
- Zero open Critical defects; zero open High defects or a PO exception each.
- Single-card regression suite green with the flag off and with the flag on, on the release candidate.
- Residual risks (R07 timing, R16 if unsupported, R11) recorded in the completion report and accepted in the go/no-go record.
- Completion report signed by the tester and the PO.

If time runs out, testing stops only when the PO has reviewed the "Not run — resume point" list and accepted the risk of releasing without it, in writing in the go/no-go record.

### Release gate

| ID | What it proves | Risk | Needs | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| G01 | Even split (10.00 → 5.00 / 5.00): both charges succeed, order paid, receipt and ledger show both | R02, R09 | Sandbox | N/A — not yet run |
| G02 | Odd-cent split (10.01 → 5.01 / 5.00): remainder cent on card 1, sum equals total | R02 | Sandbox | N/A — not yet run |
| G03 | Card 2 declined: card 1 refunded within 60 s (PayGate timestamps), order not placed, customer told | R01, R07 | Sandbox with decline card | N/A — not yet run |
| G04 | Card 1 declined: card 2 never charged, order not placed | R05 | Sandbox with decline card | N/A — not yet run |
| G05 | Charge 2 times out then retries: exactly one charge on card 2, no duplicate | R04 | Sandbox with timeout card, or stub if R16 is an issue | N/A — not yet run |
| G06 | Single-card checkout, flag on and flag off, unchanged end to end | R03, R12 | Stub in CI plus one live sandbox run | N/A — not yet run |
| G07 | First-card amount above the total, or second card below 0.01, is rejected server-side with no charge | R06 | Stub (API), confirmed once on sandbox | N/A — not yet run |
| G08 | Tampered request (client sends card-2 amount lower than remainder) is rejected; server recomputes from the stored total | R10 | Stub (API) | N/A — not yet run |

Findings not caused by this change are logged as their own defects and linked here; they do not gate. If an analysis finding proves to be caused by the change, its case moves into this table with a dated note.

### Execution order (risk-based, with overrides)

1. **G06 on stub, flag off** first on every build, before anything else: largest blast radius, and no sandbox needed. Resource override: it runs daily rather than waiting for a window.
2. **G01** at the start of each sandbox window: dependency override, since every other live case needs a working happy path to prove the environment and build.
3. **G03** (R01, score 15).
4. **G02** (R02, score 15).
5. **G05** (R04, score 15). Runs after G03 because the timeout card, if PayGate provides one, may leave a pending charge the tester must clear before the next cases.
6. **G08** then **G07** (R10, R06): stub on any day, one confirmation on sandbox.
7. **G04** (R05, score 8).
8. **G06 live** on sandbox, last in each window, so a gateway hiccup late in the day cannot block the critical cases above.
9. **Analysis cases** in register order, stub first, sandbox-only ones queued for the next window; the tail (R09 ledger detail, R11 latency) is the pre-agreed drop list under R14.

### Metrics to collect

- Gate cases passed / failed / not run per build and per window (answers: can we release?).
- Open defects by severity, daily (answers: do we need a fix window before 11-05?).
- Risk coverage: register rows with at least one executed case, per window (answers: what is still unproven live?).
- Sandbox utilization: hours used of 16 available (answers: is R13 becoming an issue?).
- Effort spent against the estimate in item 7, weekly (answers: does R14 trigger the drop list?).

**Control directive, recorded in advance:** a fix that changes gateway-facing code after the 2026-11-05 window cannot be verified live before 11-06. Either it ships with the flag off and is verified on Tue 2026-11-10, or the release of the split feature moves to 2026-11-10. The PO decides at go/no-go.

### Test data and environment

Fixture set (document kept with the cases; no credentials, pointer to the team vault):

| Record | State assumed | May be changed? | Rebuild |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| PayGate sandbox merchant account | Active, refunds enabled | Read only; charges are writes, voided at end of each window | Vendor contact; nobody on the team can |
| Sandbox test cards: success, decline, timeout, refund-fail | As documented by PayGate, verified on 10-27 | Read only | From PayGate docs |
| Orders O-001 (10.00), O-002 (10.01), O-003 (0.01), O-004 (0.02), O-005 (maximum total), O-006 (single-card baseline) | Unpaid, in staging catalogue | Written to by tests; reset by seed script after each window | Seed script in the repo |
| Flag `split_payment` | Off by default; on for split cases | Set per case and recorded in its precondition | Flag service |
| PayGate stub recordings from 10-27 | Versioned in the repo with the recording date | Read only | Re-record on the next window |

Environment: staging deployment, build identified by commit SHA and pipeline run; PayGate sandbox API version recorded in each result; stub version recorded when used.

**Deviations from test policy and strategy:** N/A — no organizational test policy or strategy was provided; this plan stands alone.

## 7. Estimate

Technique: **three-point estimation** (one estimator, margin of error required). E = (a + 4m + b) / 6, SD = (b − a) / 6, in tester hours.

| Task | a | m | b | E | SD |
| :--- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Static review of brief, test design (BVA table, decision table, state table, gate and analysis cases, fixture set) | 6 | 8 | 12 | 8.3 | 1.0 |
| Sandbox execution, 4 windows (gate runs, exploratory charters, timing capture) | 10 | 14 | 18 | 14.0 | 1.3 |
| Stub-based execution on non-sandbox days (API cases, regression runs, retests) | 4 | 6 | 10 | 6.3 | 1.0 |
| Single-card regression review and live run | 3 | 4 | 6 | 4.2 | 0.5 |
| Defect reports, retests, progress and completion reports, go/no-go record | 4 | 6 | 10 | 6.3 | 1.0 |
| **Total** | | | | **39 h** | **± 5 h** (SDs summed, conservative) |

Reported as **39 ± 5 tester hours (between 34 and 44)**, against about 40 hours available. The pessimistic end exceeds capacity, which is risk R14 and why the drop list exists.

Developer test effort, same technique, both developers combined: unit and integration tests plus stub, a = 12, m = 16, b = 24, giving **17 ± 2 hours (15 to 19)**.

Assumptions behind the figures: A2 (four full sandbox days), A6 (decline and timeout can be forced), A7 (a regression suite exists), A10 (developers own levels below system). If A6 fails, subtract about 3 sandbox hours and add 2 stub hours; if A7 fails, add 6 to 8 tester hours and the estimate no longer fits.

## 8. Budget and Schedule

Budget: N/A — no monetary budget was given; the effort in item 7 stands in for it. No tool purchase is needed.

| Day | Date | Sandbox | Tester (about 4 h) | Developers |
| :-- | :-- | :-: | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Mon 10-26 | | Static review of the brief, ask PayGate contact about decline, timeout and refund semantics, start test design, fixture set | Build cent helper and validator with unit tests; start stub |
| 2 | Tue 10-27 | ✓ | **Window 1: gateway spike.** Verify test cards, refund latency, timeout behavior, idempotency on sandbox; record responses for the stub | Finish stub from recordings; orchestrator |
| 3 | Wed 10-28 | | Finish cases; review developers' BVA and decision tables; G06 on stub flag off | Integration tests; deploy to staging behind flag |
| 4 | Thu 10-29 | ✓ | **Window 2:** G01 to G06 on first build (relaxed entry); file defects | Fix on the spot where possible |
| 5 | Fri 10-30 | | Progress report review, retests on stub, G07 and G08 via API | Fixes; CI green flag on and off |
| 6 | Mon 11-02 | | Analysis cases on stub; prepare window-3 queue | Fixes; code review of retry logic |
| 7 | Tue 11-03 | ✓ | **Window 3:** full gate on release candidate 1, exploratory charter 1, latency capture | Fixes |
| 8 | Wed 11-04 | | Retests on stub, ledger review with Finance, completion report draft | Final fixes; RC2 tagged by end of day |
| 9 | Thu 11-05 | ✓ | **Window 4:** full gate on RC2, exploratory charter 2, PO acceptance of G01 and G03, completion report | Standby; no gateway-facing changes after this day |
| 10 | Fri 11-06 | | Go/no-go record; release with flag off, then flag on; post-release sanity with the company test card on production, voided (assumed allowed) | Release; monitor refund alerts and error rate |

Contingency: if R15 occurs and window 2 is lost, windows 3 and 4 carry the first and final gate runs with no live retest between them; the PO is told on 10-29 that a Critical defect found on 11-03 means either a flag-off release or a slip to 11-10.

## 9. Configuration Management of Testware

- This plan, the test cases, the fixture set, the stub and its recordings, and the reports live in the repository under the release 5.3 QA folder, versioned with the code; each is a configuration item with an ID (TP-SPLIT-5.3, TC-SPLIT-NNN, DR-SPLIT-NNN, FX-SPLIT-001, STUB-PAYGATE-<recording date>).
- Every result names the build (commit SHA and pipeline run), the environment (staging), the gateway (sandbox API version or stub recording date) and the flag state. A result without all four is not recorded.
- The staging environment with RC2 deployed, the sandbox merchant configuration and the flag values form the baseline for the release decision; changes after 2026-11-05 go through the control directive in item 6.
- Previous baselines (RC1) remain tagged so a result from window 3 can be reproduced.
- CI runs the unit, integration and regression suites on every push and records the run against the commit; the stub recordings are checked in and selected by date, never "the latest".
- Corrections to this plan after it is shared are made in place with a dated, attributed note; nothing is deleted.

# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

| Field | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Plan ID / version | TP-SPLIT-5.3, v1.0, 2026-10-25 |
| Owner | Tester (test management role and testing role, one person) |
| Board | N/A — no tracker URL given; assumed Jira project PAY, epic PAY-530 |
| Release date | 2026-11-06 (Friday), 10 working days from 2026-10-26 |
| Environments | Local, Dev (PayGate simulator), Staging (PayGate sandbox on Tue/Thu; simulator otherwise), Production |

## 1. Context of Testing

**Test basis.** The feature brief for Split payment, decomposed into these requirements. The brief is the only source given; the IDs below are this plan's.

| Req | Statement |
| :--- | :--- |
| REQ-01 | A customer pays one order with two cards. |
| REQ-02 | The customer chooses the amount on card 1; card 2 takes the rest. |
| REQ-03 | Amounts are integers in cents. |
| REQ-04 | When the total cannot be split evenly, the remainder cent goes on card 1. |
| REQ-05 | Both charges go through PayGate. |
| REQ-06 | If the second charge is declined, the first charge is refunded automatically within 60 seconds. |
| REQ-07 | The existing single-card checkout keeps working (about 4,000 orders a day). |

**Objectives.**

- Show that a split order charges exactly the order total across the two cards, with the remainder cent on card 1.
- Show that a decline on card 2 leaves the customer with no net charge within 60 seconds.
- Show that single-card checkout behaves as before, with the feature flag on and off.
- Give the go/no-go decision a written record of what passed, what did not run, and the risks still open.

**In scope.**

| Area | Test levels | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Split amount entry, validation, even-split control (REQ-02, REQ-03, REQ-04) | Component, system | P0 |
| Charge orchestration: card 1 then card 2, decline paths, timeout paths, idempotency (REQ-05, REQ-06) | Component integration, system integration | P0 |
| Automatic refund on card 2 decline, timed (REQ-06) | System integration | P0 |
| Server-side recomputation of card 2 amount; tampering via API | System (API) | P0 |
| Order state, receipt and order history showing two charges | System | P1 |
| Single-card checkout regression, flag on and flag off (REQ-07) | System, CI regression | P0 |
| Exploratory testing of the checkout UI with a split | System | P2 |

**Out of scope, and why.**

- Three or more cards: not in the brief.
- Saved cards, new payment methods, PayGate contract or API version changes: not changed by this release.
- Partial refunds issued later by support: existing behavior, not changed.
- Load or performance testing beyond timing the refund: no load environment, and 4,000 orders a day is within current capacity.
- Full accessibility audit: a half-time tester cannot fit it; a keyboard-only pass of the split form is part of exploratory session 1.
- Reconciliation and settlement reports in finance systems: verified by finance ops as acceptance, not by this plan's cases.

## 2. Assumptions and Constraints

**Constraints (given).**

- PayGate sandbox is available only on Tuesdays and Thursdays: 2026-10-27, 2026-10-29, 2026-11-03, 2026-11-05. Four windows in total.
- Release on 2026-11-06.
- One tester at half time, 40 hours over the 10 days, plus two developers who build the feature.
- Single-card checkout must keep working.

**Assumptions (stated where the brief is silent).**

| ID | Assumption |
| :--- | :--- |
| A1 | Working days run Monday 2026-10-26 to Friday 2026-11-06; the release goes out on day 10. |
| A2 | The stack is a web checkout front end with a backend payment service that calls PayGate over a REST API. The split arithmetic and the refund orchestration live in the backend. |
| A3 | Outside sandbox days, PayGate is replaced by a local HTTP simulator owned by the developers, with scenarios selected by amount or by test card number. |
| A4 | The feature ships behind a feature flag, off by default in production, so release and enablement are separate decisions. |
| A5 | The amount on card 1 must be at least 1 cent and at most total minus 1 cent; anything else is a validation error. The UI also offers an "split evenly" control; for an odd total it puts the extra cent on card 1. |
| A6 | The 60 seconds are measured from PayGate's decline response on card 2 to PayGate's acceptance of the refund request, not to settlement. |
| A7 | Card 1 is charged first. If card 1 is declined, card 2 is never charged and the order is not placed. |
| A8 | Single currency; no currency conversion. |
| A9 | Tracker is Jira; test cases are TC-SPLIT-NNN and TC-SINGLE-RNN; defects are DR-SPLIT-NNN. |
| A10 | An automated regression suite for single-card checkout exists in CI. Verified on day 1; if false, risk R19 applies. |
| A11 | A timeout or unknown result on card 2 is resolved by a status query to PayGate before any refund is decided. The product owner confirms this on day 1. |
| A12 | Both charges and the refund carry idempotency keys so a retry cannot charge or refund twice. |
| A13 | PayGate sandbox offers test cards for approve, decline and, if available, timeout and refund failure. Confirmed on 2026-10-27. |
| A14 | The PayGate sandbox merchant account is shared with other teams. |
| A15 | Production verification after release uses a company card and a low-value order that is refunded afterwards, under an existing procedure. |

## 3. Stakeholders

| Product owner | N/A — name not given | Confirms A5, A6, A11; accepts the feature; signs exceptions | Decides P1 exceptions and the go/no-go |

**Where does the business logic live?** In the backend payment service: split arithmetic, orchestration, refund. The UI holds one amount field and a control. Preset: **Backend / API: 70% unit, 20% integration, 10% E2E.** The E2E share is small on purpose because every E2E run against real PayGate costs a sandbox window.

| Quadrant | What this plan puts there |
| :--- | :--- |
| Q1 technology facing, supports the team | Unit tests on the split calculator and validation; component integration tests on the orchestration against the simulator; all in CI |
| Q2 business facing, supports the team | Gherkin scenarios for the seven requirements as acceptance criteria; API tests on the checkout endpoint; the release gate cases |
| Q3 business facing, critiques the product | Two exploratory sessions; product owner and finance ops acceptance on 2026-11-03 |
| Q4 technology facing, critiques the product | CI smoke on single-card checkout; security checks (tampered amount, tokenization path); refund timing measured against 60 s. No load test: see out of scope |

| Level | Test object | Techniques | Who tests | Independence | Why this degree |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| System (API and UI) | Checkout on staging, simulator | API tests with tampered bodies; BVA at the UI; exploratory sessions | Tester | Some (same squad, not the author) | The tester is in the squad, so independence is "some"; it is enough because PayGate's sandbox gives an external oracle for the money paths |
| System integration | Checkout on staging against PayGate sandbox | Gate cases, timed refund, record comparison with PayGate dashboard | Tester, with Dev A present on sandbox days | Some | Dev A present shortens the fix loop inside a four-hour window; the tester runs and records |
| Acceptance | Split order end to end on sandbox | Walkthrough of the Gherkin scenarios | Product owner, finance ops | High (outside the development team) | Finance ops judge reconciliation, which nobody in the squad can |

### Test types

Functional at every level. Non-functional: security (R11) and the 60-second refund timing (reliability and performance of one path). No usability lab, no load test, no compatibility matrix; one browser (assumed Chrome stable) plus the keyboard pass in exploratory session 1.

### Deliverables

- This plan, versioned.
- Gherkin scenarios for REQ-01 to REQ-07 (`/qa-bdd`), 2026-10-28.
- Test cases TC-SPLIT-001 to about 030 and TC-SINGLE-R01 to R06 (`/qa-cases`), 2026-10-28.
- Fixture set document (below), first version 2026-10-27.
- Four progress reports, one go/no-go record, one completion report.
- Defect reports as found.

### Entry criteria

| Level | Entry |
| :--- | :--- |
| Component and component integration | Simulator stubs updated from real sandbox responses recorded on 2026-10-27; state table reviewed by the tester |
| System and system integration | Feature on staging with flag on, state "Ready for QA" in Jira, CI green on that build including the single-card regression suite, by 2026-10-30 end of day; sandbox test cards listed in the fixture set; `data-testid` attributes on the amount field, even-split control, submit button and error message |
| Acceptance | Gate cases G1 to G4 passed on sandbox on 2026-11-03 |

### Exit criteria

| Level | Exit |
| :--- | :--- |
| Component and component integration | Branch coverage ≥ 80% on calculator and orchestration; every decision table column and every transition in the state table has a passing test in CI |
| System and system integration | Every gate case passed on sandbox on the release candidate build; 100% of P0 cases run and passed; 100% of P1 passed or each failure has a recorded product owner exception; zero open Critical or High defects without exception; refund latency ≤ 60 s on every timed run |
| Acceptance | Product owner and finance ops sign the go/no-go record |
| Release | Single-card regression suite green on the release build; post-release sanity on production passed |

Time running out ends testing only if the product owner records acceptance of the risk of going live without further testing (CTFL §5.1.3). The contingency written here is to release with the flag off.

### Release gate

Result column is filled per build; `Pending` until run.

| ID | What it proves | Level and environment | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TC-SPLIT-001 | Custom split, both approved: two PayGate charges summing to the total, order placed, receipt shows both | System integration, sandbox | Pending — build not yet available |
| TC-SPLIT-002 | Even split of an odd total puts the remainder cent on card 1 (unit test in CI plus one sandbox order of 10.01) | Component in CI, then sandbox | Pending — build not yet available |
| TC-SPLIT-003 | Card 2 declined: card 1 refunded, PayGate accepts the refund within 60 s, order not placed, customer told | System integration, sandbox, timed | Pending — build not yet available |
| TC-SPLIT-004 | Card 1 declined: card 2 never charged, order not placed | System integration, sandbox | Pending — build not yet available |
| TC-SPLIT-005 | Tampered card 2 amount in the API body is rejected; server recomputes from the total | System (API), simulator | Pending — build not yet available |
| TC-SPLIT-006 | Timeout on card 2 then retry: exactly one charge per card, idempotency holds | Component integration with simulator; sandbox only if PayGate can time out | Pending — build not yet available |
| TC-SINGLE-R01 | Single-card checkout unchanged with flag off and with flag on, on staging | System, sandbox | Pending — build not yet available |
| TC-SINGLE-R02 | CI single-card regression suite green on the release build | CI regression | Pending — build not yet available |

A failed gate case blocks the release. Findings outside the gate inform; one that turns out to be caused by this change moves into the gate with a dated note. Findings not caused by this change get their own ticket and never gate 5.3.

**Execution order.** The gate uses risk-based ordering; the sandbox window overrides it where noted.

1. TC-SINGLE-R02, on every push from day 1: CI, no window needed, and it must be green before any staging session starts.
2. TC-SPLIT-002 unit part and TC-SPLIT-006, from 2026-10-28 on the simulator: no sandbox needed, and they catch R02 and R03 before a window is spent.
3. TC-SPLIT-005, 2026-10-30 on the simulator: API only.
4. TC-SPLIT-001, first in the 2026-11-03 window: TC-SPLIT-003 depends on a successful charge on card 1, so the happy path runs first despite R01 outranking it.
5. TC-SPLIT-003, same window, timed with a stopwatch and the PayGate dashboard timestamp.
6. TC-SPLIT-004, same window.
7. TC-SPLIT-002 sandbox part, same window, order of 10.01.
8. TC-SINGLE-R01, end of the same window: flag toggled last so it does not disturb the split runs.
9. Full gate re-run on the release candidate in the 2026-11-05 window, same order.

Analysis cases outside the gate run requirements-based, REQ-06 first, then REQ-04, REQ-02, on the simulator from 2026-10-30, and as sandbox time allows.

### Metrics

| Metric | Decision it supports |
| :--- | :--- |
| Gate cases passed / 8, per build and environment | Go/no-go |
| Risk coverage: CRITICAL and HIGH rows with at least one executed case | Whether a sandbox window must be re-prioritized |
| Maximum refund latency over all timed runs, in seconds | Pass/fail of REQ-06 |
| Open defects by severity, with age | Exceptions needed |
| Sandbox windows used / 4, and cases blocked for lack of sandbox | Whether to ask PayGate for an extra window or fall back to flag off |
| Tester hours used / 40, against the estimate in item 7 | Whether developers take over simulator runs |

**Pre-agreed control directives.** Entry deadline missed on 2026-10-30: release 5.3 with the flag off and plan split for 5.3.1. Sandbox outage on 2026-11-03: request an extra window; if refused, run the gate on the simulator, mark sandbox cases blocked, and the go/no-go decides with the flag off. Refund latency above 60 s on any run: defect at Critical, re-run in the next window only after a fix.

### Test data and environment

**Fixture set** (first written 2026-10-27, kept in the repo next to the cases).

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| FX-CARD-DECL | Sandbox decline card | Always declines | Read only | From PayGate documentation |
| FX-CARD-TIMEOUT, FX-CARD-REFUNDFAIL | Sandbox timeout and refund-failure cards | N/A — availability confirmed 2026-10-27 | Read only | N/A — PayGate decides |
| FX-SIM-* | Simulator scenarios keyed by amount: ending .98 declines card 2, .97 times out, .96 fails the refund | As listed | Developers only, versioned | From stub files in the repo |
| FX-CUST-QA53 | Staging customer account for split orders | Empty cart at start and end | Write, restore cart | Re-create via admin |
| FX-SKU-ODD, FX-SKU-EVEN, FX-SKU-MIN, FX-SKU-MAX | Products priced 10.01, 10.00, 0.02, 9,999.99 | Available, in stock | Read only | Seed script |
| Sandbox merchant account | Shared with other teams (A14) | N/A — shared state | Write only orders prefixed QA53-; never touch others' transactions | N/A — nobody can |
| Staging feature flag | split_payment_enabled | On, except during TC-SINGLE-R01 | Write, announce in chat, restore to On | Flag admin |

A case whose fixture is missing or in the wrong state is blocked, not failed.

**Environment.** Staging must record build (commit and pipeline run), simulator stub version, flag state and, on sandbox days, PayGate API version and the date of the window. Developer and tester machines are dry runs; results are recorded only from staging and CI.

### Deviations from policy and strategy

- Sandbox E2E cases are manual this release; automating against a resource available two days a week would spend the windows on tooling. Logged as debt for 5.4.
- No accessibility audit; keyboard pass only. Reason: tester capacity.
- The release gate contains two regression cases instead of a full regression run on staging, because the CI suite carries the rest.
- Independence at system level is "some" rather than "high"; there is no tester outside the squad.

## 7. Estimate

Technique: three-point estimation, one estimator, no history for a two-card flow.

| Who | a (optimistic) | m (likely) | b (pessimistic) | E | SD | Range |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Tester | 32 h | 44 h | 68 h | 46 h | 6 h | 40 to 52 h |
| Developers, test work only, both together | 16 h | 24 h | 40 h | 25 h | 4 h | 21 to 29 h |

Tester decomposition at the likely value: planning and static review 4 h, Gherkin and cases 7 h, four sandbox sessions 16 h, API and simulator runs 6 h, two exploratory sessions 4 h, defect reports and progress reports 4 h, go/no-go and completion 3 h.

**Assumptions behind the figure.** The feature reaches staging by 2026-10-30; the simulator exists on day 1; sandbox is up on all four days; at most two Critical defects are found. The available 40 hours sit at the low end of the range, so the plan already moves simulator runs and the gate dry run to the developers; if more than two Critical defects appear, the shortfall becomes the control directive "release with flag off". Re-estimate after 2026-10-29.

## 8. Budget and Schedule

**Budget.** Tester 40 h, developers about 25 h of test work inside their build time. PayGate sandbox and the simulator are assumed free. No tool purchase.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 2 | Tue 2026-10-27, sandbox 1 | Record real PayGate responses on current single-card checkout: approve, decline, refund, timeout if possible; list test cards; write fixture set; update simulator stubs | Tester, Dev A |

| 7 | Tue 2026-11-03, sandbox 3 | Full gate run on sandbox, refund timed; finance ops and product owner acceptance; progress report | Tester, Dev A, PO, Finance |
| 8 | Wed 2026-11-04 | Fixes; confirmation on simulator; exploratory session 2 (retry after decline, double submit) | Tester, developers |
| 9 | Thu 2026-11-05, sandbox 4 | Gate re-run on the release candidate; go/no-go meeting end of day | Tester, all |
| 10 | Fri 2026-11-06 | Release with flag off, canary of flag on at 5% if go; production sanity per A15; completion report | Release manager, Tester |

## 9. Configuration Management of Testware

- This plan, the Gherkin scenarios, test cases, fixture set, simulator stubs and reports live in the product repository under a docs/qa/5.3 folder, version controlled with the code; each has an identifier and a version, and this plan is TP-SPLIT-5.3 v1.0.
- Every case traces to a REQ-NN and to a register row; every result names the build (commit and CI run), the environment, the flag state, the simulator stub version or the sandbox window date.

- CI records unit, integration and regression results per commit automatically; sandbox results are recorded by hand in the results page, one case per row, with a "Not run — resume point" section.
- Corrections to any shared document are made in place with a dated note, never by deletion.
