# Test Plan: Split Payment (release 5.3)

| Field | Value |
| :-- | :-- |
| Project / version | Checkout, release 5.3, feature "Split payment" |
| Plan owner | Tester (holds the test management role and the testing role) |
| Plan date | 2026-10-25 |
| Release date | 2026-11-06 (working day 10; day 1 is Monday 2026-10-26) |
| Board URL | N/A — not provided; placeholder ticket ID `SPLIT-53` is used below |
| Tech stack | N/A — not provided; assumed a web checkout backed by a payment service that calls PayGate over HTTPS |
| Environments | Local, CI, Staging (connected to PayGate sandbox on Tuesdays and Thursdays), Production |

## 1. Context of testing

**Scope, in:**

- Split rules: customer-entered amount for card 1, remainder to card 2; integer cents; the "split evenly" option puts the odd cent on card 1.
- Two sequential PayGate charges, and automatic refund of charge 1 within 60 s when charge 2 is declined.
- Failure handling around PayGate: declines, errors, timeouts, duplicate submissions, process crash between the two charges.
- Order, receipt and ledger records for a split order and for a refunded split attempt.
- Regression of the existing single-card checkout (about 4,000 orders a day).
- Existing post-purchase refund flow applied to a split order (analysis only, see R09).

**Scope, out:** more than two cards; mixing a card with vouchers or wallets; 3-D Secure flows (assumed handled by PayGate unchanged); currencies without 100 minor units; native mobile apps; a PCI audit; load testing of PayGate; a full accessibility audit (a keyboard-only check of the new field is included in the exploratory session).

**Objectives:**

1. Show the split arithmetic is correct to the cent for every partition and boundary, and that the two charges always sum to the order total.
2. Show the charge-2-declined path refunds charge 1 automatically, every time, within 60 s, and that no path leaves money taken without an order.
3. Show the single-card checkout behaves exactly as before, with the feature flag off and on.
4. Give the Product Owner a go/no-go record on 2026-11-06 built from results obtained against the real PayGate sandbox.

**Test basis:** the feature brief above; the PayGate API documentation (version N/A — not provided; to be pinned on day 1); the existing single-card checkout test suite; the assumptions in item 2 until the Product Owner confirms or corrects them.

## 2. Assumptions and constraints

Assumptions (each one is a question for the Product Owner on day 1; testing proceeds on the stated value until answered):

- A1. One currency with 100 minor units. Amounts travel as integer cents from the browser to PayGate; no floating point on the path.
- A2. The UI offers both "enter amount for card 1" and "split evenly". The remainder-cent rule applies to "split evenly" and to any server-side rounding.
- A3. Each card must carry at least 1 cent; an amount of 0 or of the full total is rejected as "not a split". PayGate's own minimum charge, if higher, replaces 1 cent.
- A4. Card 1 is charged first. If card 1 is declined, card 2 is never charged and nothing is refunded.
- A5. "Declined" for charge 2 covers an explicit decline, a PayGate error, and a timeout whose status query returns "not charged". A status still unknown after the retry budget is treated as declined and charge 1 is refunded.
- A6. The 60 s is measured from the application receiving the decline of charge 2 to PayGate acknowledging the refund request, read from application logs.
- A7. The feature ships behind a feature flag, off in production until the go decision. The off state must equal today's behaviour.
- A8. Card data is tokenised by PayGate hosted fields; no card number touches the application.
- A9. Feature-complete build on Staging by Monday 2026-11-02 (day 6); partial builds are deployable earlier.
- A10. A working day is 8 h; half time is 40 h over the ten days, and the tester may concentrate hours on sandbox days.
- A11. An automated single-card checkout smoke suite exists and runs in CI. If it does not, TC-CHK-001 below becomes a manual run of the five main single-card scenarios and R03 is re-scored.
- A12. Both developers are full time on this feature.

Constraints: PayGate sandbox reachable only on 2026-10-27, 10-29, 11-03 and 11-05 (four windows, none on release day); one half-time tester; ten working days; no history of similar work for estimation.

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Who | Responsibility | Relevance to testing |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Product Owner | N/A — name not provided | Confirms assumptions A1 to A9, grants P1 exceptions, makes the go/no-go decision | Receives the gate evidence; witnesses TC-SPLIT-003 on 2026-11-05 |
| Developers (2) | N/A — names not provided | Build the feature, unit and component integration tests, the PayGate recorded fake, fixes | Hold the testing role at component and component integration level |
| Tester | N/A — name not provided | This plan, test design, system and system integration execution, reports, go/no-go record | Test management role and testing role |
| Finance / reconciliation | N/A — assumed to exist | Confirms a split order and a refunded attempt reconcile in the ledger | Acceptance check of TC-SPLIT-008 evidence |
| Support / on-call | N/A — assumed to exist | Receives refund-failure alerts in production | Confirms the alert from TC-SPLIT-007 reaches them |
| PayGate support | N/A — contact not provided | Sandbox test cards, decline and timeout simulation, API version | Needed on day 1 for R12 |

## 4. Communication

- **Daily stand-up**: test status in one line, blockers named.
- **Progress report** at the end of each sandbox day (10-27, 10-29, 11-03, 11-05) and on 10-30, in the tracker, using the progress report content of CTFL §5.3.2: period, progress against this plan, impediments, metrics from item 6, new or re-scored risks, next period.
- **Defect reports**: one `DR-SPLIT-NNN` per finding, filed the same day it is found, linked from the progress report.
- **Go/no-go meeting**: 2026-11-06, 09:00, Product Owner, both developers, tester. Input: the completion report with every case on one row and the "Not run — resume point" section.
- **Templates**: test cases `TC-SPLIT-NNN` and `TC-CHK-NNN`; defect reports `DR-SPLIT-NNN`; completion report in the row format of the reporting reference.

## 5. Risk register

| 12 | R12 | Only four sandbox windows; a build that misses a window loses two days of real-gateway testing, and no window exists on release day | Project | 4 | 4 | 16 | 🔴 CRITICAL | Record real PayGate responses on 10-27 and build a fake from them for the other days; each window has a named case list; a PayGate-touching fix after 11-05 means no-go or ship with flag off | QA/PO |

| 14 | R14 | Tester capacity (40 h) is below the pessimistic estimate (61 h) | Project | 3 | 3 | 9 | 🟠 HIGH | Risk-based order; developers run the unit and fake-based levels; pre-agreed drop list in item 7 | QA/PO |

Register reviewed at every progress report; re-scores recorded as dated notes, never overwritten.

## 6. Test approach

**Pyramid preset:** Backend / API (70% unit, 20% integration, 10% end-to-end). The business logic (split arithmetic, validation, charge and refund state machine) lives in the payment service, not in the UI.

**Quadrant check:** Q1 unit and component integration tests in CI (developers). Q2 API cases and the gate cases, written as `TC-SPLIT-NNN` from the acceptance criteria. Q3 one exploratory session on the split UI on 2026-11-03 (charter: amount field, even-split option, error messages, keyboard-only use, two browsers) and the Product Owner and finance acceptance checks. Q4 smoke suite, security checks (R05, R06), reliability and time behaviour (R01, R02, R07), and a light performance check (R03). Usability lab and compatibility matrix are not in Q3/Q4: the UI change is one field and one option, and the two-browser exploratory session is the accepted coverage.

**Levels, who tests, independence:**

| Level | Test object | Who tests | Degree | Why it fits |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Component | Split calculator, validators, state machine | Author, reviewed by the other developer | Some | Logic is exhaustively testable here and cheap; tester reviews the case list against the BVA and decision-table items below |
| Component integration | Payment service + PayGate recorded fake, order and ledger writers | Developers; tester pairs on failure scenarios | Some | Needs code-level control of timeouts, crashes and retries that the sandbox cannot inject |
| System and system integration | Staging + PayGate sandbox, UI and API | Tester | Some (same delivery team) | A high degree is not available with one tester in the team; compensated by the Product Owner witnessing TC-SPLIT-003 and finance checking the ledger |
| Acceptance | Gate evidence, ledger of one split order and one refunded attempt | Product Owner, finance | Some | Validates the business need (money correct, customer never left charged) |

**Types:** functional (all levels); non-functional: time behaviour (refund ≤ 60 s, timeout budgets), reliability (crash and retry), security (tampering, idempotency), performance efficiency (single-card p95 unchanged on Staging); usability through the exploratory session only.

**Techniques and coverage items:**

- Equivalence partitioning and 2-value BVA on card 1 amount for total T: 0, 1, T−1, T (A3), plus T+1, negative, non-integer, comma decimal, empty; totals T = 1, 2, 3 (even split gives 2/1), 1001 (even split gives 501/500), and a large value near the gateway maximum. Coverage: every partition and boundary item exercised, at unit level, with one API negative run on Staging.
- Decision table on charge-2 outcome (approved, declined, error, timeout) × status query result (charged, not charged, unknown) → actions (mark paid, refund charge 1, alert). Every feasible column exercised; infeasible columns deleted and listed.
- State transition testing of the order attempt (Created → Charge1Authorised → Paid; Charge1Authorised → Charge2Declined → RefundRequested → Refunded; RefundRequested → RefundFailed → alerted; Charge1Declined → Failed). Criterion: all transitions, invalid ones attempted one per case (R11), because the object is money.
- Error guessing: double submit, back button after charge 1, process killed between the charges, same card for both halves, refund arriving before the decline is persisted.
- Exploratory testing: one 90-minute session, charter above.
- Checklist-based: receipt, e-mail, order detail, ledger, each showing two charges with the right amounts.

**Coverage floors:** 100% of register rows R01 to R11 with at least one executed case; branch coverage of the split calculator and state machine 80% or higher (read the uncovered branches, do not chase the number).

**Deliverables:** this plan; `TC-SPLIT-001` to about `TC-SPLIT-030` and `TC-CHK-001`; the PayGate recorded fake with its recording date; five progress reports; defect reports; the completion report; the go/no-go record.

**Entry criteria, component and component integration:** test basis item and ticket in "In development"; fake recorded from the 2026-10-27 window; CI green on the branch.

**Entry criteria, system and system integration:** ticket "Ready for QA"; build deployed to Staging with commit SHA and deployment ID recorded; CI green for that SHA; flag state recorded; sandbox test cards and credentials available in the secrets store; it is a Tuesday or Thursday.

**Exit criteria, component and component integration:** all BVA, decision-table and all-transitions items have a test; branch floor met or deviations read and accepted by the tester.

**Exit criteria, system level and release:** every gate case passed on a sandbox day against the release candidate SHA; 100% P0 cases passed; 100% P1 cases passed or each failure holds a recorded Product Owner exception; zero open Critical, zero open High without exception; single-card smoke green with flag off and on; refund timing max ≤ 60 s over at least 10 sandbox runs; completion report signed by tester and Product Owner. Stopping for lack of time is allowed only with the Product Owner's recorded acceptance of the named residual risks.

**Release gate** (failure of any row stops the release):

| ID | What it proves | Where | Technique | Result |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| TC-SPLIT-001 | Manual split, both approved: order paid, two PayGate charges whose amounts sum to the total | Staging + sandbox | EP | N/A — not yet run |

| TC-SPLIT-004 | Charge 1 declined: charge 2 never attempted, no refund, order not paid | Staging + sandbox | State transition | N/A — not yet run |
| TC-SPLIT-005 | Card 1 amount of 0, T, T+1, negative and non-integer rejected by the server with a clear message | Staging API | BVA | N/A — not yet run |

Execution order of the gate (risk-based, with overrides):

1. TC-CHK-001 flag off, on day 8 (Wednesday 2026-11-04): needs no sandbox, so it leaves the windows for the others.
2. TC-SPLIT-001 on the sandbox day, before TC-SPLIT-003 although it ranks lower: 003 depends on a working charge-1 path.
3. TC-SPLIT-003, ten repetitions, timings recorded.
4. TC-SPLIT-004.
5. TC-SPLIT-002.
6. TC-SPLIT-007: the fake part runs in CI any day; the alert check runs on Staging the same sandbox day.
7. TC-SPLIT-005 and TC-SPLIT-006: API-only, run at the end of the window or on the fake if the window closes.
8. TC-CHK-001 flag on, on the release candidate, 2026-11-05.

Analysis cases (inform, do not gate): timeout-then-charged and timeout-then-not-charged (R02), double submit (R05), crash between charges (R01), concurrent retry during pending refund (R11), receipt, e-mail and ledger checks (R08), post-purchase refund of a split order (R09, TC-SPLIT-010), same card twice, large totals, the exploratory session. A finding here moves into the gate only when it is caused by the change, with a dated note.

**Metrics collected:** gate cases passed / 8; register rows with an executed case / 15; cases planned vs executed per sandbox window; open defects by severity; refund timing max and p95 over the sandbox runs; tester hours spent against the estimate.

**Control directives agreed in advance:** if the feature-complete build misses 2026-11-02, the 2026-11-03 window runs the gate on the partial build and 2026-11-05 becomes the only full run (R15). If a fix after 2026-11-05 touches any PayGate call, the Product Owner chooses no-go or release with the flag off (R12). If hours exceed 36 by day 8, the drop list in item 7 applies.

**Test data (fixture set):** sandbox test cards for approve, decline, insufficient funds and, if PayGate provides them, timeout and refund failure (credentials in the team secrets store, never in testware); one test customer; orders with totals 1, 2, 3, 1001 and 10000 cents, writable by tests and rebuilt from a seed script; the recorded PayGate fake, read-only, dated with its recording window; ledger entries for the finance check, read-only once created. A missing fixture blocks a case; it does not fail it.

**Environment:** Staging with the release candidate SHA, its deployment ID, flag state, PayGate sandbox API version and the fake version recorded on every result. Local runs are dry runs and produce no results.

**Deviations from test policy and strategy:** N/A — no written policy or strategy was provided; the one deviation from this package's default is that component integration results obtained on the fake count as evidence on non-sandbox days, while system integration results count only from sandbox days.

## 7. Estimate

Technique: three-point estimation, one estimator, no history for ratios. Tester effort in person-hours, decomposed:

| Task | a | m | b | E |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| Test analysis and design (cases, decision table, state table, charter) | 4 | 6 | 9 | 6.2 |
| Recording the fake with the developers, reviewing unit cases | 2 | 4 | 8 | 4.3 |
| Sandbox execution over four windows, including timing runs | 12 | 18 | 28 | 18.7 |
| Single-card regression, latency comparison, flag off and on | 3 | 4 | 7 | 4.3 |
| Defect reports, retests, progress and completion reports, go/no-go record | 3 | 5 | 9 | 5.3 |
| **Total** | **24** | **37** | **61** | **38.8** |

Reported as 39 ± 6 person-hours (between 33 and 45) against 40 available. The pessimistic case does not fit. Drop list, in order, if hours run out: the exploratory session, receipt and e-mail checks (ledger stays), TC-SPLIT-010, large-total cases. Developer test effort is assumed at 16 to 24 person-hours for unit tests and the fake (A12).

# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

| Field | Value |
| :-- | :-- |
| Plan ID / version | TP-SPLIT-5.3 v1.0, 2026-10-25 |
| Owner | Tester (test management role and testing role; see item 6) |
| Release date | Friday 2026-11-06 (10 working days from Monday 2026-10-26) |
| PayGate sandbox windows | Tue 2026-10-27, Thu 2026-10-29, Tue 2026-11-03, Thu 2026-11-05 |
| Board | N/A — tracker not named in the brief; assumed JIRA, ticket key SPLIT-5.3, all IDs below are relative to it |

## 1. Context of testing

**Scope.** Release 5.3 adds split payment: one order paid with two cards, the customer sets the first-card amount, the second card carries the rest. Amounts are integers in cents. On an even split of an odd total, the extra cent goes on the first card. Both charges go through PayGate. If the second charge is declined, the first charge is refunded automatically within 60 seconds.

**In scope**

- Split amount entry and validation (custom amount and even split), in the checkout UI and in the API.
- Orchestration of the two PayGate charges and the order outcome for every combination of charge results.
- Automatic refund of the first charge when the second is declined, including the 60-second limit and the failure path of the refund itself.
- Idempotency of the checkout submission (no duplicate charges on retry, double-click or reload).
- Regression of the existing single-card checkout (about 4,000 orders a day), with the feature flag off and on.
- Security of the amount handling (server-side authority over amounts, no card data in logs).
- A latency check of the two-charge flow against the current single-card checkout.

**Out of scope**

- PayGate's own correctness and availability (external; covered by its contract and by R15).
- Refund behaviour on the customer's bank statement timing (outside the system; only the PayGate refund acknowledgement is checked).
- Three or more cards, saved-card wallets, gift cards, currencies without a minor unit (not in the brief; assumed not built).
- Full load testing of checkout (no tool or environment for it in 10 days; latency is measured, not load-tested; recorded as a deviation in item 6).

**Objectives**

1. Show that money is split and charged exactly as the brief states, to the cent, in every outcome combination.
2. Show that a customer is never left charged without an order, and never charged twice.
3. Show that the single-card checkout behaves exactly as before the change.
4. Give the Product Owner a release gate record from a sandbox-verified build before 2026-11-06.

**Test basis.** The feature brief above; PayGate API documentation (charge, decline codes, refund, idempotency key); the existing single-card checkout test suite; the decision table and state model in item 6, which the team reviews on day 1 as the agreed reading of the brief.

## 2. Assumptions and constraints

Assumptions (each stated because the brief is silent; any one proven wrong re-scores the register):

- **A1.** Stack is a web front end over a backend API; the split arithmetic, charge orchestration and refund live in the backend, not in the browser.
- **A2.** The feature ships behind a feature flag that is off by default in production. Off must equal today's checkout.
- **A3.** The customer can either type the first-card amount or choose an even split. The remainder-cent rule applies to even splits of odd totals; a typed amount is used as typed.
- **A4.** Valid first-card amounts are 1 cent to total minus 1 cent inclusive; each card must carry at least 1 cent. Zero and the full total are rejected (otherwise it is a single-card order).
- **A5.** The first charge is captured, not merely authorized, so "refund" is a PayGate refund call. If it is a void of an authorization instead, the same cases apply with the refund call renamed.
- **A6.** Outside sandbox days, the developers provide a PayGate stub whose responses are recorded from the sandbox on 2026-10-27. No such stub exists today (project risk R13).
- **A7.** The PayGate sandbox offers test cards for approve, decline and timeout, and accepts refunds. It cannot force a refund to fail; that path is tested against the stub only.
- **A8.** A single currency with two decimal places; all amounts are integer cents end to end.
- **A9.** A company test card can place one real low-value order in production for the post-release sanity check, with Finance's agreement.
- **A10.** Card data is tokenized by PayGate; the application never holds a card number, so PCI scope is unchanged.

Constraints:

- PayGate sandbox available only on Tuesdays and Thursdays: four windows, the last one the day before release.
- One tester at half time: 10 days × 4 h = 40 person-hours for all system-level testing, analysis and reporting.
- Two developers build the feature and own component and component integration testing.
- Fixed release date 2026-11-06; no slack after the last sandbox window.
- Single-card checkout must keep working; it is the revenue path.

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Who | Responsibility | Relevance to testing |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Product Owner | N/A — name not given; assumed one PO exists | Accepts the decision table on day 1, signs off exceptions, decides go/no-go | Owns the acceptance test on 2026-11-05 and every P1 exception |
| Developer A | N/A — name not given | Backend orchestration, refund, idempotency, unit and integration tests | Builds the PayGate stub; author of the code under test |
| Developer B | N/A — name not given | Checkout UI, amount validation, flag wiring, unit tests | Reviews Developer A's tests (some independence) and vice versa |
| Tester | N/A — name not given | Test plan, cases, sandbox sessions, regression, exploratory, reports | Holds both the test management role and the testing role |
| PayGate support contact | N/A — not named; assumed reachable by email | Sandbox credentials, test card list, decline codes | Needed before 2026-10-27; a missing contact blocks the first window |
| Operations / on-call | N/A — not named | Receives refund-failure alerts in production | Confirms the alert for R01 reaches a person |
| Finance | N/A — not named | Reconciliation of charges and refunds | Reads the daily reconciliation report; agrees to A9 |

## 4. Communication

| Progress report | After each sandbox window (Tue, Thu) and on Friday 2026-10-30 | Period, gate cases run / passed, refund timings measured, defects by severity, risks re-scored, next window's plan | Progress report format of the package's test reporting reference, posted on the ticket |
| Defect reports | As found | DR-SPLIT-NNN with build, environment, flag state and PayGate mode (sandbox or stub) | `/qa-defect` format |
| Completion report | 2026-11-05 evening, finalized 2026-11-06 morning | Every case one per row, "Not run — resume point", unmitigated risks, go/no-go evidence | Completion report format of the package's test reporting reference |
| Retrospective | Week of 2026-11-09 | Three questions of CTFL §2.1.6, actions with owner and date | Whole team, 45 minutes |

Test cases follow the package's TC-CODE-NNN format (`/qa-cases`), codes TC-SPLIT-NNN for the feature and TC-CHK-NNN for single-card regression.

## 5. Risk register

| 13 | R13 | No PayGate stub exists, so nothing can be tested on Mon, Wed and Fri until one does | Project | 3 | 3 | 9 | 🟠 HIGH | Dev A builds the stub from the 2026-10-27 recordings by 2026-10-28; the stub's responses are versioned (item 9) | Dev A |
| 14 | R14 | Feature not ready for QA before the third window (2026-11-03), leaving one window for everything | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Vertical slice (both charges, no UI polish) delivered by 2026-10-29; entry criteria checked daily; if missed, PO decides on 2026-11-02 whether to move the release | Dev A / PO |

Monitoring: the register is re-read at every progress report; a row is re-scored in place with a dated note when its facts change (never deleted).

## 6. Test approach

### 6.1 Test levels, who tests and independence

| Level | Test object | Who tests | Degree | Why it fits the risk |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Component | Split function, validation, payment state machine, idempotency key logic | Developer who wrote it, tests reviewed by the other developer in the PR | Some | Arithmetic and state logic are cheapest to cover here; the peer review is the independence; the tester reads the branch coverage report of the split and state modules (floor 100% branches, below it the uncovered branch is read before the PR merges) |
| Component integration | Orchestration against the PayGate stub, persistence between charges, refund retry | Developer A, reviewed by Developer B; tester reviews the decision table coverage of the integration tests | Some | The stub's recorded responses come from the tester's sandbox session, which gives the tests an oracle independent of the author's belief |
| System and system integration | Checkout on Staging with the real PayGate sandbox on Tue/Thu, the stub on other days | Tester | Some (same team as the authors; the highest degree available) | The risk level of R01 and R02 would justify High; it is not available with one tester, so the decision table and the gate results are also reviewed by the PO, who has no stake in the implementation |
| Acceptance | Gate run on 2026-11-05 observed by the PO; business rule check of the split and the refund message | Product Owner | Some (business representative) | Validation of the brief's intent, especially A3 and A4, which the tester assumed |

The tester holds both the test management role (this plan, monitoring, reports) and the testing role (cases, execution). Developers hold the testing role at their levels.

### 6.2 Test pyramid and quadrants

Preset: **Backend / API** (70% unit, 20% integration, 10% E2E). The business logic lives in the backend orchestration and arithmetic (A1); the checkout UI is a form. The existing single-card E2E suite is reused as is.

| Quadrant | What this plan puts there |
| :-- | :-- |
| Q1 | Unit tests on split arithmetic, validation and the state machine; integration tests against the stub, run in CI on every push |
| Q2 | TC-SPLIT cases from the decision table and BVA; an API test file for amount tampering; Gherkin scenarios for the four gate outcomes via `/qa-bdd` if time allows (cut list item) |
| Q3 | Two exploratory sessions (charters in 6.4); PO acceptance on 2026-11-05 |
| Q4 | Single-card `@smoke` suite; security checklist (6.4); latency measurement of the two-charge flow. No load test: no tool or environment in 10 days; recorded as a deviation in 6.9 |

### 6.3 Techniques by risk level

| Risk | Technique | Coverage items and target |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| R01, R05, R06, R09 (charge outcomes) | Decision table: conditions card 1 result {approved, declined, timeout} × card 2 result {approved, declined, timeout, not attempted}; actions place order, attempt charge 2, refund charge 1, query status, alert. Infeasible columns removed (card 2 attempted after card 1 declined) | Every feasible column exercised: 100% at integration level on the stub; the approved/declined columns also on the sandbox |
| R01, R06 (payment lifecycle) | State transition: Initiated → Card1Charged → Card2Charged → Completed; Card1Charged → Card2Declined → RefundPending → Refunded; RefundPending → RefundFailed → RefundRetry; Card1Declined → Failed | All transitions at unit level (money path treated as mission-critical, invalid transitions attempted one per case); valid transitions at system level |
| R04, R08 (amounts) | EP and 3-value BVA on the first-card amount: 0, 1, 2, total−2, total−1, total, total+1; odd totals 1, 3, 10,001; even total 10,000; invalid partitions non-numeric, negative, three decimals, separators | Every partition and every boundary item exercised; Each Choice for the amount × entry mode (typed, even split) |
| R02, R06, R10 | Error guessing: double submit, back button after charge 1, reload on the processing page, same card used twice, session expiry between charges, network drop after charge 2 request sent | Each item has one case or one exploratory note |
| R07 | Checklist (security): second amount recomputed server-side; total taken from the order, not the request; no PAN, CVV or token in application logs; idempotency key not guessable; rate limit on checkout unchanged | Every item answered yes or a defect filed |
| R03 | Regression: existing single-card suite plus one manual order with the flag off and one with the flag on; impact analysis limits manual scope to checkout, order confirmation and the payment record | Suite green on the release candidate build |
| R10, R11 | Exploratory sessions, 90 minutes each | Charter report with notes, defects, and coverage of the charter |

### 6.4 Exploratory charters

1. **Session 1 (2026-10-30, stub):** "Explore the split entry form and the confirmation page with odd totals, even split, and every invalid amount, to discover display and message defects." Targets R08, R10, R11.
2. **Session 2 (2026-11-04, stub):** "Explore interruptions between charge 1 and charge 2 (reload, back, close tab, expire session, slow network) to discover half-paid or double-charged states." Targets R02, R06.

### 6.5 Entry and exit criteria per level

| Level | Entry | Exit |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Component | Decision table and state model agreed on 2026-10-26 | 100% branch coverage of split and state modules; all unit tests green in CI |
| Component integration | Stub available with versioned recordings (by 2026-10-28) | Every feasible decision table column has a green integration test |
| System and system integration | Build passed CI; deployed to Staging with a recorded SHA; flag state known; fixture set (6.7) present; sandbox credentials valid on the day; a `data-testid` on amount field, even-split control, submit button and outcome message | All gate cases pass on one sandbox-verified build; 100% P0 and P1 cases pass or each P1 failure has a PO exception; zero open Critical or High defects; measured refund time under 60 s on every decline run; single-card suite green on the same build |
| Acceptance | Gate passed on Staging | PO signs the completion report |

Running out of time ends testing only when the PO has reviewed the "Not run — resume point" section and accepted the residual risk in writing.

### 6.6 Release gate

Eight cases. A failure here blocks the release; findings outside this table inform and are filed as DR-SPLIT-NNN tickets.

| ID | What it proves | Risks | Where it runs | Result |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| G01 / TC-SPLIT-001 | Typed amount, both cards approved: two PayGate charges whose cents sum to the total, order placed, confirmation shows both charges | R04, R11 | Staging + sandbox | N/A — not yet run |
| G02 / TC-SPLIT-002 | Even split of an odd total (10,001 cents): first card 5,001, second card 5,000 | R04 | Staging + sandbox | N/A — not yet run |
| G03 / TC-SPLIT-003 | Second card declined: first charge refunded automatically, elapsed time under 60 s measured from the decline response, no order placed, customer told | R01 | Staging + sandbox | N/A — not yet run |
| G04 / TC-SPLIT-004 | First card declined: second card never charged, no refund issued, no order record | R09 | Staging + sandbox | N/A — not yet run |
| G05 / TC-SPLIT-005 | Amount boundaries: 1 and total−1 accepted; 0, total and total+1 rejected at API and UI | R08 | Staging + stub (validation is pre-gateway) | N/A — not yet run |
| G06 / TC-SPLIT-006 | Resubmitting the same checkout (double submit, reload) creates no additional charge on either card | R02 | Staging + sandbox | N/A — not yet run |
| G07 / TC-CHK-001 | Single-card checkout unchanged: automated suite green on the release build, plus one manual order with flag off and one with flag on | R03 | Staging, CI | N/A — not yet run |
| G08 / TC-SPLIT-007 | Refund call fails: retry succeeds or an alert reaches on-call and the reconciliation entry is written | R01, R15 | Staging + stub only (A7) | N/A — not yet run |

**Execution order** (risk-based, with the resource window and dependencies overriding):

1. G07 automated part runs in CI on every push from day 1, before anything else, because the single-card suite is already automated and R03 needs no sandbox.
2. G05 on the stub on 2026-10-30, because validation needs no gateway and must pass before sandbox time is spent on invalid input.
3. G08 on the stub on 2026-10-30, because the sandbox cannot force a refund failure (A7).
4. G03 first in every sandbox window (2026-10-29, 2026-11-03, 2026-11-05), because R01 is the highest product risk and the refund timer needs the real gateway.
5. G06 second in the sandbox, because R02 is CRITICAL and idempotency against the real gateway is the only proof.
6. G01 third in the sandbox; G02 right after it, since G02 reuses G01's customer and cart fixture (dependency).
7. G04 last in the sandbox, lowest score of the sandbox cases.
8. G07 manual part on 2026-11-02 and again on the release candidate on 2026-11-05, after the flag-on gate cases, because it must run on the same build the gate passed on.

Control directive recorded in advance: any code change merged after the 2026-11-05 window means the flag stays off in production until the gate is re-run in the next sandbox window (2026-11-10), unless the PO records an exception. The code can still deploy on 2026-11-06 with the flag off.

### 6.7 Test data and environment

Fixture set (one document, kept with the cases):

| Record | State assumed | May tests write to it | Rebuild |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| PayGate sandbox test cards: approve, decline (insufficient funds), decline (do not honour), timeout | As PayGate documents them; credentials in the team vault, never in the cases | Read only | From PayGate documentation |
| Customer SPLIT-CUST-01 on Staging with an address and an empty cart | Empty cart before each case; a case empties it after | Write (cart only) | Script `seed-split-customer` (to be written by Dev B, assumption) |
| Products P-ODD (10,001 cents) and P-EVEN (10,000 cents) | Published, in stock | Read only | Same seed script |
| Feature flag `split_payment` | Off on Staging except during a split run; the run records the state it set and restores it | Write, logged | Flag admin screen |
| Stub recordings v1 (2026-10-27) | Versioned with the code | Read only | Re-record in a sandbox window |

Environments: Dev (stub only), Staging (sandbox on Tue/Thu, stub on other days; PayGate mode is recorded in every result), Production (flag off at deploy, canary afterwards). CI runs unit and integration tests on every push; the single-card E2E suite on every push to main. Sandbox-dependent E2E cases cannot run in CI on every push; they run as a scripted run by the tester in the windows, and are not reported as automated.

### 6.8 Metrics

| Metric | Decision it answers |
| :-- | :-- |
| Gate cases run / passed, per build and PayGate mode | Is the build releasable on 2026-11-06 |
| Refund elapsed time on every decline run (max must be under 60 s) | Does R01 hold against the real gateway |
| Open defects by severity, and retests pending | Can the exit criteria be met before the last window |
| Risk coverage: register rows with at least one executed case | Which risks are still untested before each window |
| Sandbox windows used as planned / lost | Trigger for the PO decision in R14 |
| Tester hours spent against the estimate in item 7 | When to apply the cut list |

### 6.9 Deviations from the test policy and strategy

- No load or performance test beyond a latency measurement (no tool, no environment, 10 days).
- Sandbox cases run manually outside CI, on fixed days, instead of in the nightly job.
- One gate case (G08) is proven on a stub only; residual risk recorded in the completion report and covered by the production refund alert and reconciliation report.
- Independence at system level is "some", not "high"; compensated by PO review of the decision table and the gate results.

**Deliverables:** this plan; decision table and state model; TC-SPLIT and TC-CHK cases; fixture set; exploratory session reports; DR-SPLIT defect reports; progress reports after each window; completion report; retrospective actions.

## 7. Estimate

Technique: **three-point estimation** (one estimator, margin of error must be shown; no history for a split-payment feature in this organization is assumed). Tester effort only; developers' testing is part of their build effort, assumed at roughly a 3:2 development-to-test ratio inside their own days.

| Task | a (h) | m (h) | b (h) |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Analysis and design: decision table, state model, BVA sets, cases, fixture set | 6 | 8 | 12 |
| Stub-based dry runs on Staging (Mon, Wed, Fri) | 4 | 6 | 9 |
| Three sandbox sessions incl. preparation and refund timing | 10 | 12 | 15 |
| Single-card regression (suite trigger, manual flag-off and flag-on orders, twice) | 3 | 4 | 6 |
| Two exploratory sessions with session reports | 3 | 4 | 6 |
| Defect reports, retests, progress and completion reports | 3 | 5 | 8 |
| **Total** | **29** | **39** | **56** |

E = (29 + 4×39 + 56) / 6 = 40.2 h; SD = (56 − 29) / 6 = 4.5 h. Reported as **40 ± 4.5 person-hours (between 36 and 45)** against 40 available.

Assumptions behind the figure: the vertical slice is testable by 2026-10-29 (R14); the stub exists by 2026-10-28 (R13); the sandbox credentials arrive before 2026-10-27; no more than two High defects need a sandbox retest. The pessimistic case exceeds capacity by 5 hours; the agreed cut list, in order, is: Gherkin scenarios, exploratory session 2 (its charter moves to a developer), then the API tampering test is run by Developer B with the tester reviewing the evidence. The PO records which cuts were taken.

## 8. Budget and schedule

Budget: 40 tester hours; developer test effort within the feature's build; no tool purchase; no sandbox cost assumed. Any PayGate sandbox fee is N/A — not stated in the brief.

| Day | Date | Sandbox | Tester (≈4 h) | Developers |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |

# Test Plan: Split Payment (Release 5.3)

**Version** 1.0 | **Date** 2026-10-25 | **Author** QA (test management and testing roles) | **Status** Draft for review | **Tracker** N/A — no board URL given; assumed Jira, epic key `PAY-53` used below as a placeholder

## 1. Context of testing

**Scope, in**

| Area | What is tested | Levels | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Split amount calculation | Customer-chosen first-card amount, remainder on second card, cent arithmetic, remainder-cent rule | Unit, integration, system | P0 |
| Two-charge orchestration with PayGate | Both charges succeed; order moves to paid only when both have succeeded | Integration, system integration | P0 |
| Compensating refund | Second charge declined, first charge refunded automatically within 60 s; refund failure handling | Integration, system integration | P0 |
| Input validation and boundaries | First-card amount at 0, 1, total − 1, total, above total, negative, non-numeric, decimal input | Unit, system | P1 |
| Idempotency | Double submit, retry after timeout, back button, produces no duplicate charges | Integration, system integration | P1 |
| Single-card checkout regression | Existing flow unchanged with the feature on and off | System, smoke in production | P0 |
| Feature flag | Split option hidden when off; no behaviour change for single card | System | P1 |
| Order record and reconciliation | Order stores two transactions; existing exports and admin views still read it | Integration, exploratory | P2 |

**Scope, out** (with reason)

- Post-purchase refunds or cancellations of an order paid with two cards through the existing customer-service flow. Not in the brief; logged as risk R08 and raised to the Product Owner as an open question. Assumed to stay single-card-only in 5.3.
- Three or more cards, gift cards, or mixing card with another payment method. Not in the brief.
- Load and stress testing. Volume is about 4,000 orders a day, under one order per 20 s on average; the split path adds one gateway call per order. Latency is measured, load is not generated (see item 6, Q4).
- PCI-scope audit. Assumed that card data is tokenized client-side by PayGate's SDK and never reaches the application servers; one checklist item confirms the assumption (R09).
- Accessibility audit of the new form. Only a keyboard and screen-reader smoke check is done in the exploratory session; a full WCAG audit is deferred to 5.4.

**Objectives**

1. Show that every split produces two charges whose sum equals the order total, in cents, with the remainder cent on the first card.
2. Show that a declined second charge leaves the customer with no net charge within 60 s, and that a failed refund is never silent.
3. Show that single-card checkout is unaffected, before release and during the first hours in production.
4. Give the Product Owner a go/no-go record by Thursday 2026-11-05 with residual risks listed.

**Test basis**

- Feature brief "Split payment (release 5.3)" (this document's source; no ticket version given).
- PayGate API documentation for charge, refund and decline codes. Assumption: the version the current single-card integration uses; its version string is recorded in item 9.
- Existing single-card checkout acceptance tests and regression suite. Assumption: an automated regression suite exists and runs in CI.
- Open questions sent to the Product Owner on 2026-10-26 (listed in item 2). Answers become part of the test basis when received.

## 2. Assumptions and constraints

**Constraints (given)**

- PayGate sandbox is reachable only on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Within the 10 working days that gives four windows: Tue 2026-10-27, Thu 2026-10-29, Tue 2026-11-03, Thu 2026-11-05.
- Release date Friday 2026-11-06 (10 working days from today, 2026-10-25).
- One tester at half time, about 40 person-hours over the period, plus two developers building the feature.
- Single-card checkout handles about 4,000 orders a day and must keep working.

**Assumptions (made where the brief is silent; each is marked and will be corrected in place if wrong)**

| # | Assumption | Why it matters |
| :-- | :--- | :--- |
| A1 | Web checkout with a browser front end and a backend service; the split, orchestration and refund logic live in the backend. | Chooses the backend-heavy pyramid preset. |
| A2 | The customer enters the first-card amount as a decimal value in the UI; the backend converts to cents. The remainder-cent rule applies when the UI offers an equal-split shortcut or a percentage, and when a decimal input converts to a fractional cent. | Defines the inputs that can produce an uneven split. If no shortcut exists, the rule is still tested at the unit level on the conversion. |
| A3 | Valid first-card amount is 1 cent to total − 1 cent inclusive; 0 and total are rejected as "use single card". PayGate's minimum charge is not known; assumed 1 cent, to be confirmed on the first sandbox day. | Sets the boundaries for BVA. If PayGate has a higher minimum, the boundaries move and R06 is re-scored. |
| A4 | The 60 s limit is measured from the decline response of the second charge to PayGate acknowledging the refund request, not to settlement. | Makes the requirement measurable. |
| A5 | If the refund request fails, the system retries with backoff, alerts operations, and keeps the order in a "payment failed, refund pending" state visible to support. | The brief does not say; without this the customer can be charged with no order. Logged as R05. |
| A6 | The same card may be used for both halves; no rule forbids it. | Tested once; not a release blocker either way. |
| A7 | Charges are made sequentially: first card, then second. The first charge is a capture, not an authorization hold. | Determines whether a refund or a void is needed. If the team uses auth-then-capture, the compensation becomes a void and R02 cases are rewritten, not removed. |
| A8 | A feature flag exists or will be added so that split payment can be switched off in production without a deploy. | Main non-test mitigation for R03 and R18. |
| A9 | PayGate sandbox provides test card numbers that approve, decline, and time out, and a refund endpoint that behaves as in production. Verified on the first sandbox day. | Needed to run G02 against the real gateway. |
| A10 | A PayGate stub (recorded responses, scenario-selectable) can be built by the developers by Wednesday 2026-10-28, so that all non-sandbox days have a deterministic gateway. | The plan does not work without it; see R14. |
| A11 | The tester sits in the same product team as the developers. | Sets the independence degree in item 6. |
| A12 | Dev, staging and production environments exist; staging can reach the PayGate sandbox; dev uses the stub. | Environment plan in item 6. |

**Open questions sent to the Product Owner** (plan proceeds under the assumption named)

1. Is the first-card amount free-form, a shortcut, or both? (A2)
2. Does PayGate enforce a minimum charge? (A3)
3. What should the customer and support see when the refund itself fails? (A5)
4. How is an order paid with two cards refunded later by customer service? (R08, out of scope)

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Who | Responsibility | Relevance to testing |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Product Owner | N/A — name not given | Owns acceptance, answers open questions, signs the go/no-go, records any exception | Decides on residual risk; does a short UAT on 2026-11-05 |
| Developers (2) | N/A — names not given | Build the feature, write unit and integration tests, build and maintain the PayGate stub, fix defects | Hold the testing role at component and component integration level |
| Tester (half time) | N/A — name not given | Test management role (this plan, monitoring, reports) and testing role at system and system integration level | Single point of failure; see R13 |
| Payments or finance operations | N/A — assumed to exist | Reconciles PayGate settlements with orders | Reviews how two transactions per order appear in exports (R11); consulted in the exploratory session |
| Customer support | N/A — assumed to exist | Handles customers whose second card was declined | Reviews the customer-facing message and the "refund pending" state (A5) |
| PayGate technical contact | N/A — assumed to exist | Sandbox access, decline test cards, API questions | Needed on 2026-10-27 if A9 fails |

## 4. Communication

| Form | Frequency | Content | Template |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Stand-up note in the team channel | Daily, working days | Cases run, blocked, defects opened, what runs tomorrow | Free text, three lines |
| Progress report | Evening of each sandbox day (10-27, 10-29, 11-03, 11-05) | Period, progress against plan, impediments, metrics from item 6, new and changed risks, next period | Progress report format of the `qa-reference` skill's test-reporting reference |
| Defect reports | As found | DR-SPLIT-NNN with severity, steps, expected and actual, environment and build, evidence | `/qa-defect` format |
| Go/no-go record | Once, 2026-11-05 | Each gate case with result and build; exceptions; residual risks; defects not fixed | `/qa-release` format |
| Completion report | Once, 2026-11-06 after release | Every case one per row, "Not run — resume point", lessons learned | Completion report format of the test-reporting reference |
| Retrospective | Once, week of 2026-11-09 | What to keep, what to change, actions with owner and date | Whole-team meeting |
| Risk register review | At each progress report | Re-scored rows with a dated note | In this plan, item 5 |

## 5. Risk register

Score = Likelihood (1 to 5) × Impact (1 to 5). Levels: 15 to 25 CRITICAL, 8 to 14 HIGH, 4 to 7 MEDIUM, 1 to 3 LOW.

| # | ID | Risk Description | Category | L | I | Score | Level | Mitigation Strategy | Owner |
| :-- | :-- | :--- | :--- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | R01 | Split amounts do not sum to the order total, or the remainder cent lands on the second card, or decimal-to-cent conversion rounds wrongly | Product | 3 | 5 | 15 | 🔴 CRITICAL | Pure function for the split; unit tests with BVA and EP on cents; property-style check that first + second = total for a range of totals; integration test asserts the two amounts sent to PayGate; gate case G01 on sandbox | Dev / QA |
| 2 | R02 | Second charge declined and the first charge is not refunded, or is refunded after 60 s | Product | 3 | 5 | 15 | 🔴 CRITICAL | State transition tests on the payment state machine (all transitions); stub scenarios for decline, timeout and 5xx on the second charge; refund latency measured and logged on every run; gate case G02 on sandbox; production alert on refund latency above 45 s | Dev / QA |

One exploratory check of what the existing refund screen does with a two-transaction order, so the PO decides with evidence | PO |

| 15 | R15 | Feature not "Ready for QA" before the third sandbox window (2026-11-03) | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Entry criterion for system test set at end of 2026-10-30; if missed, the PO is told on 2026-11-02 and the release decision moves to flag-off ship or slip | Devs / PO |

**Risk control.** Rows R01, R02 and R12 drive the order of execution and the gate. R08 is a decision for the PO, not a test. R03 and R18 are reduced by non-test measures (flag, canary, alerting) as much as by tests. Each row is re-scored in the progress report when its facts change, with a dated note in place.

## 6. Test approach

**Pyramid preset.** Backend / API: about 70% unit, 20% integration, 10% end-to-end. The business logic (split arithmetic, state machine, compensation) lives in the backend (A1). The UI adds one form and one message, covered by a few component tests and the end-to-end gate cases.

**Test levels, who tests, independence**

| Level | Test object | Who | Independence | Why this degree fits |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Component | Split function, validation, state machine, refund scheduler | Developers, with the other developer reviewing the tests | Some (peer from the author's team) | Fast feedback on arithmetic; the peer review catches the author's assumptions about rounding and boundaries |
| Component integration | Checkout service with PayGate client against the stub; order repository | Developers; tester reviews scenario list | Some | The stub scenarios are the main defect-finding tool for R02, R04, R05 and R07; the tester's review adds the failure modes a developer tends to skip |
| System | Full checkout through the UI and API against the stub (dev) | Tester | Some (same team, A11) | A tester from outside the team is not available; the tester did not write the code and challenges the brief's gaps, which is what matters for R01 and R06 |
| System integration | Staging against the PayGate sandbox, Tuesdays and Thursdays | Tester, paired with a developer on sandbox days | Some | The pairing is for speed in a four-hour window, not for independence; the tester records every result |
| Acceptance | Gate cases G01 to G03 walked through by the PO on 2026-11-05 | Product Owner | Some (business representative within the organisation) | Confirms the behaviour matches business intent, in particular the remainder-cent rule and the customer message |

**Test types.** Functional (all levels); non-functional: performance measurement of checkout duration and refund latency (no load), security checklist for card data (R09), a keyboard and screen-reader smoke check of the new form. Black-box techniques dominate at system level; branch coverage is read at component level for the split and state-machine code (floor 80%, a trigger to look, not a target).

**Techniques by risk level**

| Risk | Technique | Coverage items |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R01 CRITICAL | EP and 3-value BVA on cents; decision table for shortcut versus free-form input versus decimal conversion; property check first + second = total over totals 1 to 100,000 cents | Every partition and boundary; every feasible decision-table column |
| R02 CRITICAL | State transition testing, all-transitions criterion, on the payment state machine: states pending, leg1_charged, paid, leg2_declined, refund_requested, refunded, refund_failed; one invalid transition per case | Every valid transition exercised and every invalid one attempted |
| R04, R05, R07 HIGH | Error guessing with stub scenarios: duplicate request, timeout then success, 500 on refund, process killed between legs | One scenario per guessed fault |
| R06 HIGH | EP and 3-value BVA on first-card amount: 0, 1, 2, total − 2, total − 1, total, total + 1, negative, non-numeric, three decimals | Every boundary and its neighbours |
| R03 HIGH | Existing regression suite plus two gate cases; impact analysis of files touched by the change to pick which regression cases run manually | Changed modules and their callers |
| R08, R11, R16 | Exploratory session, 90 minutes, charter "split-paid order through admin, refund screen, export, and support message" | Session notes and defects |
| R09 MEDIUM | Checklist-based testing, five items (no PAN, CVV or expiry in logs, DB, analytics, URL, error messages) | Every item checked once |
| R10 MEDIUM | Measurement: checkout duration per leg, 10 runs on stub, 5 on sandbox; compared with single-card baseline | One measurement table |

**Testing quadrants check.** Q1: unit and component integration tests in CI. Q2: Gherkin scenarios for the split rules and decline-refund path written before coding, API tests of the checkout endpoint. Q3: exploratory session with finance operations and support, PO acceptance walkthrough. Q4: smoke suite, latency measurement, security checklist. Nothing is empty; load testing is the one Q4 activity left out, for the volume reason in item 1.

**Deliverables.** This plan; Gherkin scenarios (`/qa-bdd`) for R01, R02, R06; test cases TC-SPLIT-001 onward (`/qa-cases`) with the gate cases marked; PayGate stub scenario list with its version; exploratory session charter and notes; defect reports; progress reports on sandbox days; go/no-go record; completion report.

**Entry criteria**

| Level | Entry criteria |
| :--- | :--- |
| Component and component integration | Gherkin scenarios reviewed by PO; stub scenario list agreed; CI runs the suites on every push |
| System (dev, stub) | Feature behind flag, flag on in dev; build identifier known; stub version pinned; fixture set F1 to F6 seeded; `data-testid` on the amount field, card forms, submit and message; "Ready for QA" set in the tracker by end of 2026-10-30 |
| System integration (staging, sandbox) | System-level gate cases G04 to G06 and G08 passing on the stub; staging deployed with the same build; sandbox credentials in the secret store; decline test cards confirmed on 2026-10-27 |
| Acceptance | Gate cases G01 to G03 passed on sandbox at least once |

**Exit criteria (measured against the release gate)**

- Every gate case passing on the build proposed for release, on staging against the sandbox for G01, G02, G03, G07, and on the stub for G04, G05, G06, G08.
- 100% of P0 cases passed; 100% of P1 cases passed or each failure carries a recorded PO exception.
- Zero open Critical defects; zero open High defects without a recorded PO exception.
- Single-card regression suite green on the release build; smoke suite green on the supported browsers (assumed: current Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge).
- Refund latency in G02 under 60 s on every measured run, and under 45 s on the sandbox run so production has margin.
- Go/no-go record signed by the PO and the tester.
- Time running out ends testing only when the PO reviews the untested items and accepts the risk in the go/no-go record.

**Release gate**

| ID | Case | What it proves | Level / environment | Window | Result |
| :-- | :-- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| G01 | TC-SPLIT-001 | Uneven total (e.g. 100.01 split equally) charges 50.01 on card 1 and 50.00 on card 2, both succeed, order paid, stored amounts sum to total | System integration, staging + sandbox | Tue 11-03, confirm Thu 11-05 | N/A — not yet run |
| G02 | TC-SPLIT-002 | Card 2 declined: card 1 refund acknowledged by PayGate within 60 s, order not paid, customer sees the decline-and-refund message | System integration, staging + sandbox | Tue 11-03, confirm Thu 11-05 | N/A — not yet run |
| G03 | TC-CHK-SMOKE-001 (existing) | Single-card checkout succeeds unchanged with the flag on | System integration, staging + sandbox | Tue 11-03, confirm Thu 11-05 | N/A — not yet run |
| G04 | TC-SPLIT-010 | Refund returns 500 then 200: retry succeeds, alert fired, order in "refund pending" then "refunded" | System, dev + stub | From Mon 11-02 | N/A — not yet run |
| G05 | TC-SPLIT-015 | Submitting the same split order twice produces exactly two charges, never four | System, dev + stub | From Mon 11-02 | N/A — not yet run |
| G06 | TC-SPLIT-020 | Amount boundaries: 1 cent and total − 1 cent accepted; 0 and total rejected with a message naming the field | System, dev + stub (API and UI) | From Mon 11-02 | N/A — not yet run |
| G07 | TC-CHK-SMOKE-004 (existing) | Single-card decline still shows the existing decline message and leaves no charge | System integration, staging + sandbox | Tue 11-03, confirm Thu 11-05 | N/A — not yet run |
| G08 | TC-SPLIT-030 | Flag off: split option absent, single-card checkout identical to 5.2 | System, dev + stub | From Mon 11-02 | N/A — not yet run |

Existing case IDs TC-CHK-SMOKE-001 and -004 are assumed; the real IDs replace them once the regression suite is checked.

**Execution order (risk-based, with resource windows and dependencies applied)**

1. G06 on the stub, Mon 11-02. First because G01 depends on a valid amount being accepted, and it needs no sandbox.
2. G08 on the stub, Mon 11-02. Confirms the flag before anything else is trusted.
3. G05 on the stub, Mon 11-02. Idempotency must hold before the sandbox run, or sandbox charges multiply.
4. G04 on the stub, Mon 11-02. Refund failure path; cannot be forced on the sandbox, so it runs here.
5. G01 on staging + sandbox, Tue 11-03, first thing in the window. Highest risk (R01).
6. G02 on staging + sandbox, Tue 11-03, immediately after G01. Highest risk (R02); refund latency recorded on five runs.
7. G03 and G07 on staging + sandbox, Tue 11-03. Moved after G01 and G02 only because the sandbox window is shared and the split cases are the ones that cannot run elsewhere.
8. Full analysis set and exploratory session, Mon 11-02 to Wed 11-04, on the stub.
9. Confirmation run of G01, G02, G03, G07 on the release build, Thu 11-05. The sandbox resource window fixes this date; any fix landing after Wed 11-04 cannot be confirmed before release.

Analysis cases (not in the gate): decision-table cases for input modes, remaining BVA points, all-transitions cases for the state machine, process-kill recovery, same-card-twice, latency measurement, security checklist, reconciliation export, admin refund screen, usability and keyboard check. A failure there informs; if a failure is traced to the change and would stop the release, its case moves into the gate with a dated note.

## 7. Estimate

**Technique:** three-point estimation (CTFL v4.0 §5.1.4), chosen because one estimator is available and the margin of error must be visible. Work decomposed into tasks; E = (a + 4m + b) / 6, SD = (b − a) / 6, in person-hours.

| Task | Who | a | m | b | E |
| :--- | :--- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Test analysis and design: Gherkin, decision table, BVA, state-transition cases, gate | Tester | 5 | 7 | 10 | 7.2 |
| Stub scenario list and review of stub fidelity | Tester | 2 | 3 | 5 | 3.2 |
| Sandbox execution, two windows, plus characterization on 10-27 | Tester | 6 | 8 | 12 | 8.3 |
| Single-card regression: suite run, impact-based manual cases | Tester | 2 | 3 | 5 | 3.2 |
| Exploratory session and security checklist | Tester | 2 | 4 | 6 | 4.0 |
| Progress reports, go/no-go record, completion report | Tester | 2 | 3 | 4 | 3.0 |
| **Tester total** | | **19** | **28** | **42** | **28.8** |
| Unit and component integration tests, including state machine and idempotency | Developers | 8 | 12 | 20 | 12.7 |
| Build and record the PayGate stub | Developers | 2 | 3 | 5 | 3.2 |
| **Developer test total** | | **10** | **15** | **25** | **15.8** |

**Result.** Tester effort 29 ± 4 h (between 25 and 33), against 40 h available. The remaining 7 to 11 h are the buffer for fix-and-retest cycles (R19). Developer test effort 16 ± 3 h (between 13 and 19), on top of building the feature.

**Assumptions behind the figures.** A10 holds (stub ready by 10-28); the regression suite is automated and green today; no more than two Critical or High defects need a second sandbox confirmation; the PO answers the open questions by 10-28. If any fails, the estimate is re-issued in the next progress report with a dated note, not overwritten.

## 9. Configuration management of testware

- **Identification and versioning.** This plan, the Gherkin files, test cases TC-SPLIT-NNN, the stub scenario set, exploratory notes and reports live in the repository under a folder for release 5.3 (assumed `docs/qa/5.3-split-payment/`), versioned with the code. Defect reports live in the tracker and link back by case ID.
- **References by identifier and version.** Every result names the git commit SHA, the staging deployment tag, the stub version (v1, bumped on any change) and, for sandbox runs, the date and PayGate API version header observed. "Latest build" is never a valid reference.
- **Baselines.** Staging on 11-04 after code freeze is the release baseline: build SHA, flag state, stub version, fixture seed version recorded in the go/no-go record. The sandbox is external and unversioned; its date stands in for a version, and the characterization notes from 10-27 record what it did.
- **Restorable baselines.** Any earlier build can be redeployed to dev by SHA, with the matching stub version, to reproduce a result.
- **In CI/CD.** Unit, component integration and the stub-based system suite run on every push; the run ID is the result's identifier. Sandbox runs are manual and recorded in the progress report of that day.
- **Handover-ready state.** The plan's gate table, the fixture set and the "Not run — resume point" section are updated at the end of each day, so a developer or the PO can continue the gate if the tester is unavailable (R13).

**Corrections.** Nothing in this plan is deleted once shared. Re-scored risks, revised estimates, assumptions proved wrong and gate changes are corrected in place as `Correction, YYYY-MM-DD, <author>: <what was wrong and what is right>` or with strike-through and the reason.
